definition_zh: 再植被；重新绿化；使重新长满植物
definition_en: to plant or restore vegetation on land where the plants have been lost
core_image: 采矿坑边先铺上草籽，几个月后整面坡重新变绿
scene: 矿坑关闭后，工人先在坡面上撒种，希望这片废地重新长出植被。After the mine closed, workers redressed the slopes with seed and fertiliser to revegetate the waste ground.
sceneCN: 这里 revegetate 是「使重新长满植物」（第 1 个义项：让失去植被的土地重新覆盖植物）；句意：矿山关闭后，工人在坡面撒种，让废地重新长草。

pos.zh: 再植被；重新绿化；使重新长满植物

collocations.zh: 用本地物种重新覆盖植被

derivatives.zh: 再植被；重新绿化
已重新长满植被的
植被；植物

senses.title: To cover bare land with plants again
senses.definition: to establish plant cover on land that has lost it
senses.definitionCN: 让失去植被的土地重新长出植物覆盖层
senses.example: Volunteers revegetated the burnt hillside with native shrubs.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者用本地灌木让烧过的山坡重新长满绿色。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again while the stem carries the Latin word for growing plants, so the verb restores plant life to a place.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再次」，词干则承继拉丁语中表示植物生长的一词，因此这个动词是把植物生命交还某地。

senses.title: To restore vegetation after human damage
senses.titleCN: 迹地植被恢复；修复性绿化
senses.definition: to repair land damaged by mining, building, or grazing by re-establishing plants
senses.definitionCN: 通过重新种植来修复因采矿、建设或放牧而受损的土地
senses.example: The company must revegetate the quarry before its permit expires.
senses.exampleCN: 公司必须在许可证到期前完成采石场的植被恢复。
senses.why: In resource industries the prefix points back to the cover that existed before the damage, so the verb becomes a legal duty.
senses.whyCN: 在资源行业中，这个前缀指回破坏之前原本存在的植被，于是这个动词成了一种法定义务。

senses.title: To let vegetation return on its own
senses.titleCN: （自然或人工辅助地）重新长出植被
senses.definition: to cause plants to recolonise an area, whether by planting or by assisted natural regeneration
senses.definitionCN: 使植物重新占据某片区域，无论靠人工栽植还是辅助自然更新
senses.example: Wetter seasons helped the reserve revegetate faster than predicted.
senses.exampleCN: 更湿润的季节让保护区比预期更快地重新变绿。
senses.why: Where seeds are already in the soil, the verb can describe nature doing the work with management simply letting it happen.
senses.whyCN: 当土壤中已有种子时，这个动词也可以描述自然在动手，而管理只是让它发生。

intro.en: Revegetate is a learned modern formation from the re- prefix and the Latin verb vegetare, to enliven or grow.
intro.cn: revegetate 是现代书面构词，由前缀 re- 与拉丁语动词 vegetare（使有生气、生长）合成。

items.en: Vegetus means lively, and vegetare means to enliven.
items.cn: vegetus 意为有生气的，vegetare 意为使有生气。

items.en: Vegetatio names the growing of plants.
items.cn: vegetatio 指植物的生长状态。

items.en: Vegetation enters English in the sense of plant growth.
items.cn: vegetation 以「植物生长」之义进入英语。

items.en: The verbs vegetate and vegetation appear in botany and land writing.
items.cn: 动词 vegetate 与 vegetation 出现在植物学与土地记述中。

items.en: Revegetate is coined as a practical compound for land repair.
items.cn: revegetate 作为土地修复的实用复合词被造出。

items.en: Ecologists prefer the longer noun revegetation in restoration reports.
items.cn: 在恢复生态学报告中，学者更常用较长的名词 revegetation。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same veget- root; group two holds the vocabulary of ecological restoration.
note.cn: 第一组是以同一词干 veget- 构成的词；第二组是生态修复领域的相关词。

entries.definition: Plants considered as a whole cover.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体覆盖层的植物。

entries.definition: To grow as a plant does; in medicine, to live without mental activity.
entries.definitionCN: 像植物一样生长；医学上指无意识地活着。

entries.definition: The act of replanting a forest; different stem.
entries.definitionCN: 重新植树造林的行为；词干不同。

entries.definition: To bring damaged land back into use; closely related in land policy.
entries.definitionCN: 使受损土地恢复可用；在土地政策中关系密切。

entries.definition: To plant something again in the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 把植物再次种入土中。

entries.definition: To bring an ecosystem back to a former condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使生态系统恢复到先前的状态。

entries.definition: To return damaged land to health.
entries.definitionCN: 使受损土地恢复健康。

normalIntro.en: Take re- as again and vegetate as to grow plants: land taken back by stems and leaves.
normalIntro.cn: 把 re- 理解为「再次」，把 vegetate 理解为植物生长：土地重新被茎叶占据。

normal.en: The stem veget- appears in vegetation and vegetarian.
normal.cn: 词干 veget- 也出现在 vegetation 与 vegetarian 中。

normal.en: Use re- when the plants were lost and must return.
normal.cn: 植物失去后要回来时，用 re- 表示「再次」。

normal.en: The noun revegetation is the standard term in restoration reports.
normal.cn: 名词 revegetation 是生态修复报告中的标准术语。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again, but the word implies a slow process.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再次」，但这个词暗示一个缓慢的过程。

normal.en: Mining and road laws often require revegetation after work ends.
normal.cn: 采矿与道路法规常要求工程结束后进行植被恢复。

abstract.en: Picture a black mining slope turning green after seed is spread.
abstract.cn: 想象黑色矿坡在撒种之后转绿。

abstract.en: Imagine a car park being restored so that grass creeps over the asphalt.
abstract.cn: 想象停车场被还原，青草慢慢爬上沥青。

abstract.en: Think of a desert track sealed by shrubs that close the wounds of the soil.
abstract.cn: 想想灌木封住沙地车辙，像给土地疗伤。

examples.en: Engineers revegetate the spoil heaps with a mix of grasses and shrubs.
examples.cn: 工程师用草与灌木的混合让废石堆重新长满植物。

examples.en: It may take a decade to revegetate land stripped by open-pit mining.
examples.cn: 让被露天矿剥蚀的土地重新长草可能要十年。

examples.en: Farmers revegetate eroding banks by planting willows along the river.
examples.cn: 农民沿河栽柳，让受侵蚀的河岸重新长满植被。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞维吉泰特」——维「吉」时把太荒的地再「泰」然绿化，就是 revegetate；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: re-（再次）＋ 拉丁语 vegetare（使有生气、生长，源于 vegetus「有生气的」）→ revegetate，核心义「让土地重新长出植物覆盖」。

sensesIntro.en: Revegetate moves from a general description of returning plant cover to the legal repair of industrial damage, and finally to assisted natural recovery.
sensesIntro.cn: revegetate 先从植物覆盖层回归的一般描述出发，进入对工业破坏的法定修复，最后指向人工辅助下的自然恢复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare slope that turns green again after seed is spread.
core.cn: 核心意象：撒种后重新变绿的裸露坡面。

branches.en: Putting plant cover back on bare ground is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 在裸地上恢复植物覆盖是字面义。

branches.en: Repair of industrial damage is the policy sense.
branches.cn: 对工业破坏的修复是政策义项。

branches.en: Assisted natural recovery extends the verb to passive regrowth.
branches.cn: 辅助自然恢复把动词扩展到被动再生长。

branches.en: Both describe plants returning to ground that once held them.
branches.cn: 两者都描述植物回到曾经拥有它们的土地。

branches.en: Reclamation projects often rely on both planting and natural regeneration.
branches.cn: 土地复垦项目常常同时依靠栽植与自然更新。

intro.en: Both halves of revegetate are Latin: the prefix re- and the stem veget- from vegetare.
intro.cn: revegetate 的两半都来自拉丁语：前缀 re- 与源自 vegetare 的词干 veget-。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegetus means lively, and vegetare means to grow or to keep alive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vegetus 意为有生气，vegetare 意为生长或使之有生命。

items.example: Re- marks the returning of plant cover.
items.exampleCN: re- 标示植物覆盖层的回归。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of life.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载生命之意。

items.example: The ending forms a verb.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾使词成为动词。

items.example: The suffix gives revegetation.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 revegetation。

items.example: Vegetation names the result of the process.
items.exampleCN: vegetation 指这一过程的结果。

items.example: Vegetate is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: vegetate 是基础动词。

items.example: The participle describes repaired land.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词描述已修复的土地。

items.example: The gerund follows prepositions.
items.exampleCN: 动名词跟在介词之后。

items.example: Erosion is what revegetation fights.
items.exampleCN: 植被恢复对抗的正是侵蚀。

definition_zh: 回响；余音；反响；连续的影响
definition_en: a sound echoing back, or the lasting effect of an event
core_image: 声音撞上教堂的石墙，一层层折返，久久不息
scene: 大提琴最后一个音在空荡的大厅里来回反弹，许久才散。The final chord of the cello hung in the empty hall, its reverberation fading only after many seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 reverberation 是「回响；余音」（第 1 个义项：声音在空间里反弹）；句意：大提琴最后一个和弦在空荡的大厅里挂住，余音数秒后才散去。

pos.zh: 回响；余音；反响；连续的影响

derivatives.zh: 回响；回荡；产生连锁反应
有回响的；回荡的
产生回响的（较少用）

senses.title: A sound bouncing back
senses.definition: a sound that is reflected repeatedly from surfaces so that it lingers
senses.definitionCN: 声音经表面反复反射，因而持续不散
senses.example: The reverberation of the bell crossed the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 钟声的回响传遍了山谷。
senses.why: The verb behind it means to strike back, and the noun names the echo that keeps returning after the first sound.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的动词意为「反弹」，这个名词于是指最初声音之后不断折返的声波。

senses.title: The lasting effects of an event
senses.definition: the continuing indirect effects of an event, spread over time or place
senses.definitionCN: 某一事件在时间或地域上不断扩散的后续影响
senses.example: The reverberations of the bank crash reached every small town.
senses.exampleCN: 银行倒闭的余波传到了每个小镇。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the acoustics: news, like sound, hits a wall and travels onward, so consequences are heard long after the moment.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻借用了声学：消息像声音一样撞墙而传开，所以后果在事件之后很久仍能被听见。

senses.title: Acoustic resonance in a space
senses.definition: the prolongation of sound in an enclosed space, measured in acoustics
senses.definitionCN: 封闭空间内声音延续的现象，声学中可测量
senses.example: Acousticians reduce the reverberation by adding felt to the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 声学专家在墙上加毛毡来降低混响。
senses.why: Modern acoustics treats reflection as a measurable property of a room, so one everyday echo becomes a technical quantity.
senses.whyCN: 现代声学把反射当作房间可测量的属性，于是日常的回声变成一项技术指标。

intro.en: Reverberation comes from Latin verberare, to beat or lash, doubled with re- so that the striking comes back.
intro.cn: reverberation 源于拉丁语 verberare（打、鞭打），加 re- 表示反打回来。

items.en: Verberare means to beat, and verber is a lash or stroke.
items.cn: verberare 意为打击，verber 意为鞭子或一击。

items.en: Reverberare means to beat back or reflect.
items.cn: reverberare 意为反打回去或反射。

items.en: Reverbération is used of light and sound thrown back.
items.cn: 古法语 reverbération 用于被反照回来的光与声。

items.en: Reverberation names mirrored light and echoed sound.
items.cn: 英语中的 reverberation 既指被反射的光，也指被折返的声音。

items.en: Science writing applies the noun to echo in enclosed spaces.
items.cn: 科学文献把这个名词用于封闭空间中的回声。

items.en: The figurative sense of spreading consequences becomes common in journalism.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，指后果扩散的比喻义在新闻报道里变得常见。

note.en: Group one holds the same verber- family and close spelling cousins; group two holds other acoustic words and near meanings of consequence.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 verber- 词族与拼写相近的词；第二组是其他声学词与表示后果的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb to echo and to spread as consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 回响并以后果形式扩散的动词。

entries.definition: Adjective: producing or full of echoes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：产生或充满回响的。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective meaning tending to reflect sound.
entries.definitionCN: 较少用的形容词，指易于反射声音。

entries.definition: The everyday language spoken in a region.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区的日常语言；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sound heard again after reflection.
entries.definitionCN: 反射后再次听见的声音。

entries.definition: Deep, full sound that goes on; also a chord of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 深沉持久的音响；也指引起情感共鸣。

entries.definition: Consequences of an event; smaller in scope.
entries.definitionCN: 事件造成的后果；范围较小。

normalIntro.en: Picture the Latin root verber, a lash: a sound beaten back from a wall, again and again.
normalIntro.cn: 想想拉丁词根 verber（鞭打）：声音被墙打回去，一次又一次。

normal.en: The verb is reverberate; the noun adds the -ation ending.
normal.cn: 动词是 reverberate，名词加上 -ation 词尾。

normal.en: Use it as a plural for events: the reverberations of the war.
normal.cn: 讲事件的影响常用复数：战争的余波。

normal.en: The prefix re- marks the return of the blow.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 标明这一击折返回来。

normal.en: Note the spelling: double r after the single e.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：单个 e 之后接双 r。

normal.en: Acousticians measure it as reverberation time.
normal.cn: 声学专家把混响量化为混响时间。

abstract.en: Imagine a shout in a stone church folding back on itself.
abstract.cn: 想象石砌教堂中的喊声折叠着返回自身。

abstract.en: Think of a wave in a bathtub sloshing back and forth.
abstract.cn: 想想浴缸里的水波来回晃荡。

abstract.en: Picture news of a closed plant travelling from family to family.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂关闭的消息逐家逐户传开。

examples.en: The reverberation of the cannon lasted several seconds.
examples.cn: 炮声的回响持续了好几秒。

examples.en: The reverberation of the verdict was felt across the whole industry.
examples.cn: 这一裁决的反响波及了整个行业。

examples.en: Thick curtains shorten the reverberation in small studios.
examples.cn: 厚窗帘能缩短小型录音棚里的混响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞维波」——「维」持着「波」来回反弹的声音，就是 reverberation；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（返回）＋ verberare（抽打，源于 verber 鞭子）→ reverberare（反打、反射）→ 古法语 reverbération → 英语 reverberation，核心义「被打回去的声音」。

sensesIntro.en: Reverberation starts as a returning sound, then grows into the idea of effects that keep coming back, and finally becomes a measured acoustic property.
sensesIntro.cn: reverberation 先指折返的声音，随后引申为不断折返的影响，最后成为可测量的声学属性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound struck back from a stone wall, staying in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：被石墙打回来、在空气中滞留的声音。

branches.en: Echo is the literal acoustic sense.
branches.cn: 回声是最基本的声学义。

branches.en: Hidden consequences are heard like echoes of an event.
branches.cn: 隐蔽的后果像事件的回声一样被人听见。

branches.en: Measurement turns the same reflection into engineering data.
branches.cn: 测量把同一种反射变成工程数据。

branches.en: Both are bound to the physics of a room.
branches.cn: 两者都离不开房间的物理属性。

branches.en: Both keep the idea of something returning to its listener long afterwards.
branches.cn: 两者都保留了事物很久之后仍回到听者耳边的意思。

intro.en: Reverberation is built from Latin pieces: re-, verberare, and the Latin noun suffix -io.
intro.cn: reverberation 由拉丁成分构成：re-、verberare 以及拉丁名词词尾 -io。

latinIntro.en: Latin verber means a lash, and verberare means to beat or strike; reverb means to beat it back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verber 意为鞭子，verberare 意为抽打、击打，re- 加在其前表示打回去。

items.example: Re- adds the returning path.
items.exampleCN: re- 加上折返的路径。

items.example: The stem supplies the striking image.
items.exampleCN: 词干提供击打的意象。

items.example: The ending forms the verb reverberate.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成动词 reverberate。

items.example: The ending forms the noun reverberation.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成名词 reverberation。

items.example: The ending forms reverberant.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 reverberant。

items.example: The verb is the engine of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词是名词义的来源。

items.example: The adjective modifies halls and voices.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词修饰大厅与声音。

items.example: The participle gives an ongoing picture.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词给出持续的画面。

items.example: Echo is the everyday neighbour.
items.exampleCN: echo 是日常的对等词。

definition_zh: 尊敬；崇敬；敬畏
definition_en: to respect and admire someone or something deeply, with a sense of awe and love
core_image: 一个人微微低头、双手交叠，站在雕像前久久不动
scene: 村口的旧石碑旁摆着一束束野花，经过的人都会放慢脚步、稍稍低头。Every morning the villagers stop by the old stone tablet to revere the names carved on it.
sceneCN: 这里 revere 是「崇敬、敬仰」（第 1 个义项：怀着敬畏与爱意深深敬重某人或某物）；句意：每天早晨，村民们都会在旧石碑前停下，敬仰上面刻着的名字。

pos.zh: 尊敬；崇敬；敬畏

derivatives.zh: 由 revere 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「崇敬；敬畏」
由 revere 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「恭敬的；虔敬的」
由 reverent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「恭敬地」
由拉丁语 reverendus 而来，义为「值得尊敬的」；作头衔时指牧师
由 reverence 加 -al 构成，义为「恭敬的；崇敬的」，语气比 reverent 更书面

senses.title: To respect and admire deeply
senses.definition: to feel and show deep respect and admiration for a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物怀有并表现出深深的敬意与钦佩
senses.example: Students still revere their old professor decades after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业几十年后，学生们仍然敬仰他们从前的教授。
senses.why: The Latin verb revereri means to stand in awe of and to hold in great respect, so the word keeps respect as its living centre.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 revereri 意为「怀着敬畏并高度敬重」，所以这个词的核心始终是敬意。

senses.title: To regard as sacred
senses.definition: to treat a place, object, or practice as sacred or holy
senses.definitionCN: 把某地、某物或某种做法视为神圣而加以敬奉
senses.example: Pilgrims revere the ancient shrine and leave offerings at its gate.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者敬奉这座古老的神殿，并在门前留下供品。
senses.why: The prefix re- adds a sense of awe to vereri, so the strongest form of respect becomes the holy regard shown to sacred things.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 给 vereri 添上敬畏的一层，于是最强烈的敬意就落在对神圣事物的崇奉上。

senses.title: To honour the memory of
senses.definition: to keep a dead person or a past event in honoured memory
senses.definitionCN: 把逝者或往事珍藏于敬重的记忆之中
senses.example: The town reveres the miners who worked below it for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇追念那些在地下一连劳作了一个世纪的矿工。
senses.why: When the person is gone, respect turns into held memory, so the word comes to mean honouring what has passed.
senses.whyCN: 当人已不在，敬意就转为留存的记忆，于是这个词也指追念已经过去的人和事。

senses.title: To value highly
senses.definition: to prize something such as an idea, a skill, or a custom very highly
senses.definitionCN: 对某种理念、技艺或习俗推崇备至
senses.example: The school reveres research and rewards careful scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校推崇研究，并奖励严谨的学术。
senses.why: The awe in the word softens into strong esteem, so any practice or idea may be honoured as if it were precious.
senses.whyCN: 词里的敬畏渐渐柔化为强烈的推崇，于是任何做法或理念都可以被珍视得像是稀世之物。

senses.title: To worship
senses.definition: to worship a deity or an object of devotion with solemn respect
senses.definitionCN: 以庄重的敬意崇拜神灵或所供奉之物
senses.example: The tribe revered the sun as the source of all life.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部落把太阳当作万物的源头来崇拜。
senses.why: Awe pushed to its limit becomes worship, the formal act of devotion given to a god.
senses.whyCN: 敬畏推到极致就成了崇拜，即献给神灵的正式敬奉之举。

intro.en: Revere comes from Latin revereri, to respect or stand in awe, built from re- and vereri, to feel awe.
intro.cn: revere 来自拉丁语 revereri（敬重、心怀敬畏），由 re- 与 vereri（畏惧、敬畏）构成。

items.en: The verb vereri means to fear with awe or to hold in respect.
items.cn: 动词 vereri 意为满怀敬畏地畏惧，或心怀敬重。

items.en: Revereri adds re- and means to stand in awe of something.
items.cn: revereri 加上 re-，意为对某物心存敬畏。

items.en: The adjective reverendus means to be respected, and reverentia is the noun of awe.
items.cn: 形容词 reverendus 意为「值得尊敬的」，名词 reverentia 意为敬畏。

items.en: The verb reverer carries the strong respect sense into French.
items.cn: 动词 reverer 把强烈的敬意带进法语。

items.en: Revere enters English with its meaning close to the Latin original.
items.cn: revere 在十六世纪进入英语，含义与拉丁语原义相近。

items.en: Revere becomes a slightly formal verb, while the noun reverence stays common.
items.cn: 现代英语中 revere 成为略偏正式的动词，而名词 reverence 依然常用。

note.en: Revere belongs to the vereri family of awe, and it stands beside respect words that differ mainly in strength and tone.
note.cn: revere 属于表示「敬畏」的 vereri 词族，它与各类「尊重」词相邻，区别主要在强度和语气上。

entries.definition: showing deep respect

entries.definition: a person who reveres
entries.definitionCN: 敬仰者

entries.definition: to admire someone for their qualities or achievements
entries.definitionCN: 因某人的品质或成就而尊重

entries.definition: to regard someone or something with warm approval
entries.definitionCN: 钦佩；赞赏

entries.definition: to treat a person or thing with the highest respect
entries.definitionCN: 尊崇；敬奉

normalIntro.en: Revere keeps the awe inside Latin vereri, so even its lightest use carries a quiet lowering of the head.
normalIntro.cn: revere 保留了拉丁语 vereri 里的那份敬畏，所以即便是最轻的用法，也带着不自觉的低头。

normal.en: The noun reverence and the adjective reverent share the same stem, so the family is easy to keep together.
normal.cn: 名词 reverence 与形容词 reverent 共用同一词干，整个词族可以一起记。

normal.en: To revere the memory of someone is a set phrase for honouring the dead.
normal.cn: revere the memory of someone 是追念逝者的固定说法。

normal.en: Reverend as a title means worthy of respect, and it comes from the same Latin source.
normal.cn: 头衔 Reverend 意为「值得尊敬的」，和 revere 同出一源。

normal.en: Revere is stronger and more formal than respect, but weaker than worship.
normal.cn: revere 比 respect 更强、更正式，但弱于 worship。

normal.en: Compare revere with reverse: reverse moves backwards, revere stands and bows, so the vowel order tells them apart.
normal.cn: 对比 revere 与 reverse：reverse 是往后倒，revere 是站定鞠躬，元音顺序帮我们区分两者。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor taking off a hat long before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 想象一位来访者，还没人开口，就先脱下了帽子。

abstract.en: Imagine a museum guard who handles one small bowl as if it were breathing.
abstract.cn: 想象一位博物馆看守，捧着一个小碗时轻得像怕它呼吸。

abstract.en: See a whole village standing still for a minute at the same grave.
abstract.cn: 看见整个村子在同一座墓前静立一分钟。

examples.en: The villagers revere the old healer for her patience and skill.
examples.cn: 村民们敬仰这位老医者，因为她有耐心又有医术。

examples.en: Throughout Asia, teachers are traditionally revered as second parents.
examples.cn: 在整个亚洲，老师传统上被尊奉为第二父母。

examples.en: Conservation workers treat the burial site with complete reverence.
examples.cn: 保护工作人员以十足的敬意对待这处墓葬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞维尔」——一尊铜像在广场上发着光，路过的人都放慢脚步行注目礼，那就是 revere；这只是谐音联想，真正的来源与拉丁语 vereri（敬畏）有关。

root: 拉丁语 vereri（畏惧、敬畏）→ 加前缀 re- 成 revereri（敬重、心怀敬畏）→ 拉丁名词 reverentia、形容词 reverendus → 古法语 reverer → 英语 revere，核心义「怀着敬畏地敬重」。

sensesIntro.en: Revere starts with deep respect for a person, rises to sacred regard, then spreads to memory, to valued customs, and finally to worship.
sensesIntro.cn: revere 先从对人的深层敬重出发，上升到对神圣之物的崇奉，再延伸到追念、推崇的事业与习俗，最后抵达崇拜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visitor who lowers the head and folds the hands before something greater.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对更伟大的存在时，来访者低下头、双手交叠。

branches.en: Deep respect for a person is the plainest everyday sense.
branches.cn: 对人的深层敬重是最朴素的日常义项。

branches.en: Awe turned toward holy places and objects becomes sacred regard.
branches.cn: 敬畏投向神圣的场所与物件，就成了视为神圣的崇奉。

branches.en: Respect for someone who has died settles into honoured memory.
branches.cn: 对逝者的敬重沉淀为被珍藏的记忆。

branches.en: The same esteem can be paid to ideas, skills, and customs.
branches.cn: 同样的推崇也可以献给理念、技艺与习俗。

branches.en: Sacred regard is the step below worship, and worship is its fullest form.
branches.cn: 视为神圣是崇拜的前一步，而崇拜是它最饱满的形式。

intro.en: Revere is a plain Latin verb with a prefix, and its English family grows by adding noun, adjective, and adverb endings.
intro.cn: revere 是一个带前缀的拉丁语动词，英语词族靠加名词、形容词与副词词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin vereri means to fear with awe, and revereri adds re- to mean to stand in reverence of something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vereri 意为满怀敬畏地畏惧，revereri 加上 re-，意为对某物心存敬意。

items.meaning: to fear with awe, to respect
items.example: Vereri supplies the fear and respect at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: vereri 提供了词义核心里的敬畏与敬重。

items.meaning: again, back, or with added force
items.example: The prefix re- strengthens the verb into revereri.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把动词加强为 revereri。

items.example: Revereri is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: revereri 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Reverentia gives English the noun reverence.
items.exampleCN: reverentia 为英语提供名词 reverence。

items.example: Reverendus survives as the English title Reverend.
items.exampleCN: reverendus 以英语头衔 Reverend 的形式留存下来。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ence forms the noun reverence.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 构成名词 reverence。

items.example: Reverent adds the -ent ending of adjectives.
items.exampleCN: reverent 加上了形容词词尾 -ent。

items.example: The adverb ending -ly forms reverently.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 构成 reverently。

items.example: The negative prefix ir- turns reverent into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀 ir- 把 reverent 变成它的反义词。

items.example: The agent ending -er names a person who reveres.
items.exampleCN: 施事词尾 -er 表示怀着敬仰的人。

definition_zh: 崇敬；敬畏；敬礼；尊者
definition_en: a feeling of deep respect mixed with awe, shown to someone or something sacred
core_image: 石阶前的人静静跪下，双手在胸前合拢，连呼吸都放轻
scene: 寺院的门槛很高，台阶被踩得发亮，进门前人们会先整理衣襟，再把鞋轻轻脱下。The monk lifted the ancient scroll with great reverence and placed it on the altar.
sceneCN: 这里 reverence 是「崇敬、虔敬」（第 1 个义项：混合着敬畏的深深敬意）；句意：僧人满怀虔敬地捧起那卷古经，把它放在祭坛上。

pos.zh: 崇敬；敬畏
敬礼；鞠躬
（对神职人员的尊称）尊者

senses.title: Deep respect mixed with awe
senses.definition: a feeling of profound respect and wonder felt toward a person, place, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某地或某种理念怀有的深切敬意与敬畏
senses.example: The students stood in silence, filled with reverence for the old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们静静站着，心中充满着对这位老教师的崇敬。
senses.why: The Latin noun reverentia names a state of awe, so the English noun keeps that still, admiring feeling as its centre.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 reverentia 指敬畏的状态，所以英语名词里最核心的，正是这种静静仰望的感受。

senses.title: A formal act of respect
senses.definition: a gesture or honour, such as a bow, given to show respect
senses.definitionCN: 用以表达敬意的动作或礼节，如鞠躬、行礼
senses.example: The visiting team made a deep reverence before the match began.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛开始前，来访的队伍深深鞠了一躬。
senses.why: When the inner feeling is written on the body, it becomes a bow or salute, so the noun can name the gesture itself.
senses.whyCN: 当内心的感受写在身体上，它就变成鞠躬或行礼，于是这个名词也能指敬礼这一动作本身。

senses.title: A title for the clergy
senses.definition: the respectful title used to address a priest or minister
senses.definitionCN: 对神父或牧师等人的尊称
senses.example: The parish greeted the Father with a title of reverence.
senses.exampleCN: 教区信众用表示尊敬的称谓问候这位神父。
senses.why: Because the clergy were addressed with titles of awe, the noun itself became a form of address for them.
senses.whyCN: 因为神职人员一向用带敬畏的称谓来称呼，这个名词本身也就成了对他们的称呼。

senses.title: Honour shown to sacred things
senses.definition: the honoured treatment given to sacred objects, places, or customs
senses.definitionCN: 对神圣的物件、场所或习俗所给予的恭敬对待
senses.example: Visitors remove their shoes out of reverence for the shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 出于对神殿的敬奉，来访者都脱下鞋子。
senses.why: Awe aimed at the holy turns respect into a body of practices, so the word also names how sacred things must be handled.
senses.whyCN: 敬畏指向神圣时，敬意就化为一系列规矩，于是这个词也指神圣之物该被如何对待。

senses.title: High regard for a person or idea
senses.definition: a lasting high opinion of someone, such as an elder or a thinker, or of an idea
senses.definitionCN: 对长辈、思想家或某种理念长期保持的高度评价
senses.example: Older writers held the poet in great reverence.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的作家们对这位诗人极为尊崇。
senses.why: The daily sense of profound respect settles into a lasting reputation, so usage extends to honouring figures and ideas over time.
senses.whyCN: 日常的深切敬意沉淀为长久的声望，于是用法也扩展到对人物与理念的长期推崇。

intro.en: Reverence comes from Latin reverentia, a noun of awe built on the verb vereri, to fear or revere.
intro.cn: reverence 来自拉丁语 reverentia，这是一个表示敬畏的名词，源自动词 vereri（畏惧、敬畏）。

items.en: The root is generally linked to a family of words for fear and awe, though the precise reconstruction is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为其词根与表示畏惧、敬畏的一族词相关，但确切的构拟形式尚有争议。

items.en: The verb vereri means to fear or to hold in awe, and revereri adds the prefix re-.
items.cn: 动词 vereri 意为畏惧或敬畏，revereri 则加上了前缀 re-。

items.en: Reverentia names the state of awe, and reverendus means to be respected.
items.cn: reverentia 指敬畏的状态，reverendus 意为值得尊敬的。

items.en: The noun reverence carries both the feeling and the respectful title for clergy.
items.cn: 名词 reverence 同时承载了这种感受与对神职人员的尊称。

items.en: Reverence enters English as a name for honour shown to God or to a person of rank.
items.cn: reverence 进入英语时，专指献给上帝或地位尊贵者的敬意。

items.en: The word settles into a formal noun, with a rare verb use for bowing.
items.cn: 现代英语中它稳定为正式名词，偶尔作动词表示行礼。

note.en: Reverence is the noun of the revere family, and its neighbours differ mainly in how much fear or how much mere politeness they carry.
note.cn: reverence 是 revere 词族的名词，它与邻近词的差别，主要在于带多少敬畏、多少单纯的礼貌。

entries.definition: showing deep respect

entries.definition: full of reverence
entries.definitionCN: 恭敬的；崇敬的

entries.definition: a feeling of wonder mixed with fear or respect
entries.definitionCN: 敬畏；惊叹

entries.definition: a feeling of admiration for someone
entries.definitionCN: 尊敬

entries.definition: the deepest respect shown to a holy person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 尊崇；敬奉

normalIntro.en: Reverence names the feeling behind the verb revere, and its whole family of endings stays close to the Latin noun reverentia.
normalIntro.cn: reverence 是动词 revere 背后的那种感受，它的整个词尾家族都贴近拉丁语名词 reverentia。

normal.en: The phrase hold someone in reverence uses the preposition in, the longest and most formal of the patterns.
normal.cn: hold someone in reverence 用介词 in 搭配，是这一族说法里最长、最正式的一种。

normal.en: The negative prefix ir- builds irreverence, the direct opposite of the noun.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 ir- 构成 irreverence，正是这个名词的反义。

normal.en: The adjective reverential is heavier than reverent and belongs to written accounts of ritual.
normal.cn: 形容词 reverential 比 reverent 更重，多出现在关于仪式的书面叙述里。

normal.en: The ending -ence marks a state, so reverence is the state a person stands in.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ence 标示状态，所以 reverence 是人处于其中的那种状态。

normal.en: Keep reverence apart from revenge, which speaks of harm, never of honour.
normal.cn: 把 reverence 和 revenge 分开：后者说的是伤害，与敬意毫无关系。

abstract.en: Picture a child copying the grandparents and bowing in perfect mimicry.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子照着祖辈的样子，也在认真地鞠躬。

abstract.en: Imagine a choir hushing itself before the first line of music.
abstract.cn: 想象唱诗班在唱出第一句之前，先让全场安静下来。

abstract.en: See a crowd falling silent as the relic is carried through the street.
abstract.cn: 看见圣物沿街而行时，人群渐渐安静下来。

examples.en: The museum asks visitors to handle the manuscripts with reverence.
examples.cn: 博物馆请来访者怀着敬意对待这些手稿。

examples.en: She spoke of her grandfather with a respect close to reverence.
examples.cn: 她谈起祖父时，语气恭敬得近乎崇敬。

examples.en: Young athletes often hold their club legend in reverence.
examples.cn: 年轻运动员常常敬仰自己俱乐部里的传奇人物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞弗伦斯」——想象一座老图书馆里，翻书的人都把手指放得很轻，这份郑重的敬重就是 reverence；这只是谐音联想，真正的来源与拉丁语 reverentia 有关。

root: 拉丁语 vereri（畏惧、敬畏）→ revereri 加前缀 re- → 名词 reverentia（敬畏）→ 古法语 reverence → 中古英语 reverence → 现代英语 reverence，核心义「混合着敬畏的深深敬意」。

sensesIntro.en: Reverence starts with a deep feeling of awe, becomes a bow when the body answers it, then spreads into a title, into sacred practice, and into lasting regard.
sensesIntro.cn: reverence 从混合敬畏的深切感受出发，当身体做出回应时就成了鞠躬行礼，再延伸到神职称号、对神圣之物的奉礼，以及对人物与理念的长期尊崇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure kneeling at a threshold with hands joined and breath kept light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跪在门槛前，双手合拢，连呼吸都放轻。

branches.en: The inner feeling of awe is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 内心那份敬畏的感受，是这个词的首义。

branches.en: A bow or salute is the feeling written into the body.
branches.cn: 鞠躬或行礼，是这份感受写在身体上的样子。

branches.en: Rules for handling holy things turn the feeling into practice.
branches.cn: 对待圣物的种种规矩，把这份感受变成了日常实践。

branches.en: Lasting respect for a master or an idea grows out of the same feeling.
branches.cn: 对大师或某种理念的长久尊崇，也生长于同一种感受。

branches.en: A title is a verbal bow, and both are formal gestures of honour.
branches.cn: 称号是口头上的鞠躬，两者都是正式的致敬之举。

intro.en: Reverence is a Latin abstract noun, and English surrounds it with adjectives, an adverb, verbs, and a negated form.
intro.cn: reverence 是一个拉丁语抽象名词，英语围绕它构建了形容词、副词、动词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin reverentia means awe and respect, and its verb revereri means to stand in awe of something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reverentia 意为敬畏与敬重，其动词 revereri 意为对某物心怀敬畏。

items.example: Vereri supplies the awe that the noun carries.
items.exampleCN: vereri 提供了这个名词所带的敬畏。

items.example: Revereri is the verb behind the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: revereri 是拉丁语名词背后的动词。

items.example: Reverentia is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: reverentia 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -entia turns a state into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -entia 把一种状态变成抽象名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The English -ence mirrors the Latin -entia in reverence.
items.exampleCN: 英语词尾 -ence 在 reverence 里对应拉丁语 -entia。

items.example: Reverent is the adjective paired most often with the noun.
items.exampleCN: reverent 是最常与这个名词配对的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms the heavier adjective reverential.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成更书面的形容词 reverential。

items.example: The prefix ir- forms the noun irreverence.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 构成名词 irreverence。

items.example: Irreverence names the opposite of the honoured feeling.
items.exampleCN: irreverence 指与敬意相反的态度。

items.example: As a rare verb, reverence means to make a bow to someone.
items.exampleCN: 作罕见动词时，reverence 意为向某人鞠躬。

definition_zh: 白日梦；遐想；幻想曲
definition_en: a state of pleasant, dreamy thinking in which you forget the present
core_image: 有人望着窗外，手里的杯子停在半空，眼神越过街道和树梢
scene: 咖啡馆里很吵，桌上那杯茶已经凉了，望向窗外的人一直没动，直到朋友敲了敲桌子。Lost in a reverie, she did not hear the waiter calling her name twice.
sceneCN: 这里 reverie 是「遐想、出神」（第 1 个义项：愉快而恍惚的白日梦状态）；句意：她沉醉在遐想中，连服务生叫了她两遍名字也没听见。

pos.zh: 白日梦；遐想；出神
（音乐）幻想曲；梦幻曲

derivatives.zh: 罕见派生词，由 reverie 加 -ist 构成，义为「爱沉思遐想的人」
复合形容词，由 reverie 加 -like 构成，义为「如梦似幻的」
同源于古法语 resver 的词，义为「说胡话；狂热地谈」

senses.title: A pleasant dreamy state
senses.definition: a state of being pleasantly absorbed in a person own thoughts so that the present goes unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地沉浸在自己的思绪里，以致忽略了眼前
senses.example: She was lost in a reverie during the whole lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 整堂讲座期间她都沉浸在遐想中。
senses.why: The Old French verb resver means to be delirious or to dream wildly, so the noun first names a mind that has wandered off to another place.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 resver 意为疯癫或胡乱做梦，所以这个名词最初指的是飘到别处去的大脑。

senses.title: A fanciful daydream
senses.definition: a set of imagined scenes that the mind builds while the body sits still
senses.definitionCN: 身体静坐不动时，头脑里构筑的一系列想象画面
senses.example: In his reveries the small shop became a chain of stores.
senses.exampleCN: 在他的白日梦里，那家小店变成了一整排连锁店。
senses.why: Once the wandering is pleasant, it takes shape as pictures and plans, so the word also names the dream itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这份游走变得愉快，它就会成形为画面和计划，于是这个词也指那个梦本身。

senses.title: A dreamy musical piece
senses.definition: a short, dreamy piece of music or writing that suggests wandering thought
senses.definitionCN: 短小而梦幻的器乐或文学作品，给人以思绪飘游之感
senses.example: The pianist closed the recital with a gentle reverie.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家以一首轻柔的幻想曲结束了独奏会。
senses.why: Composers borrowed the word to label music that sounds like daydreaming, so the noun gained an artistic sense.
senses.whyCN: 作曲家借这个词来标记听起来像在做白日梦的音乐，于是名词获得了艺术领域的一义。

senses.title: A state of melancholy thought
senses.definition: a state of lost, slightly melancholy thought, especially after a loss
senses.definitionCN: 一种出神而略带忧郁的思路，尤指在失去之后
senses.example: He fell into a reverie whenever her name came up.
senses.exampleCN: 每当有人提起她的名字，他就会陷入一阵忧郁的沉思。
senses.why: The old French sense carried a hint of wildness, and when dreamy thought turns inward it easily takes on a sad colour.
senses.whyCN: 古法语原义带着一丝狂乱，当出神的思绪转向内心，很容易染上悲伤的色调。

senses.title: An idle daydream habit
senses.definition: a habit of idle daydreaming that keeps a person apart from everyday work
senses.definitionCN: 一种爱做白日梦、使自己远离日常事务的习惯
senses.example: Her reveries often made her late for meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 她爱做白日梦的习惯常让她开会迟到。
senses.why: When the state repeats, it becomes a trait, so the plural can name the tendency of a person to drift away.
senses.whyCN: 当这种状态反复出现，它就成了性格的一部分，于是复数形式可以指一个人老是走神的毛病。

intro.en: Reverie comes from French reverie, built on the old verb rever, to dream or be delirious, whose origin is not certain.
intro.cn: reverie 来自法语 reverie，源自古动词 rever（做梦、胡言乱语），其更远的来源并不确定。

items.en: The verb resver or rever means to be mad, to rave, or to dream wildly, and other Romanic languages have a similar-looking verb.
items.cn: 动词 resver 或 rever 意为发狂、胡言乱语或胡乱做梦，其他罗曼语族语言也有形似的动词。

items.en: The noun resverie means madness as well as a wild dream, and printers often show its long s as an f-like form.
items.cn: 名词 resverie 既指疯癫也指狂乱的梦，旧时印刷常把它长 s 的形状排得有点像 f。

items.en: The noun softens and comes to mean a pleasant daydream or a moment of dreamy thought.
items.cn: 这个名词渐渐柔化，转而表示愉快的白日梦或一段梦幻般的思绪。

items.en: English borrows reverie with the gentler sense of a dreamy, wandering state of mind.
items.cn: 英语借用 reverie 时，取的是「思绪飘游」这类较柔和的意思。

items.en: The word extends to music and literature, and French also revives it as the spelling reverie.
items.cn: 这个词延伸到音乐与文学领域，法语后来也以 reverie 这一拼写重新使用它。

items.en: Today the word usually describes a gentle, pleasant drift of the mind.
items.cn: 今天这个词通常描述温和愉快的走神。

note.en: Reverie names the drifting mind, and it sits between true dreams, idle daydreaming, and the calm state of being lost in thought.
note.cn: reverie 指飘游的心神，夹在真正的梦、闲散的白日梦与静静出神之间。

entries.definition: deep respect and awe
entries.definitionCN: 崇敬；敬畏，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the Old French verb for dreaming wildly
entries.definitionCN: 古法语动词，意为胡乱做梦，是这个词的更早来源

entries.definition: in a deeply respectful way
entries.definitionCN: 恭敬地，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: pleasant imagination while awake
entries.definitionCN: 白日梦

entries.definition: a half conscious state absorbed in something
entries.definitionCN: 恍惚；出神

entries.definition: quiet thinking that floats along
entries.definitionCN: 默想；沉思

normalIntro.en: Reverie keeps the sense of a wandering mind from French rever, soft enough now to feel pleasant rather than mad.
normalIntro.cn: reverie 保留了法语 rever 里「心神游走」的意思，只是今天已经柔化到与愉快相关，而与疯癫无关。

normal.en: The phrase be lost in a reverie uses the preposition in, like being lost in a forest.
normal.cn: be lost in a reverie 用介词 in 搭配，就像迷失在森林里一样。

normal.en: The verb wake from a reverie marks the moment the mind returns to the room.
normal.cn: wake from a reverie 用来标记心神回到房间的那一刻。

normal.en: The plural reveries changes only the y to ies, like story to stories.
normal.cn: 复数 reveries 只是把 y 变成 ies，和 story 变 stories 的规则一样。

normal.en: In music, a reverie is a dreamy solo piece, not a grand concerto.
normal.cn: 在音乐里，reverie 指的是梦幻的独奏小品，而不是宏大的协奏曲。

normal.en: Keep reverie apart from reverence and reverse, which share letters but carry respect and turning, not dreaming.
normal.cn: 把 reverie 与 reverence、reverse 分开：它们字母相近，但分别表示敬重和倒转，与做梦无关。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle whistling while nobody in the kitchen hears it.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房里的水壶正在尖叫，却没有人听见。

abstract.en: See a page of notes with a pen stopped halfway through one word.
abstract.cn: 看到整整一页笔记里，有一支笔停在一个词的半中间。

abstract.en: Imagine a rainy afternoon where the clock ticks louder than usual.
abstract.cn: 想象一个下雨的午后，钟表走得比平时更响。

examples.en: A knock at the door woke him from his reverie.
examples.cn: 一阵敲门声把他从遐想中唤醒。

examples.en: The long train ride left her plenty of time for reveries.
examples.cn: 漫长的火车旅途中，她有充足的时间遐想。

examples.en: The composer wrote a short reverie for piano and cello.
examples.cn: 这位作曲家为钢琴与大提琴写了一首短小的梦幻曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞夫瑞」——想象一个人望着窗外的雨帘，脑子里已经飘到另一座城市去了，这就是 reverie；这只是谐音联想，真正的来源与古法语 rever（做梦、胡言）有关。

root: 古法语 resver（发狂、胡乱做梦，更远来源不确定）→ 中古法语 resverie（疯癫；狂乱的梦）→ 法语 reverie（白日梦、遐想）→ 英语 reverie，核心义「心神飘离眼前、做起白日梦」。

sensesIntro.en: Reverie begins as a pleasantly wandering mind, takes the shape of imagined scenes, lends its name to dreamy music, can darken into melancholy, and can settle into a habit.
sensesIntro.cn: reverie 始于愉快飘走的心神，随后变成想象中的画面，也为梦幻的音乐命名，还可能在悲伤时染上忧郁，最后沉淀为一种习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person staring past the street with a cup held still halfway to the mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人越过街道望向远处，杯子停在送到嘴边的一半处。

branches.en: The gentle, absorbed state of mind is the central sense.
branches.cn: 温和而出神的心境，是这个词的中心义项。

branches.en: The imagined scenes built in that state are the daydream sense.
branches.cn: 在这种状态里构筑的想象画面，就是白日梦一义。

branches.en: Music that sounds like dreaming borrows the word as a title.
branches.cn: 听起来像在梦游的音乐借用了这个词作标题。

branches.en: When the drift turns inward, the dreamy state takes on sadness.
branches.cn: 当思绪向内飘去，这种梦幻状态就带上了悲伤。

branches.en: Repeated drifting turns one lost moment into a settled habit.
branches.cn: 反复走神，就把一次次走神变成了一种固定的习惯。

intro.en: Reverie is a French loanword with a light English family, built mainly on the noun and a few compounds.
intro.cn: reverie 是一个法语借词，英语词族较轻，主要围绕名词本身和少量复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Reverie has no reliable Latin ancestor, so its Latin connection is limited to a debated root and a shared Romance family.
latinIntro.cn: reverie 没有可靠的拉丁语祖先，它与拉丁语的联系仅限于一个存疑的词根与罗曼语族里的同族词。

items.example: Resver is generally taken as the base of reverie.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为 resver 是 reverie 的词基。

items.example: French reverie shifts from madness to pleasant dreaming.
items.exampleCN: 法语 reverie 从疯癫转向愉快的做梦。

items.example: English keeps the French spelling of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了这个法语名词的拼写。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或场所的法语词尾
items.example: The suffix -erie builds abstract nouns in French.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -erie 在法语里构成抽象名词。

items.example: The plural changes y to ies.
items.exampleCN: 复数把 y 变成 ies。

items.example: The rare noun reverist names a daydreamer.
items.exampleCN: 罕见的名词 reverist 指爱做白日梦的人。

items.example: The compound reverie-like means dreamlike.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 reverie-like 意为如梦似幻的。

items.example: Rave is a distant cousin from the same old verb.
items.exampleCN: rave 来自同一个古老动词，算是远亲。

items.example: Daydream is the plain English near synonym of reverie.
items.exampleCN: daydream 是 reverie 朴素的英语近义词。

items.example: Musing is calmer and less dreamlike than reverie.
items.exampleCN: musing 比 reverie 更平静，也不那么像做梦。

definition_zh: 复活；复兴；复苏；重新流行；（宗教的）奋兴
definition_en: the process of returning to life, strength, or popularity after a period of decline
core_image: 熄灭的火堆被重新点燃，火光再次照亮四周
scene: 老城区的石板街沉寂多年，如今咖啡馆和书店纷纷开张，街区迎来了新的生机。The old cobbled quarter enjoyed a revival after new cafés and bookshops opened there.
sceneCN: 这里 revival 是「复兴」（第 3 个义项：某地在衰落后重新兴旺）；句意：新开的咖啡馆和书店让这条老石板街区迎来了复兴。

pos.zh: 复活；复兴；复苏；重新流行

derivatives.zh: revival 的基础动词，义为「使复活；使复兴；苏醒」
revival 加后缀 -ist，指推动复兴运动的人，尤指宗教奋兴者
revival 加后缀 -ism，指努力恢复旧信仰或旧风俗的倾向
revivalist 也作形容词，义为「复兴运动的；复兴主义的」

senses.title: A return to life or consciousness
senses.definition: the act of coming back to life or consciousness after death or a serious illness
senses.definitionCN: 死亡或重病之后重新获得生命或意识的过程
senses.example: Miracles of revival are rare outside emergency rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 在医院急诊室之外，起死回生的奇迹很罕见。
senses.why: Revival is the noun of revive, so it names the act of life coming back to a body.
senses.whyCN: revival 是 revive 的名词形式，core image 中重新燃起的火堆正对应身体重新得到生命，所以最先得到「复活」义。

senses.title: A return of public interest
senses.definition: a time when something that was unfashionable or forgotten becomes popular and active again
senses.definitionCN: 曾经不时髦或被遗忘的事物重新流行、重新活跃起来的时期
senses.example: There has been a revival of interest in vinyl records.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对黑胶唱片的兴趣重新高涨起来。
senses.why: From a body regaining life the noun shifts to any declining thing regaining popularity, a trend drawn as a second flame.
senses.whyCN: 从身体重新获得生命，名词自然转向任何衰落事物重新获得人气，把回潮的趋势画成第二簇火焰。

senses.title: The recovery of a town or economy
senses.definition: the process by which a place, business, or economy becomes successful and busy again
senses.definitionCN: 地方、企业或经济重新变得繁荣、活跃的过程
senses.example: The new port brought a revival to the small fishing town.
senses.exampleCN: 新港口让这座小渔镇重新繁荣起来。
senses.why: An economy is pictured as a living body, so its recovery is described with the same life-returning noun.
senses.whyCN: 经济被想象成有生命的身体，因此它的复原直接沿用了「生命回归」的名词，义为复苏。

senses.title: A new production of an old work
senses.definition: a new production of an old play, film, or musical, or a new edition of an old book
senses.definitionCN: 旧戏剧、影片或音乐剧的新版演出，或旧书的新版
senses.example: The directors staged a revival of the classic comedy.
senses.exampleCN: 导演们把这出经典喜剧重新搬上了舞台。
senses.why: A work that left the repertory had gone dark, so bringing it back to the stage is another revival.
senses.whyCN: 退出演出剧目的作品像火一样暗了下来，把它重新搬回舞台，正好又是一次「复燃」。

senses.title: A religious awakening
senses.definition: a period of renewed enthusiasm for religious faith, often with large public meetings
senses.definitionCN: 宗教信仰重新高涨的时期，常伴随大规模布道集会
senses.example: A great religious revival swept through the American frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 一场盛大的宗教奋兴运动席卷了美国边疆地区。
senses.why: Faith believed to have cooled is reheated, and the resulting revival became a fixed name for mass religious enthusiasm.
senses.whyCN: 被视为冷却了的信仰被重新加热，这一「复燃」顺势成为宗教热潮的固定名称。

intro.en: Revival comes from the Latin root vivo, to live, and the verb revive, with the noun suffix -al.
intro.cn: revival 来自拉丁语词根 vivo（活着）与动词 revive，再加上名词后缀 -al。

items.en: Vivere means to live, and revivere means to live again.
items.cn: vivere 意为活着，revivere 意为重新活过来。

items.en: The verb revivre carries the form into French.
items.cn: 动词 revivre 把这一词形带入法语。

items.en: The verb revive is recorded in English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语动词 revive 在十六世纪有记录。

items.en: The abstract noun revival appears later, from revive plus -al.
items.cn: 抽象名词 revival 出现较晚，由 revive 加 -al 构成。

items.en: Revival becomes the usual word for renewed faith, art styles, and economy.
items.cn: revival 成为指信仰重新高涨、艺术风格回潮与经济的常用词。

note.en: Revival is the noun of revive and shares the living root viv with survive and vivid; in meaning it overlaps with restoration, renaissance, and comeback.
note.cn: revival 是 revive 的名词，与 survive、vivid 共享「活」词根 viv；意义上与 restoration、renaissance、comeback 有重叠。

entries.definition: to bring back to life or activity
entries.definitionCN: revival 的基础动词，义为「使复活；使复兴」

entries.definition: to stay alive through danger
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的「存活」，sur- 表示在上、超过

entries.definition: bright and full of life
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的「生动的；鲜艳的」，源自「活」的词根

entries.definition: a return to success or popularity
entries.definitionCN: 更口语的「复出；回潮」

entries.definition: a rebirth of art or learning
entries.definitionCN: 更正式的「文艺复兴式的新生」

entries.definition: the act of returning something to an earlier state
entries.definitionCN: 近义：把事物恢复到原来状态的行为

normalIntro.en: Revival is revive plus -al, so it keeps the re- again and viv live shape of its verb.
normalIntro.cn: revival 由 revive 加 -al 构成，保留了动词里 re-（再次）加 viv（活）的结构。

normal.en: Keep the verb revive in mind, then add the noun suffix -al.
normal.cn: 先记住动词 revive，再加上名词后缀 -al。

normal.en: An economic revival means falling trade has risen again.
normal.cn: economic revival 意味着萧条的交易重新回升。

normal.en: A revival of interest is a second wave of popularity.
normal.cn: a revival of interest 就是人气的第二波。

normal.en: A play revival puts an old show back on the stage.
normal.cn: play revival 就是让旧剧目重新登台。

normal.en: The viv root also appears in survive and vivid.
normal.cn: viv 词根同样出现在 survive 与 vivid 中。

abstract.en: See an ember glowing under grey ash.
abstract.cn: 想象灰烬底下还有一颗炭火在发红。

abstract.en: Imagine a forgotten street filling with music again.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被遗忘的街道重新响起音乐。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd singing a song it stopped singing years ago.
abstract.cn: 想象人群唱起一首多年前不再唱的老歌。

examples.en: The town has seen a revival since the railway reopened.
examples.cn: 自从铁路重新通车，这座小镇就复苏了。

examples.en: Her revival of the old craft won a national prize.
examples.cn: 她对这门古老手工艺的复兴赢得了全国奖项。

examples.en: Folk music is enjoying a revival among young listeners.
examples.cn: 民谣音乐正在年轻听众中重新流行起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞外欧」——外面的一团火又「燃」起来了，就是复兴；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ vivere（活着）→ revivere（重新活过来）→ 英语 revive → revive + -al → revival，核心义「生命、活力的回归」。

sensesIntro.en: Revival begins with a body or a fire coming back to life, then widens to popularity returning, places and economies recovering, old works being staged again, and finally religious fervour rekindled.
sensesIntro.cn: revival 先从身体或火堆重新获得生命说起，再扩展到人气回潮、地方与经济复苏、旧作品重新上演，最后是宗教信仰重新高涨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of ashes stirred into a fresh bright fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆灰烬被重新拨亮，火光再次照亮四周。

branches.en: Life returning to a body is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 生命回到身体，是字面义。

branches.en: A trend that faded regains public interest.
branches.cn: 褪色的风尚重新获得公众兴趣。

branches.en: Places and economies recover their activity.
branches.cn: 地方与经济恢复活力。

branches.en: Works return to the stage and faith returns to the heart.
branches.cn: 作品回到舞台，信仰也回到心中，都是「重新燃起」。

branches.en: Saving a life and saving a town both use the fire coming back image.
branches.cn: 救人命与拯救小镇都借用「火重新燃起」的画面。

intro.en: Revival is re- plus viv plus the noun suffix -al, a shape shared with survive, vivid, and revivalist.
intro.cn: revival 由 re- 加 viv 再加名词后缀 -al 组成，这一结构同样见于 survive、vivid 与 revivalist。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere means to live and vivus means alive, the source of the whole viv family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere 意为活着，vivus 意为活着的，是整个 viv 词族的来源。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the idea of a second time.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 增添「再一次」的意思。

items.example: Vivere is the living root behind revive.
items.exampleCN: vivere 是 revive 背后的「活」词根。

items.example: Revivere is the Latin forerunner of revive.
items.exampleCN: revivere 是 revive 的拉丁语前身。

items.example: The suffix -al turns revive into revival.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把 revive 变成 revival。

items.example: Revival names the process of coming back.
items.exampleCN: revival 表示回归的过程。

items.example: Revive is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: revive 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.example: Survive keeps the viv root as vive.
items.exampleCN: survive 把 viv 词根写成 vive。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms revivalist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 revivalist。

items.meaningCN: 复兴运动者；奋兴布道家
items.example: Revivalist is a person who spreads revival.
items.exampleCN: revivalist 指推动复兴的人。

items.meaningCN: 表示主义或倾向的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ism forms revivalism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 revivalism。

definition_zh: 复活；苏醒；复苏；使复兴；重新流行
definition_en: to bring back to life, strength, or activity, or to come back to life
core_image: 熄灭的火苗被人吹了一口气，重新燃起
scene: 演出中场休息时观众都垂头丧气，压轴乐队上台一开嗓，全场立刻重新振奋起来。When the headline band opened with a fast number, the tired audience revived immediately.
sceneCN: 这里 revive 是「重新振奋起来」（第 3 个义项：恢复活力与精神）；句意：压轴乐队以一首快歌开场时，疲惫的观众立刻重新振奋起来。

pos.zh: 使复活；使苏醒；使复兴；重新上演
苏醒；复苏；重新流行

derivatives.zh: revive 加名词后缀 -al，构成「复兴；复苏；复活」
revive 加施事后缀 -er，指使某事物复活或重新流行的人
revive 同源的 -ify 动词，义为「使恢复生机」，更书面
revive 的现在分词转作形容词，义为「提神的；令人振作的」

senses.title: To bring somebody back to consciousness
senses.definition: to make a person who has fainted or nearly died conscious again
senses.definitionCN: 使昏倒或近乎死亡的人重新恢复意识
senses.example: The lifeguard managed to revive the swimmer on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 救生员在海滩上设法让那名游泳者苏醒过来。
senses.why: The re- prefix means again, and live supplies the life, so to revive is literally to give life back.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示「再次」，词干 live 表示「生命」，所以 revive 字面上就是「把生命还回去」，意象是熄灭后又亮起的火苗。

senses.title: To bring a practice or idea back into use
senses.definition: to make a custom, art form, or idea active and popular again after a period of decline
senses.definitionCN: 使习俗、艺术形式或观念在衰落一段时间后重新活跃、重新流行
senses.example: The council hopes to revive the old riverside market.
senses.exampleCN: 市政委员会希望让河边那处老集市重新兴旺起来。
senses.why: From reviving a body the verb extends to reviving anything that seemed dead, such as a tradition or an industry.
senses.whyCN: 从「让身体复活」引申到「让看似已死的事物复活」，传统、行业、活动都能被 revive，所以有了「复兴、重新流行」。

senses.title: To become lively or strong again
senses.definition: to feel or become full of energy, strength, or enthusiasm again
senses.definitionCN: 重新感到或变得精力充沛、有力量、有热情
senses.example: After a short nap she revived enough to join the hike.
senses.exampleCN: 小睡片刻后她恢复了精力，足以参加徒步。
senses.why: Because the word names life returning, it also describes energy and mood coming back after fatigue.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词的核心是「生命回归」，所以它也描述精力与情绪在疲惫之后重新回来，这个义项用不及物用法。

senses.title: To stage an old work again
senses.definition: to put on a play, film, or other work again after it had been out of production or out of print
senses.definitionCN: 把已停演或绝版的戏剧、影片等作品再次上演或再版
senses.example: The theatre revived the play for its fiftieth anniversary.
senses.exampleCN: 剧院为这部戏上演五十周年重新排演了它。
senses.why: A work taken off the stage is figuratively dead, so bringing it back is another instance of the life-returning image.
senses.whyCN: 一个作品被撤下舞台，在比喻意义上就「死了」，把它重新搬回舞台正是「生命回归」意象的又一实例。

senses.title: To restore a failing thing
senses.definition: to make something that is failing, weak, or in decline strong and successful again
senses.definitionCN: 使衰败、疲弱或下滑的事物重新强健、重新成功
senses.example: Tax cuts were used to revive the struggling local economy.
senses.exampleCN: 减税被用来振兴苦苦挣扎的地方经济。
senses.why: An economy or a business is pictured as a living body, so helping it recover uses the same verb as helping a patient.
senses.whyCN: 经济或企业被想象成有生命的身体，帮助它们复原自然就借用了救病人的同一个动词，所以义为「振兴」。

intro.en: Revive joins the Latin prefix re-, meaning again, to the root vivo, to live, through the senses of the Latin verb revivere.
intro.cn: revive 由拉丁语前缀 re-（再次）与词根 vivo（活着）结合而成，经由拉丁语动词 revivere 传入英语。

items.en: Vivere means to live, and revivere means to live again.
items.cn: vivere 意为活着，revivere 意为重新活过来。

items.en: The re- prefix marks repetition, so revivere is to come back to life.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 表示重复，因此 revivere 就是重新回到生命。

items.en: The verb revivre is attested in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 动词 revivre 在十五世纪已有使用记录。

items.en: The verb revive enters English with the sense of returning to life.
items.cn: 英语 revive 在十五世纪进入英语，义为「复活」。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to traditions, industries, plays, and old fashions.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词扩展到传统、行业、戏剧和旧时尚。

note.en: Revive shares the Latin root viv with vivid and survive, and sits close to restore, resurrect, and recover.
note.cn: revive 与 vivid、survive 共享拉丁语词根 viv，意义上靠近 restore、resurrect、recover。

entries.definition: the act or fact of coming back to life or popularity
entries.definitionCN: revive 加 -al 构成的名词，义为「复兴；复苏」

entries.definition: to continue to live despite a threat
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的「存活」：sur- 表示「在上、超过」，词根同为 viv

entries.definition: producing powerful impressions or bright colours
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的「生动的；鲜艳的」，源自 vivere 的「活」义

entries.definition: to bring something back to a former condition
entries.definitionCN: 近义：把事物恢复到原来的状态

entries.definition: to bring a dead person or a forgotten thing back
entries.definitionCN: 更正式的近义：使死者复活，或使被遗忘的事物重新被提起

entries.definition: to become healthy or strong again
entries.definitionCN: 近义：恢复健康或体力

normalIntro.en: Revive is built from re- again and vivo live, so every use pictures life or energy returning.
normalIntro.cn: revive 由表示「再次」的 re- 与表示「活着」的 vivo 构成，无论怎么用都离不开生命或活力的回归。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again and viv means life.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，viv 表示生命。

normal.en: Revive the economy means to make it active again.
normal.cn: revive the economy 指让经济重新活跃起来。

normal.en: A stage play can be revived for a new audience.
normal.cn: 一部舞台剧可以为新观众重新上演。

normal.en: Revival is the noun, and both words keep the re- plus viv shape.
normal.cn: revival 是名词形式，两步拼写都保留 re- 加 viv 的结构。

normal.en: Remember survive and vivid share the same living root.
normal.cn: 记住 survive 与 vivid 共享同一个「活」的词根。

abstract.en: Picture a doused campfire catching flame again.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆被浇灭的营火再次腾起火焰。

abstract.en: Imagine a tired runner finding a second wind on the hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一位疲惫的跑者在山坡上重新找回力气。

abstract.en: Think of an old-fashioned tune suddenly played at a new party.
abstract.cn: 想象一支老派曲调忽然在年轻人的聚会上被奏响。

examples.en: He revived quickly after the trainer gave him some water.
examples.cn: 教练给他喝了点水之后，他很快就缓过来了。

examples.en: The city wants to revive its old harbour district.
examples.cn: 这座城市想让它老旧的港区重新兴旺起来。

examples.en: A popular film revived interest in classical music.
examples.cn: 一部热门电影重新激起了人们对古典音乐的兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞歪五」——冬天过去，歪斜的树又「活」过来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ vivere（活着）→ revivere（重新活过来）→ 古法语 revivre → 英语 revive，核心义「生命、活力重新回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Revive starts with a body coming back to life, spreads to customs and ideas returning to use, and then to freshness of energy and to any failing thing being restored.
sensesIntro.cn: revive 先从身体复活说起，再延伸到习俗与观念的重新流行，最后扩展到精力恢复和任何衰败事物的振兴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dying flame that is blown on and burns again.
core.cn: 核心意象：快要熄灭的火苗被吹一口气，重新烧了起来。

branches.en: A person regaining consciousness is the literal return to life.
branches.cn: 人恢复意识，是字面意义上的「重新活过来」。

branches.en: Customs and ideas that faded are brought back into use.
branches.cn: 褪色的习俗与观念被重新拿回来使用。

branches.en: Energy and enthusiasm return after fatigue.
branches.cn: 疲惫之后精力与热情重新回来。

branches.en: A tradition and a stage work both come back for a new audience.
branches.cn: 传统与舞台作品都以「为新观众复活」的方式回归。

branches.en: Saving a patient and rescuing an economy share the same life metaphor.
branches.cn: 救病人与救经济共享同一个「生命」隐喻。

intro.en: Revive is re- plus root viv, the living root that also forms survive, vivid, and vivacious.
intro.cn: revive 由前缀 re- 加词根 viv 构成，这个「活」词根还构成 survive、vivid、vivacious。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere means to live, and vivus means alive, giving English the viv family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere 意为活着，vivus 意为活着的，共同构成英语的 viv 词族。

items.example: The prefix re- marks a second happening.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示事情再次发生。

items.example: Vivere is the living root of revive.
items.exampleCN: vivere 是 revive 的「活」词根。

items.example: Vivo is the first person form of vivere.
items.exampleCN: vivo 是 vivere 的第一人称形式。

items.example: Vivus describes a living thing.
items.exampleCN: vivus 描述活着的生物。

items.example: Revivere joins re- to vivere.
items.exampleCN: revivere 由 re- 与 vivere 结合。

items.example: Survive is built from sur- plus vive.
items.exampleCN: survive 由 sur- 加 vive 构成。

items.example: Vivid means full of life to the eye.
items.exampleCN: vivid 指在视觉上充满生命感。

items.example: The suffix -al forms revival.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 revival。

items.example: Revival names the process of coming back.
items.exampleCN: revival 表示复活的过程。

items.example: Reviving describes fresh air or a cool drink.
items.exampleCN: reviving 可形容清新的空气或冷饮。

definition_zh: 撤销；废除；吊销；撤回
definition_en: the official act of cancelling a law, licence, decision, or promise
core_image: 一份盖了公章的授权书被当众收回，重新压回抽屉
scene: 交通部门查实司机醉酒驾车后，依法收回了他手里的驾驶执照，并寄出了正式通知。After the driver was caught drunk at the wheel, the transport office ordered the revocation of his licence.
sceneCN: 这里 revocation 是「吊销；撤销」（第 2 个义项：正式取消许可证、合同、决定等）；句意：司机醉驾被抓后，交通部门下令吊销他的驾照。

pos.zh: 撤销；废除；吊销；撤回

collocations.zh: 可被撤销；随时可能被撤销

derivatives.zh: revocation 的基础动词，义为「撤销；废除；吊销」
revoke 加 -able，义为「可撤销的；可废除的」
revocable 加 -ity，指「可撤销性」
否定前缀 ir- 加 revocable，义为「不可撤销的；无法挽回的」

senses.title: The calling back of a right or privilege
senses.definition: the act of officially taking back a right, privilege, or power that had been granted
senses.definitionCN: 正式收回此前授予的权利、特权或权力
senses.example: The order called for the revocation of all fishing permits.
senses.exampleCN: 该命令要求撤销所有捕捞许可证。
senses.why: The Latin verb revocare means to call back, so revocation is the formal act of calling a granted thing back in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 revocare 意为「把……叫回来」，所以 revocation 就是正式「把已给出的东西叫回来」，对应那份被收回的授权书。

senses.title: The cancellation of a licence or agreement
senses.definition: the official cancellation of a licence, contract, or legal agreement
senses.definitionCN: 对许可证、合同或法律协议的正式取消
senses.example: Driving after a ban can lead to the revocation of the licence for life.
senses.exampleCN: 被禁驾后仍然驾车，可能导致终身吊销驾照。
senses.why: Once written permission is withdrawn it no longer exists, so the everyday legal sense is cancelling a permit or agreement.
senses.whyCN: 书面许可一旦被撤回就失去效力，因此在法律日常语境中就是吊销许可证、撤销合同。

senses.title: The repeal of a law or decision
senses.definition: the act of withdrawing or ending a law, ruling, or official decision
senses.definitionCN: 撤回或终止法律、裁决、官方决定的行为
senses.example: The revocation of the old housing act opened the site to developers.
senses.exampleCN: 旧住房法的废除使该地块向开发商敞开大门。
senses.why: A law is a public order; to call it back is to erase it, so the noun also covers repealing a regulation.
senses.whyCN: 法律是一条公开的命令，把它「叫回来」就等于抹去它，因此这个词也指废除法规、裁决。

senses.title: The withdrawal of a statement or promise
senses.definition: the act of taking back a promise, offer, or statement that had been made
senses.definitionCN: 收回已作出的承诺、提议或言论的行为
senses.example: He issued a public revocation of his earlier support for the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他公开撤回了此前对该计划的支持。
senses.why: Words once given can be called back too, so the legal noun stretches to withdrawing a promise or an open offer.
senses.whyCN: 说出口的话同样可以被「叫回来」，所以这个法律名词自然延伸到撤回承诺、撤回公开支持。

senses.title: In law, the annulment of an act
senses.definition: a legal term for the annulment of an agent act by the person who gave the authority
senses.definitionCN: 法律术语，指授权人宣告其代理人所做的行为无效
senses.example: The agency ended with the revocation of the power of attorney.
senses.exampleCN: 随着授权委托书被撤销，这一代理关系随之终止。
senses.why: In Roman and modern law the granter keeps the power to call agency back, which gives the noun its technical legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法与近现代法律中，授权者始终保有「把代理权叫回来」的权力，这一制度背景给了名词专门的法律义。

intro.en: Revocation goes back to Latin vocare, to call, and the verb revocare, to call back, with the prefix re- meaning back.
intro.cn: revocation 可追溯到拉丁语 vocare（呼叫）与动词 revocare（叫回来），前缀 re- 表示「往回」。

items.en: Vocare means to call, and re- means back, so revocare means to call back.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼叫，re- 意为往回，所以 revocare 意为把……叫回来。

items.en: Revocatio names the act of calling something back, especially a promise or an order.
items.cn: revocatio 表示「把某物叫回来」的行为，尤指承诺或命令。

items.en: The noun reaches French as revocation.
items.cn: 这一名词以 revocation 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English borrows revocation for the repeal of laws and grants.
items.cn: 英语借入 revocation，用于法律的废止与授权的收回。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly for licences, parole, and legal agreements.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用于执照、假释与法律协议。

note.en: Revocation shares the calling root voc with evoke, provoke, and vocal; among near meanings it sits beside cancellation and repeal.
note.cn: revocation 与 evoke、provoke、vocal 共享「叫」的词根 voc；近义一侧靠近 cancellation 与 repeal。

entries.definition: to cancel a licence, law, or permission
entries.definitionCN: revocation 的基础动词，义为「撤销；吊销」

entries.definition: able to be cancelled
entries.definitionCN: 同根的形容词，义为「可撤销的」

entries.definition: relating to the voice
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的「声音的」，词根 voc 意为呼叫

entries.definition: the act of stopping a booking or agreement
entries.definitionCN: 近义：取消预订或协议的通用说法

entries.definition: the official ending of a law
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语：正式废止法律

entries.definition: the act of taking something back
entries.definitionCN: 近义：撤回、收回

normalIntro.en: Revocation is revoke plus -ation, and the root voc means to call, so the word pictures something being called back.
normalIntro.cn: revocation 由 revoke 加 -ation 构成，词根 voc 意为「叫」，整个词就是在画「被叫回来」这件事。

normal.en: Revoke is the verb, and revocation is the act of cancelling.
normal.cn: revoke 是动词，revocation 是取消的行为本身。

normal.en: The root voc appears in voice, vocal, and evoke.
normal.cn: 词根 voc 出现在 voice、vocal 与 evoke 中。

normal.en: Revocation of a licence means the licence is taken away.
normal.cn: revocation of a licence 就是执照被收回。

normal.en: Anything revocable can be revoked, but it stays irrevocable once final.
normal.cn: 凡 revocable 的都能被撤销，但变成 irrevocable 后就无可挽回。

normal.en: Legal English pairs revocation with words such as parole and contract.
normal.cn: 法律英语里 revocation 常与 parole、contract 这样的词搭配。

abstract.en: See an official stamp being lifted off a document.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚公章从文件上被拿开。

abstract.en: Imagine a driver handed back his keys with a red notice.
abstract.cn: 想象司机把钥匙交回去，同时收到一张红色通知。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled backwards, reeling a boat in.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子往回拉，把船收回来。

examples.en: The committee voted for the revocation of the planning permission.
examples.cn: 委员会投票决定撤销该规划许可。

examples.en: Any breach of the rules may result in the revocation of your membership.
examples.cn: 任何违反规定的行为都可能导致会员资格被撤销。

examples.en: He faced the revocation of his passport after the investigation.
examples.cn: 调查之后，他面临护照被吊销的处境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞沃凯申」——「瑞」气到头，把人「叫」回来把证件收回，就是撤销；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（往回）+ vocare（呼叫）→ revocare（叫回来）→ revocatio（召回；撤销）→ 古法语 revocation → 英语 revocation，核心义「把已给出的东西收回」。

sensesIntro.en: Revocation starts with a right being called back, extends to cancelling a licence or agreement, to repealing a law, to withdrawing a promise, and finally to a technical annulment in law.
sensesIntro.cn: revocation 从「收回已授予的权利」讲起，再延伸到吊销许可证、废除法律、撤回承诺，最后收窄到法律上的专门废止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed permission being pulled back and locked away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一纸签好的许可被收回，重新锁进抽屉。

branches.en: A granted right is called back by the granter.
branches.cn: 授予的权利被授予者收回。

branches.en: Licences and agreements are cancelled by official order.
branches.cn: 许可证与协议被官方命令取消。

branches.en: Laws and rulings are repealed or withdrawn.
branches.cn: 法律与裁决被废除或撤回。

branches.en: A spoken promise and an agent act can both be called back.
branches.cn: 口头承诺与代理行为都能被「叫回」作废。

branches.en: Both a permit and a regulation lose force once revoked.
branches.cn: 许可证与法规一旦被撤销就同时失去效力。

intro.en: Revocation is re- plus voc plus -ation, the same calling pattern found in evoke, provoke, and convoke.
intro.cn: revocation 由 re- 加 voc 再加 -ation 组成，这一「呼叫」模式同样见于 evoke、provoke 与 convoke。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare means to call and vox means voice, the source of the whole voc family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare 意为呼叫，vox 意为嗓音，是整个 voc 词族的来源。

items.example: The prefix re- points the action backwards.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把动作指向回去。

items.example: Vocare is the calling root of revocation.
items.exampleCN: vocare 是 revocation 的「呼叫」词根。

items.example: Vox gave English word voice.
items.exampleCN: vox 派生出了英语的 voice。

items.example: Revocare gives the core sense of the English word.
items.exampleCN: revocare 给出了这个词的核心义。

items.example: Revocatio is the direct ancestor of the noun.
items.exampleCN: revocatio 是这个名词的直接祖先。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms revocation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 revocation。

items.example: Revoke is the verb behind the noun.

items.example: A revocable offer can still be withdrawn.
items.exampleCN: 可撤销的要约仍可被撤回。

items.example: The prefix ir- before r- marks a negation.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 在 r 前表示否定。

items.example: An irrevocable letter of credit cannot be recalled.

definition_zh: 彻底改变；使发生根本性变革；使革命化
definition_en: to change something so completely that a new order or stage replaces the old one
core_image: 一只轮子整圈翻转，原来的上下全对调过来
scene: 实验室里新到的机器，把整整一辈人做手术的方式都换了样。New imaging tools have revolutionised the way surgeons plan an operation.
sceneCN: 这里 revolutionise 是「彻底改变」（第 1 个义项：使某事物的根本样貌完全改变）；句意：新的成像工具有彻底改变了外科医生规划手术的方式。

pos.zh: 彻底改变；使发生根本变化；使革命化

collocations.zh: 使一个行业发生根本变革
使医疗护理发生革命性变化
彻底改变我们对……的理解

senses.title: To change something completely
senses.titleCN: 彻底改变；使发生根本性变化
senses.definition: to change a thing, system, or practice so completely that it is no longer what it was
senses.definitionCN: 使事物的性质、制度或做法彻底改变，不再有原来的样子
senses.example: The internet has revolutionised the way people shop.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网彻底改变了人们的购物方式。
senses.why: The Latin stem means a rolling over, and a body that rolls over comes to rest upside down, so the verb pictures a complete turnabout.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干本义是「翻滚」，翻过一整圈的东西会以倒过来的姿态停下，所以这个词画出的是一次彻底翻转。

senses.title: To overturn a government or order
senses.definition: to overthrow a political or social order and bring a new one into being
senses.definitionCN: 推翻政治或社会旧秩序，建立新的秩序
senses.example: Printing revolutionised the spread of ideas across Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术彻底改变了思想在欧洲传播的方式。
senses.why: When a whole order turns over, the people inside it become the agents of a revolution, so the verb takes on the political sense of the noun it was built from.
senses.whyCN: 当整套秩序被翻过来时，身处其中的人就成了革命的推动者，于是动词承接了名词的革命含义。

senses.title: To transform a field or industry
senses.titleCN: 使行业发生革命性变革
senses.definition: to transform an industry, discipline, or market by introducing something decisively new
senses.definitionCN: 通过引入决定性的新事物而使某个行业、学科或市场发生转变
senses.example: Cheap flights revolutionised the travel industry.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价航班让旅游业发生了革命性变革。
senses.why: A turn that reaches a whole field becomes a breakthrough that resets its rules, so news writers speak of an industry being revolutionised.
senses.whyCN: 翻转波及整个领域时，就成了重设规则式的突破，所以新闻里常说某个行业被彻底改变。

senses.title: To change how people think
senses.titleCN: 改变观念；使思想发生转变
senses.definition: to alter people habits of thought or their basic assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 改变人们习以为常的想法或基本的假定
senses.example: Studies of the brain have revolutionised our ideas about learning.
senses.exampleCN: 对大脑的研究彻底改变了我们对学习的看法。
senses.why: Ideas can roll over too, which is why the word is used for shifts in understanding rather than only for machines or laws.
senses.whyCN: 观念同样可以翻跟头，所以这个词不只用来说机器或法律，也用来说认知上的转向。

senses.title: To remake everyday tools
senses.titleCN: 使日常器物与生活方式彻底改观
senses.definition: to remake an ordinary object or routine so thoroughly that the old version feels obsolete
senses.definitionCN: 把普通的器物或日常习惯改造得面目全非，使旧版本显得过时
senses.example: The smartphone revolutionised how we take photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 智能手机彻底改变了我们拍照的方式。
senses.why: The image starts with a single turning object, so a small handheld tool can carry the same force as a political upheaval.
senses.whyCN: 意象起点只是一个转动的物件，所以一件掌上小工具也能像政治剧变一样带有翻转之力。

intro.en: Revolutionise comes from revolution, from Latin revolutio, a rolling back, built on volvere, to roll.
intro.cn: revolutionise 来自 revolution，源于拉丁语 revolutio（向后滚动、回转），词根是 volvere（滚动）。

items.en: Volvere means to roll or to turn around.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚动、转动。

items.en: Revolutio means a rolling back or a turning around.
items.cn: revolutio 意为向后滚动、回转。

items.en: Revolution, meaning a turning or a course of time, enters English and later names political upheaval.
items.cn: revolution 以「旋转、时序更替」之义进入英语，后来才用来指政治剧变。

items.en: Revolutionary and related forms spread as the word becomes political.
items.cn: 随着词义政治化，revolutionary 等相关形式流行起来。

items.en: The verb revolutionise appears, with the British spelling and the regular -ise ending.
items.cn: 动词 revolutionise 出现，采用英式拼写与常规的 -ise 词尾。

items.en: Today revolutionise covers technology, medicine, and thought as well as politics.
items.cn: 今天 revolutionise 除了政治，也覆盖技术、医学与思想。

note.en: Revolutionise belongs to the rolling root of volvere, and it stands beside change words that differ mainly in force.
note.cn: revolutionise 属于表示「滚动」的 volvere 词根，它与各类「改变」词相邻，区别主要在力度上。

normalIntro.cn: revolutionise 是在名词 revolution 后加动词词尾 -ise，政治名词由此变成了动作。

normal.en: The verb is built on revolution by the regular -ise ending.
normal.cn: 这个动词由 revolution 加常规词尾 -ise 构成。

normal.en: British English writes -ise, while American English writes -ize.
normal.cn: 英式拼写用 -ise，美式拼写用 -ize。

normal.en: The past participle revolutionised often describes a changed industry.
normal.cn: 过去分词 revolutionised 常用来形容被彻底改变的行业。

normal.en: Compare revolution, a noun, and revolutionary, an adjective.
normal.cn: 对比名词 revolution 与形容词 revolutionary。

normal.en: The base verb revolved joins the same volvere root.
normal.cn: 动词 revolved 与它共享 volvere 词根。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy wheel that turns all the way over and lands upside down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的轮子整个翻转过来，倒着落地。

abstract.en: Imagine an old workshop where every machine is suddenly replaced overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一间老工坊，一夜之间所有机器都换了新样。

abstract.en: Think of a globe spun by a finger until a different side faces you.
abstract.cn: 想象用手指转动地球仪，直到另一面朝向自己。

examples.en: The printing press revolutionised how knowledge reached ordinary readers.
examples.cn: 印刷机彻底改变了知识抵达普通读者的方式。

examples.en: Railways revolutionised trade in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 铁路在十九世纪使贸易发生了根本变化。

examples.en: This single invention has revolutionised surgical care around the world.
examples.cn: 这一项发明让全世界的外科医疗发生了革命性变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞沃路神」——一只轮子沿着「瑞沃路」翻了个大跟头，事物便被彻底改变；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（滚动）→ re-（向后）+ volvere 构成 revolvere（滚回、转回）→ 拉丁语 revolutio（回转；巨变）→ 古法语 revolution → 英语 revolution（革命）→ 加 -ise 成 revolutionise，核心义「整圈翻转、面目全非」。

sensesIntro.en: Revolutionise starts with a thing completely turned over, widens to a political order overthrown, then to an industry, a set of ideas, and finally to everyday tools.
sensesIntro.cn: revolutionise 先从某物被整圈翻转讲起，扩展到被推翻的政治秩序，再延伸到行业、观念，最后落回到日常器物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel that turns all the way over, so what was up is now down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只轮子整个翻转过去，原来朝上的现在朝下。

branches.en: A thing changed beyond recognition is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 事物被改得面目全非，是日常义项。

branches.en: A political order overthrown is the historical sense.
branches.cn: 旧制度被推翻，是历史义项。

branches.en: An industry reset by a breakthrough is the market sense.
branches.cn: 行业被突破重设，是市场义项。

branches.en: A shift in how people think is the intellectual sense.
branches.cn: 人们想法的转向，是认知义项。

branches.en: Both an industry and a handheld tool can be turned over by one new idea.
branches.cn: 一个行业与一件掌上工具，都可能因一个新想法被翻个底朝天。

definition_en: to move in a circle around a centre, or to have something as its central point
core_image: 一颗行星沿轨道一圈圈绕着恒星转
scene: 课堂讨论里每个人都在发言，但所有问题最后都绕回同一个核心。The whole debate revolved around one question: who should pay for the new bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 revolve 是「以……为中心展开」（第 2 个义项：事情围绕某个核心话题或人物运转）；句意：整场辩论都围绕一个问题展开：新桥该由谁来出钱。

pos.zh: 旋转；环绕；围绕……转
反复思考；仔细考虑

senses.title: To turn in a circle
senses.definition: to move in a circle around a centre or an axis
senses.definitionCN: 绕中心或轴线呈圆周运动
senses.example: The earth revolves on its own axis.
senses.exampleCN: 地球绕自身的轴旋转。
senses.why: Latin revolvere means to roll back, so a body that rolls all the way round returns again and again to its starting point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 revolvere 意为滚回，整圈滚动的东西会一遍遍回到起点，这正是旋转的样子。

senses.title: To have something as a centre
senses.definition: to be centred on a particular thing, person, or question
senses.definitionCN: 以某个事物、人物或问题为中心
senses.example: Her whole life revolved around her children.
senses.exampleCN: 她的全部生活都围绕着孩子。
senses.why: If everything circles one point, attention and care can circle a person in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 如果万物都绕着一个点转，那么注意与牵挂也能绕着一个人转，这就是「以……为中心」。

senses.title: To orbit a larger body
senses.definition: to travel in a fixed orbit around a planet or star
senses.definitionCN: 沿固定轨道绕行星或恒星运行
senses.example: The planets revolve around the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 行星围绕太阳运行。
senses.why: The same circling motion, viewed from outside, becomes an orbit around a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 同样的圆周运动，换个视角从外部看，就成了绕大天体运行的轨道。

senses.title: To turn ideas over in the mind
senses.definition: to consider a problem over and over in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心里一遍又一遍地考虑某个问题
senses.example: He revolved the offer in his mind for days.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个提议在心里盘算了好几天。
senses.why: A thought that keeps coming back to the same point is doing what a wheel does, so the verb moves from the body to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 一个念头不断回到同一点，就像轮子在转，于是这个词从身体动作转到心理活动。

senses.title: To make a part turn round
senses.definition: to turn a knob, handle, or other part round and round
senses.definitionCN: 把旋钮、把手或其他部件一圈圈转动
senses.example: She revolved the dial until the light came on.
senses.exampleCN: 她把旋钮一直转，直到灯亮起来。
senses.why: The object sense of the verb appears when a hand makes a small wheel turn on its centre.
senses.whyCN: 当手让一个小轮绕轴转动时，就出现了这个词的及物用法。

intro.en: Revolve comes from Latin revolvere, to roll back, made of re- and volvere, to roll.
intro.cn: revolve 来自拉丁语 revolvere（滚回），由前缀 re- 与 volvere（滚动）组成。

items.en: The reconstructed root wel- means to turn or to wind, according to standard reconstructions.
items.cn: 按通行的重构，原始印欧语词根 wel- 意为转动、缠绕。

items.en: Volvere means to roll or to turn over.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚动、翻动。

items.en: Revolvere means to roll back or to turn round again.
items.cn: revolvere 意为滚回、再转一圈。

items.en: Revolutio names a rolling back or a turn, first in the calendar and the sky.
items.cn: revolutio 指回转、循环，最早用于历法与天象。

items.en: Revolve enters English through Latin and French, meaning to turn or to roll round.
items.cn: revolve 经拉丁语与法语进入中古英语，意为转动、滚动。

items.en: Modern English extends the word from planets to the mind and to daily routines.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从行星延伸到心智与日常生活。

note.en: Revolve belongs to the rolling root of volvere, and it stands beside turn words that differ mainly in shape and force.
note.cn: revolve 属于表示「滚动」的 volvere 词根，它与各类「转动」词相邻，区别主要在轨迹与力度上。

entries.definitionCN: 绕轴旋转

entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转

normalIntro.en: Revolve is Latin re- plus volvere, a rolling back to the start point, and it keeps company with revolution, revolver, and evolve.
normalIntro.cn: revolve 是拉丁语 re- 加 volvere（滚回起点），与 revolution、revolver、evolve 同族。

normal.en: Revolve around is the most common pattern, used for planets and for topics.
normal.cn: revolve around 是最常见的搭配，既用于行星也用于话题。

normal.en: The revolving door turns and brings everyone back to where they started.
normal.cn: revolving door 转一圈又把人带回原处，正合「滚回」之义。

normal.en: The noun revolution keeps the same turning idea in politics.
normal.cn: 名词 revolution 在政治里保留着同样的转动之意。

normal.en: Evolve, same root, rolls a thing gradually out into a new form.
normal.cn: 同根的 evolve 是慢慢把事物「滚」成新形态。

normal.en: The double l in revolved but the single l in revolving follow English spelling rules of doubling.
normal.cn: revolved 双写 l，revolving 不双写，这是英语拼写规则在起作用。

abstract.en: Picture a moon that never stops circling a dark planet.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗月亮永不停歇地绕着一颗暗色行星转。

abstract.en: Imagine a child spinning a globe while a finger picks out one country.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子转动地球仪，一根手指点住某个国家。

abstract.en: Think of a record on a player, always returning to the same first groove.
abstract.cn: 想象唱片在唱机上转，每次都回到最初那道纹路。

examples.en: The wheels revolved slowly in the mud.
examples.cn: 车轮在泥里缓慢地转动。

examples.en: Their plans revolve around finding affordable housing.
examples.cn: 他们的计划都以找到可负担的住房为核心。

examples.en: For weeks she revolved the same question in her mind.
examples.cn: 好几个星期，她心里反复琢磨着同一个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞沃轮」——一轮子绕着中心转个不停，所以 revolve 是旋转、绕转；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（滚动）→ re-（向后、再）+ volvere 构成 revolvere（滚回、再转一圈）→ 拉丁语 revolutio（回转；循环）→ 古法语 → 中古英语 revolve，核心义「绕圈回转」。

sensesIntro.en: Revolve begins with a body turning on its centre, widens to anything centred on a person or topic, becomes an orbit, turns inward to the mind, and finally works on a knob.
sensesIntro.cn: revolve 从物体绕轴转起，扩展到以人或话题为中心，再到天体公转，然后转向内心的盘算，最后落在转动物件上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a planet that keeps circling the same star.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗行星不停地绕着同一颗恒星转。

branches.en: A body turning on its axis is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 物体绕轴转动，是物理义项。

branches.en: Being centred on a person or issue is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 以人或议题为中心，是引申义项。

branches.en: Travelling round a larger body is the astronomical sense.
branches.cn: 绕大天体运行，是天文学义项。

branches.en: Turning a problem over in the mind is the inner sense.
branches.cn: 在脑中反复琢磨问题，是内心义项。

branches.en: A dial and a planet both turn round one centre.
branches.cn: 旋钮与行星都绕同一个中心转动。

intro.cn: revolve 是带前缀的拉丁语「滚动」动词，英语在同一词干上构成 revolver、revolution 与 revolve around。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere means to roll, and revolvere means to roll back or turn again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为滚动，revolvere 意为滚回、再转。

items.example: Volvere gives the rolling core.
items.exampleCN: volvere 给出滚动的核心义。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the return to the start.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加上回到起点的意思。

items.example: Revolvere is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: revolvere 是直接来源。

items.example: Revolutio leads to the noun revolution.
items.exampleCN: revolutio 引出名词 revolution。

items.meaningCN: 做某事的物或人的词尾

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 revolver。

items.example: The ending -ing gives revolving.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 revolving。

items.example: Evolution rolls out of the same root.
items.exampleCN: evolution 出自同一词根。

items.example: Revolt comes through French, not from volvere.
