definition_zh: 犀牛；犀科动物
definition_en: a large heavy African or Asian animal with thick grey skin and one or two horns on its nose
core_image: 一头灰皮厚甲的大兽，鼻尖竖着一只硬角
scene: 草原尽头，一头灰皮大兽低着头沿河慢慢走，鼻尖的角在夕光里发亮。At dusk a rhinoceros grazed quietly beside the river, its horn catching the last light.
sceneCN: 这里 rhinoceros 是「犀牛」（第 1 个义项：鼻端生有一只或两只角的厚皮大型哺乳动物）；句意：黄昏时分，一头犀牛在河边安静地吃草，鼻上的角映着最后一点天光。

pos.zh: 犀牛；犀科动物

derivatives.zh: 由 rhinoceros 前四个字母截短而成，义为「犀牛」；另指「鼻子」
rhinoceros 的规则复数，义为「多头犀牛」
两个名词合成的固定搭配，义为「犀角；犀牛角」
合成词，义为「犀甲虫」，因头上长角而得名

senses.title: The animal itself
senses.definition: a huge plant-eating mammal with thick folded skin and a horn or two on the nose
senses.definitionCN: 一种大型植食性哺乳动物，皮厚起褶，鼻端有一只或两只角
senses.example: A rhinoceros can weigh more than two tonnes.
senses.exampleCN: 一头犀牛的体重可以超过两吨。
senses.why: Greek rhino- means nose and keras means horn, so the name is simply the nose-horned one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 rhino- 意为鼻子，keras 意为角，这个名字直译就是「鼻子上长角的那只」。

senses.title: One of the species
senses.titleCN: 犀科物种；犀牛这一物种
senses.definition: any of several living species of rhinoceros, from Africa or Asia
senses.definitionCN: 非洲或亚洲现存的某一种犀牛物种
senses.example: The black rhinoceros is now critically endangered.
senses.exampleCN: 黑犀目前处于极危状态。
senses.why: Once the creature had a name, the same word was used to point at whole species that share the nose horn.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物有了名字之后，同一个词也被用来指共享鼻角的整个物种。

senses.title: Its horn and skin as goods
senses.titleCN: 犀角；犀皮（供制作或交易的材料）
senses.definition: the horn or the hide of the animal as a traded or worked material
senses.definitionCN: 作为交易或加工原料的犀牛角或犀牛皮
senses.example: Trading in rhinoceros horn is banned in most countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数国家，犀角交易是被禁止的。
senses.why: People hunted the creature mainly for the horn and the hide, so the animal name moved to the parts taken from it.
senses.whyCN: 人们猎杀这种动物主要图它的角与皮，于是动物名也转指从它身上取下的部件。

senses.title: A figure of the huge and armour-plated
senses.titleCN: 犀牛般笨重厚甲的形象
senses.definition: used in writing for something wonderfully heavy, armoured, or unshakeably stubborn
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中用来形容极其笨重、披着厚甲或固执得推不动的形象
senses.example: The old tank rolled forward like a rhinoceros.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆老坦克像犀牛一样向前碾去。
senses.why: The thick folded skin looks like plate armour, so writers borrow the animal for anything bulky and hard to stop.
senses.whyCN: 它厚而起褶的皮像板甲，于是作家借这种动物来形容笨重又难以阻挡的东西。

senses.title: The nose horn as a general term
senses.titleCN: 犀角状隆起；鼻部的角状结构
senses.definition: a horn-like structure or bump on the nose of other creatures or objects
senses.definitionCN: 其他生物或物件鼻部类似角的突起结构
senses.example: The beetle carries a small rhinoceros-like horn.
senses.exampleCN: 这种甲虫长着一只小犀牛角似的东西。
senses.why: The Greek name describes a shape, not only an animal, so its parts can be borrowed for horns and bumps elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名字描述的是一种形状而不只是动物，所以它的部件也能借来描述别处的角与突起。

intro.en: Rhinoceros is Greek, rhino-prefix meaning nose plus keras meaning horn, borrowed into Latin and then English.
intro.cn: rhinoceros 是希腊语，rhino- 意为鼻子，keras 意为角，经拉丁语借入英语。

items.en: Rhinokeros is a compound of rhinos, nose, and keras, horn.
items.cn: 希腊语 rhinokeros 是 rhinos（鼻子）与 keras（角）的合成词。

items.en: Writers such as Herodotus describe a horned beast of Africa under this name.
items.cn: 希罗多德等作家用这个名字描写非洲的有角巨兽。

items.en: Latin borrows the word as rhinoceros, keeping the Greek spelling.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个词作 rhinoceros，并保留希腊语拼写。

items.en: The word first appears in English in accounts of travel and natural history.
items.cn: 这个词在英语中最早见于游记与自然史著作。

items.en: As specimens reach Europe, rhinoceros settles as the ordinary zoological name.
items.cn: 随着标本传入欧洲，rhinoceros 固定为通用的动物学名称。

items.en: Modern English also uses the shortened rhino and the ordinary plural rhinoceroses.
items.cn: 现代英语还用缩写 rhino 与常规复数 rhinoceroses。

note.en: Rhinoceros carries the Greek nose-and-horn compound, and it stands beside heavy African and Asian mammal words.
note.cn: rhinoceros 带着希腊语「鼻加角」的合成结构，它与各类笨重的非洲、亚洲哺乳动物词相邻。

entries.definition: the informal short name for a rhinoceros
entries.definitionCN: 犀牛的口语简称

entries.definition: surgery to reshape the nose
entries.definitionCN: 鼻部整形手术；同样含希腊语「鼻」前缀

entries.definition: a large river-dwelling African mammal
entries.definitionCN: 河马；同为希腊语大词，此处只是结构相近

entries.definition: a very large grey animal with a long trunk
entries.definitionCN: 大象

entries.definition: a large heavy wild ox
entries.definitionCN: 水牛；野牛

entries.definition: a wild African pig with tusks
entries.definitionCN: 疣猪

normalIntro.en: Rhinoceros is a Greek description cut in two: rhino- for the nose and -ceros for the horn.
normalIntro.cn: rhinoceros 是一句被切成两半的希腊语描述：rhino- 是鼻子，-ceros 是角。

normal.en: The prefix rhino- means nose, so rhinoplasty also points at the nose.
normal.cn: 前缀 rhino- 意为鼻子，所以 rhinoplasty 也指向鼻部。

normal.en: The ending -ceros is close to Greek keras, a horn.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ceros 与希腊语 keras（角）相近。

normal.en: The plural is usually rhinoceroses, though rhinoceros is also accepted.
normal.cn: 复数通常写 rhinoceroses，写成 rhinoceros 也通用。

normal.en: The everyday shortened form is rhino.
normal.cn: 日常缩略说法是 rhino。

normal.en: Hippo in hippopotamus means horse and potamos means river.
normal.cn: hippopotamus 里的 hippo 意为马，potamos 意为河。

abstract.en: Picture a tank of folded grey plates, with one horn on the nose.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆披着灰色褶皱甲片、鼻头上竖着一只角的战车。

abstract.en: Imagine two birds named for horns perched on a grey back, pecking ticks.
abstract.cn: 想象两只以角得名的鸟停在灰色背上啄食蜱虫。

abstract.en: Think of a huge shadow rolling through tall grass at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象夕阳下，一团巨大的影子在高草里缓缓移动。

examples.en: The rhinoceros stood motionless beside the waterhole.
examples.cn: 那头犀牛在水坑边一动不动地站着。

examples.en: Poachers hunt rhinoceroses for their horns.
examples.cn: 偷猎者为了犀角而猎杀犀牛。

examples.en: Several species of rhinoceros are now critically endangered.
examples.cn: 已有好几种犀牛处于极危状态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来拿犀角」——偷猎者「来拿」犀牛的角，所以 rhinoceros 是犀牛；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 rhinos（鼻子）+ keras（角）→ 希腊语 rhinokeros → 拉丁语 rhinoceros（保留希腊拼写）→ 英语 rhinoceros，核心义「鼻子上长角的大兽」；缩略形式为 rhino。

sensesIntro.en: Rhinoceros names the animal first, then its species, then the horn and hide traded as goods, then a figure of bulk and armour, and finally any horn-like bump.
sensesIntro.cn: rhinoceros 先指这种动物本身，再指它的物种，随后指被交易的角与皮，然后是笨重厚甲的形象，最后指任何角状突起。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a huge grey beast with a hard horn on its nose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头灰皮巨兽，鼻端竖着一只硬角。

branches.en: The name of the animal is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 指这种动物本身，是字面义项。

branches.en: Naming one of the species is the scientific sense.
branches.cn: 指某个物种，是科学义项。

branches.en: The horn and hide as goods is the trade sense.
branches.cn: 角与皮作为商品，是贸易义项。

branches.en: A bulky armoured figure is the literary sense.
branches.cn: 笨重厚甲的形象，是文学义项。

branches.en: Both the beast and other creatures are named for a horn on the nose.
branches.cn: 这头巨兽与其他生物都以鼻上的角得名。

intro.en: Rhinoceros is an old Greek compound, with the nose prefix rhino- and the horn stem -ceros, joined in English by rhino and rhinoplasty.
intro.cn: rhinoceros 是古老的希腊语合成词，由表示鼻子的 rhino- 与表示角的 -ceros 组成，英语同族有 rhino 与 rhinoplasty。

latinIntro.en: The word reaches English through Latin rhinoceros, which simply copied the Greek compound.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经拉丁语 rhinoceros 传入英语，而拉丁语只是照搬了希腊语合成词。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 rhino- 见于 rhinoplasty。

items.example: The stem -ceros marks the horn.
items.exampleCN: 词干 -ceros 标示角。

items.example: Rhinokeros is the original compound.

items.example: Latin keeps the word almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语几乎原样保留了这个词。

items.example: Rhinoplasty shares the nose prefix.
items.exampleCN: rhinoplasty 共享「鼻」前缀。

items.example: Scientific names use -ceros for horned animals.
items.exampleCN: 科学命名用 -ceros 表示有角的动物。

items.example: Rhino is the everyday short form.
items.exampleCN: rhino 是日常简称。

definition_zh: 装配；配备；（船）装配桅帆索具；钻塔；钻井平台；成套装置；临时拼凑的服装；不正当手段操纵
definition_en: to fit or equip something with sails, gear, or equipment, or to set up something hastily; also the equipment, ship, platform, or piece of clothing that results, or a dishonest arrangement
core_image: 渔民把钓线、浮标和小钩一件件系上，把光秃的船桅绑成一整套齐备的索具
scene: 老渔夫把一卷新绳、几只浮标和一套小钩摊在甲板上，一样样往船桅上系。The crew spent the morning getting ready to rig the boat for a month at sea.
sceneCN: 这里 rig 是「给船只装配桅帆与索具」（第 1 个义项：给船只装上桅、帆、绳索等装备）；句意为船员们用了一上午准备，要给这条船配齐一整套索具，好在海上待一个月。画面里有船桅、缠成卷的绳索、浮标和一只只小钩。

pos.zh: 装配；配备；（船）装配桅帆索具；临时拼凑搭起；用不正当手段操纵
成套装置；钻塔；钻井平台；索具；临时拼凑的服装；一套套路或花招

derivatives.zh: 由动词 rig 加 -ing 构成，义为「船的索具；选举舞弊等操纵行为」
由动词 rig 加 -er 构成，义为「装配工；索具工；（跳伞的）叠伞员」
由动词 rig 的过去分词转化而来，义为「被操纵的；装好索具的」
与 rig 共享「起重机、钻塔」的词场，义为「起重机；井架」，词源不同

senses.title: To fit a ship with masts and ropes
senses.definition: to fit a ship with its sails, ropes, masts, and other sailing gear
senses.definitionCN: 给船只装上帆、绳索、桅杆等航行装备
senses.example: Sailors rigged the vessel before the tide turned.
senses.exampleCN: 赶在退潮之前，水手们给船装好了索具。
senses.why: The nautical rigging is the oldest recorded use, so rig begins as the act of dressing a bare hull in rope and canvas.
senses.whyCN: 航海索具是这个词最古老的有记录用法，所以 rig 最开始的画面是给光秃的船身披上绳索与帆布。

senses.title: To equip or set up for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 为某种用途配备或装置
senses.definition: to fit out a person, room, vehicle, or device with the things needed for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某人、房间、车辆或设备配备完成某项用途所需的物品
senses.example: Engineers rigged the lab with extra sensors for the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师给实验室加装了额外的传感器做试验。
senses.why: From a ship the same act spreads to any object: you dress a room or a machine in what it needs.
senses.whyCN: 从船只扩展到任何对象：给房间或机器穿上它所需要的「装备」，动作的本质并没有变。

senses.title: To set up hastily or temporarily
senses.definition: to put together or set up something quickly and often temporarily, usually the phrase rig up
senses.definitionCN: 快速、往往是临时地搭起或组装某物，常用短语 rig up
senses.example: They rigged up a shelter from a plastic sheet and two poles.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一块塑料布和两根杆子临时搭了个棚子。
senses.why: Improvised gear is still gear: when there is no time to rig properly, anything can be rigged quickly.
senses.whyCN: 临时凑出来的装备仍然是装备：来不及正经装配时，任何东西都能被迅速拼起来，临时搭起正是装配义项在仓促情形下的变体。

senses.title: A drilling derrick or platform at sea
senses.definition: a tall steel tower used for drilling, often mounted on a platform at sea
senses.definitionCN: 用于钻井的高大钢架，常架设在海上的平台上
senses.example: The oil rig stands in deep water far from the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 那座石油钻井平台矗立在离海岸很远的海面上。
senses.why: A drilling tower is a permanent rig of steel, so the noun keeps the image of parts fitted together to do one job.
senses.whyCN: 钻井塔就是一整套钢铁的 rig，名词保留了「把部件装配起来完成一件事」的画面，所以钻塔与钻井平台都叫 rig。

senses.title: A set of fitted equipment
senses.definition: a set of equipment or apparatus fitted together for a particular activity or task
senses.definitionCN: 为某项活动或任务装配起来的一套设备或器械
senses.example: The sound crew carried a small rig of speakers and lights to the gig.
senses.exampleCN: 音效人员把一套小型的音箱与灯光设备带到演出现场。
senses.why: Once the act of fitting becomes a noun, the things fitted together are a rig in their own right.
senses.whyCN: 装配的动作一旦名词化，被装配在一起的那一堆东西本身就是一个 rig，这是装置义项的来源。

senses.title: A ship with its masts and sails
senses.definition: a ship together with its masts, sails, and ropes, or the way these are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 连同桅杆、帆与绳索在内的整条船，或这些装备的布置方式
senses.example: A square rig was still common in the age of sail.
senses.exampleCN: 在帆船时代，横帆帆装仍然十分常见。
senses.why: The noun returns to the sea and names the whole fitted vessel, or the arrangement a ship wears.
senses.whyCN: 名词又回到海上，指整条装备齐整的船，也指船身上那套「穿戴」的布置方式。

senses.title: An outfit or a set of clothes
senses.definition: an outfit or set of clothes, often ordinary, old-fashioned, or humorous
senses.definitionCN: 一套衣服或装束，常带寻常、过时或调侃的意味
senses.example: He arrived in his best rig for the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着自己最好的一身行头来面试。
senses.why: Clothes are the oldest thing people rig themselves out with, so the dress sense of the verb survives in a mocking noun.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是人最早「装备」自己的东西，所以动词里「穿戴」的意思残留在名词中，多用于带调侃的「行头」义。

senses.title: A dishonest manipulation
senses.definition: a dishonest or manipulative arrangement, especially in an election or a prize draw
senses.definitionCN: 不诚实的操纵安排，尤指选举或抽奖中的舞弊
senses.example: Spotting a rig in the ballot count, observers asked for a recount.
senses.exampleCN: 察觉到计票有舞弊，观察员们要求重新计票。
senses.why: Ropes and pulleys can move things unseen, so the same word covers a hidden set of strings pulled to fix an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 绳索与滑轮能暗中牵动东西，于是同一个词也指暗中牵线、把结果预定好的那一套手脚。

intro.en: Rig has two streams. One is the sea word for fitting a ship with sails and ropes; the other is the older English verb meaning to dress or equip, and the modern senses of gear, tower, and cheating grew from these.
intro.cn: rig 有两条来源。一条是表示「给船装配帆索」的海事词，另一条是更古老的英语动词「穿着、装备」；现代的装置、钻塔与舞弊义都从这两条线长出来。

items.en: The nautical verb is recorded in late sixteenth-century English and is often linked to Scandinavian rigga, to bind or wrap. The sources do not fully agree.
items.cn: 海事动词于十六世纪晚期见于英语记载，常被认为与斯堪的纳维亚语 rigga「绑、缠」有关；各家说法并不完全一致。

items.en: Old English wrigian meant to turn, twist, or move, and may lie behind the family of dress and equip senses. This link is uncertain.
items.cn: 古英语 wrigian 意为转动、扭动或移动，可能是「穿着、装备」这一组意思的来源；这一联系不确定。

items.en: The verb names fitting out a ship with masts, sails, and ropes, and rigging arrives as the noun for that equipment.
items.cn: 动词指给船装上桅、帆与绳索，名词 rigging 随之出现，指这套装备。

items.en: The noun extends to a ship together with its rig, then to any set of fitted equipment, and the verb covers temporary set-ups such as rig up a sail.
items.cn: 名词先扩展到连帆装在内的整条船，再扩展到任何成套设备；动词也用于临时搭建，如 rig up a sail。

items.en: Oil drilling gives rig its tower and platform senses, while rig also takes on many printers and editors, a set of type or plates set up for printing.
items.cn: 石油钻井给出钻塔与钻井平台的义项；同时 rig 也用于印刷行话，指排好的一套字模或印版。

items.en: The idea of a fitted arrangement turns crooked, so a rigged election or a rig on a market names a hidden manipulation.
items.cn: 「装好的一套安排」这一观念走向歪路，于是 rigged election 或市场中的 rig 指暗中操纵。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that share the rig shape or the drilling scene; the near-meaning group holds ordinary verbs for equipping, setting up, and rigging an outcome.
note.cn: 形近组收与 rig 拼写相似、或在钻井场景里相邻的词；近义组收普通的「装备、搭起、操纵」类动词。

entries.definition: Stiff and not able to bend, or strict and not willing to change. It only shares the first letters and comes from Latin rigere, to be stiff.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「僵硬的、死板的」；只是开头的拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 rigere「僵硬」。

entries.definition: The ropes, wires, and equipment used to support a ship mast or a piece of stage and camera gear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「船的索具；舞台与摄影的吊挂设备」，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A person who fits and adjusts ropes, cranes, or parachute lines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装配工；索具工；叠伞员」，由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A crane or the steel tower over an oil well; a neighbour in the drilling scene, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起重机、井架」，与 rig 同属钻井场景，词源不同。

entries.definition: To supply a person, place, or thing with the things needed for a purpose; the plain general word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装备、配备」，是最一般的说法，不带 rig 的海事与临时搭建色彩。

entries.definition: To put something in place and make it ready to use; close to the rig up sense.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「装置、搭起」，接近 rig up 的意思。

entries.definition: To control or influence something or someone cleverly, often unfairly; close to the cheating sense of rig.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「操纵、摆布」，常带不公正的意味，接近 rig 的舞弊义。

entries.definition: To plan or put things in order; neutral, while a rigged arrangement is dishonest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「安排、布置」，属中性词；而 rigged 的安排带有欺骗性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the sailing origin of rig and the fixed phrases it appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 rig 的航海来源，以及它今天固定出现的搭配。

normal.en: Rigging is the ropes and sails a sailor fits to a bare mast.
normal.cn: rigging 就是水手给光秃的船桅装上的那一整套绳索与帆。

normal.en: An oil rig is a steel tower rigged together for drilling; the same word for equipment and for a platform.
normal.cn: oil rig 是为钻井装配起来的钢塔；同一个词既指设备，也指平台。

normal.en: To rig up a tent is to set it up quickly with whatever is at hand.
normal.cn: rig up a tent 就是用手边的东西快速把帐篷搭起来。

normal.en: A rigged election has its result set up in advance, like ropes pulled behind a curtain.
normal.cn: rigged election 的结果早就被人预先安排好，就像幕后拉动的绳索。

normal.en: Compare equip and fit out: rig is the sea word that spread to drilling, clothes, and cheating.
normal.cn: 对比 equip 与 fit out：rig 原本是航海词，后来扩展到钻井、衣着与舞弊。

abstract.en: Picture a bare mast that slowly fills with ropes, pulleys, and canvas until nothing is missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根光秃的桅杆，绳索、滑轮与帆布一件件挂上去，直到一样不缺。

abstract.en: A steel platform stands on stilts in open sea, all its pipes plugged in and running.
abstract.cn: 一座钢制平台架在高桩上立在开阔海面，管线全部接好、运转起来。

abstract.en: Think of a puppet show: invisible strings move every figure, and the ending is already chosen.
abstract.cn: 想象一场提线木偶戏：看不见的线牵动每个木偶，结局早已定好。

examples.en: Crews were rigged out with waterproof jackets before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，船员们都配好了防水外套。

examples.en: Volunteers rigged up a makeshift stage on the village square.
examples.cn: 志愿者们在村广场上临时搭起了一个台子。

examples.en: Rescue teams used a crane on the rig to lift the injured crew.
examples.cn: 救援队用平台上的起重机吊起受伤的人员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞格」——瑞气满满，船家把格架、绳索一格格装好，装配齐备；这只是谐音拆词，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为航海动词 rig「给船装帆索」与斯堪的纳维亚语 rigga「绑、缠」有关，另有假说把它同古英语 wrigian「扭动」相联系，均属来源不确定；名词由动词派生，引申出钻塔、成套装置与舞弊义。

sensesIntro.en: Rig begins as dressing a ship in gear, spreads to any equipment fitted for a job, then to a steel tower, a set of clothes, and finally to an outcome that has been secretly set up.
sensesIntro.cn: rig 先是给船「穿戴」装备，再扩展到任何为某项工作配好的设备，然后是钢制钻塔、成套行头，最后指被人暗中安排好的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare mast is fitted with ropes, pulleys, and canvas until the whole set is ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根光秃的桅杆被装上绳索、滑轮与帆布，直到整套齐备可用。

branches.en: THE ACT: you fit out a ship, a room, or a machine with what it needs.
branches.cn: 动作线：给船、房间或机器配上所需的东西。

branches.en: THE THING: the gear once fitted becomes a rig, whether it is a platform, a device, or the ship itself.
branches.cn: 产物线：装好的东西本身就是一个 rig，无论是平台、装置还是整条船。

branches.en: THE STOPGAP: whatever is at hand can be rigged quickly, from a tent to a set of clothes.
branches.cn: 应急线：手边有什么都能快速配上，从帐篷到一身衣着。

branches.en: THE TRICK: ropes hidden behind the stage become the image of a secretly arranged result.
branches.cn: 歪用线：幕后看不见的绳索，成了暗中操控结果的意象。

branches.en: FROM SAILING: the same word names the gear and the hidden strings, so both the honest fit and the crooked fix wear it.
branches.cn: 海事根源：同一个词既指装好的索具，也指暗藏的线索，正当装配与歪门操纵共用这个词。

intro.en: Rig is a short native-style verb, and English builds rigging and rigger on it with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: rig 是一个短小的动词，英语用品后缀在它上面构成 rigging 与 rigger。

latinIntro.en: Rig has no clear Latin cousin; the Latin entries below are words for fitting out and rigging a ship that borrow its meaning.
latinIntro.cn: rig 没有明确的拉丁同源词；下面列出的拉丁语词是表示「装备、给船装索具」的近邻词，借的是意思而非词源。

items.meaning: to fit out or set up
items.example: Crews rigged the boat in a single afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 船员们一个下午就把船装配好了。

items.example: The suffix makes rigging, the gear fixed to a mast.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 rigging，指固定在桅杆上的索具。

items.example: The suffix makes rigger, a person who fits gear.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 rigger，指装配装备的人。

items.example: The suffix makes rigged, as in a rigged vote.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 rigged，如 rigged vote。

items.example: They rigged up a radio antenna at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在拂晓时临时架起了一根无线电天线。

items.example: To rig out a crew is to fit everyone fully.
items.exampleCN: rig out 给全体船员配齐装备。

items.example: Gear is the plain word for the things a rig holds.
items.exampleCN: gear 就是 rig 所装的那堆东西的普通说法。

items.example: Equip is the everyday cousin of rig.
items.exampleCN: equip 是 rig 的日常近义词。

items.example: Re- forms words that are often mistaken for rig words.
items.exampleCN: re- 构成的一些词常被误看作 rig 的同根词。

items.example: A derrick stands beside a rig at the field.
items.exampleCN: 油井场上，井架就立在钻井装置旁边。

latinEntries.example: Armare gave arm and armour in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: armare 在英语中产生 arm 与 armour。
instruere 产生 instrument 与 instruct。

definition_zh: 正直的；公正的；正当的；合乎道义的；（宗教）虔诚的；（习语）义愤填膺的
definition_en: morally right and free from guilt, showing a strong sense of justice, and sometimes used to describe proud anger or moral certainty
core_image: 一个人站得笔直，身前的天平滑向自己这一边，因为他所做的一切都合规矩
scene: 法官在结案前说，这次判决只凭法律与良心，不偏袒任何一方。The judge insisted on a righteous verdict, free of any favour or pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 righteous 是「公正的、合乎道义的」（第 2 个义项：符合公平与正义标准的）；句意为法官坚持要作出一个公正的判决，不受任何偏袒或压力影响。画面里有法官、天平和一张写满条文的纸。

pos.zh: 正直的；公正的；正当的；合乎道义的；虔诚的

collocations.zh: 义人；正直的人（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 由 righteous 加 -ness 构成，义为「正直；公正；义」（宗教中也指合乎神意的状态）
由 righteous 加 -ly 构成，义为「正直地；公正地」
由 righteous 加否定的 un- 构成，义为「不义的；不正当的」
由 self 与 righteous 复合而成，义为「自以为是的；自以为正当的」

senses.title: Moral uprightness in a person
senses.definition: acting in a morally correct way and following what is right, especially in a religious or ethical sense
senses.definitionCN: 行为符合道德与正道，尤用于宗教或伦理语境
senses.example: He was a righteous man who never broke a promise.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个正直的人，从不食言。
senses.why: Right here means the straight, correct way, so a righteous person is one who keeps to that straight path in moral life.
senses.whyCN: right 在这里表示「笔直的、正确的路」，所以 righteous 指在道德生活中始终走在正道上的人。

senses.title: Fair and just by moral standard
senses.definition: fair, just, and in line with moral law, often said of a cause, verdict, or decision
senses.definitionCN: 公平、正义且符合道德准则，常用来形容事业、判决或决定
senses.example: A righteous verdict must rest on evidence, not on power.
senses.exampleCN: 公正的判决必须以证据为依据，而不是以权力为依据。
senses.why: When the straight line of right is applied to actions and judgements rather than to people, it names anything that meets the standard of justice.
senses.whyCN: 当「right」这条直线被用来衡量行为与裁决而不是人时，它就指一切符合正义标准的事物。

senses.title: Pious or approved by a religious tradition
senses.definition: living according to the rules of a religious faith, or praised as good within a tradition
senses.definitionCN: 依照宗教信仰规范生活，或在某传统中被称许为善的
senses.example: Righteous living has long been a theme in religious teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 虔诚的生活长期以来都是宗教教导的主题。
senses.why: The ethical root passed into religious language, where moral uprightness also means obedience to divine law.
senses.whyCN: 伦理上的词根进入宗教语言，在那里「道德正直」同时意味着遵从神的律法。

senses.title: Anger felt as justified
senses.definition: describing anger or indignation that the person believes is justified, as in righteous anger
senses.definitionCN: 指当事人自认为正当的愤怒或愤慨，如 righteous anger
senses.example: Her righteous anger at the fraud spilled over into the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那桩欺诈的义愤延续到了会议之中。
senses.why: If a judgement is righteous, the anger that rises from it feels righteous too, and the word can mark a moral certainty that may be hard to argue with.
senses.whyCN: 既然判断是正当的，由它而生的愤怒也自认正当；这个词于是也能标记一种不易被说服的道德确定感。

senses.title: The righteous as a group
senses.titleCN: 义人；正直的人（集合用法）
senses.definition: used with the, the people who are judged to be good and just, as in a farewell to the righteous
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指被判定为善良与公正的那群人
senses.example: The prophet promised that the righteous would not be forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 那位先知应许义人不会被遗忘。
senses.why: An adjective that names a quality easily becomes a noun for all the people who have it, so the righteous means the whole upright group.
senses.whyCN: 一个表示品质的形容词很容易变成指「拥有这种品质的所有人」的名词，所以 the righteous 指整个正直的群体。

senses.title: Complacency dressed as virtue
senses.titleCN: 自以为是；自以为正当的假德行
senses.definition: used critically of people who are too sure of their own virtue and look down on others
senses.definitionCN: 带有批评意味，指过分自信于自身德行、看不起别人
senses.example: His righteous tone made every compromise sound like a sin.
senses.exampleCN: 他那副自以为是的腔调，让任何妥协听起来都像罪过。
senses.why: The very certainty that makes virtue feel righteous can harden into pride, which is why the word is often prefixed with self-.
senses.whyCN: 正是那种让德行显得「正当」的确定感，可能硬化成傲慢，所以这个词常被加上 self- 前缀使用。

intro.en: Righteous is an English formation: right, from Old English riht, plus the suffix -eous, taken from Latin through French. Together they mean having the quality of being right.
intro.cn: righteous 是英语自己造的词：right（源自古英语 riht）加借自拉丁语、经法语来的后缀 -eous，合起来就是「具有「正确」这一性质的」。

items.en: The ancestor of right is generally reconstructed as rekhtaz, meaning straight, upright, and in the correct way.
items.cn: 一般认为 right 的祖词可构拟为 rekhtaz，意为「笔直的、直立的、合乎规矩的」。

items.en: Riht means straight, true, just, and lawful, and it also names a legal right.
items.cn: riht 意为直的、真实的、公正的、合法的，同时也指法律上的权利。

items.en: An adjective suffix meaning full of or having the quality of, arriving in English through Old French -ous.
items.cn: 一个表示「充满、具有……性质」的形容词后缀，经古法语 -ous 进入英语。

items.en: Rihtwis appears in Old English for just or upright; the later form righteous reshapes it in imitation of words like bounteous.
items.cn: 古英语已有 rihtwis 表示「公正、正直」；后来的 righteous 一词仿照 bounteous 等词改写而成。

items.en: Righteousness becomes a central term of religious writing, and self-righteous appears soon after.
items.cn: righteousness 成为宗教写作中的核心术语，self-righteous 随后不久出现。

items.en: The word stays strong in moral and legal argument, while righteous anger and a self-righteous tone keep its critical edge alive.
items.cn: 这个词在道德与法律论证中始终有力，而 righteous anger 与自以为是的腔调则保留了它带批评意味的一面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on right or bent by the same -eous suffix; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for being good and fair.
note.cn: 形近组收以 right 为词根、或被同一个 -eous 后缀改形的词；近义组收表示「善良、公正」的形容词。

entries.definition: Correct, true, or just; the plain adjective that supplies the root of righteous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正确的、正当的」，是 righteous 的词根来源。

entries.definition: Legally correct and belonging to a person by law or justice, as in a rightful owner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合法的、理应归属的」，如 rightful owner。

entries.definition: Honest and respectable in character, or standing straight up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正直的、直立的」；与 righteous 同出「笔直」的词源，但更侧重为人可靠。

entries.definition: Generous and plentiful; an older word with the same -eous shape but a different stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「慷慨的、丰盛的」，与 righteous 同带 -eous 后缀，但词干不同。

entries.definition: A poetic word for beautiful; the -eous suffix again, with no link to right.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「美丽的」，属诗歌用语，同样带 -eous，但与 right 无关。

entries.definition: Having high moral standards and doing good; close to righteous but less tied to law or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有德行的、善良的」，接近 righteous，但较少依附法律或信仰。

entries.definition: Fair and acting according to what is right; the plain legal and moral word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「公正的、正义的」，是最常见的法律与道德用语。

entries.definition: Concerned with the rules of right and wrong behaviour; neutral and descriptive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「道德的」，属中性描述语。

entries.definition: Very good and holy in the way a saint is; stronger and more religious than righteous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「圣徒般的、圣洁的」，比 righteous 宗教色彩更浓、程度更强。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on the root right and the fixed phrases righteous words appear in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子建立在词根 right 与这个词固定出现的搭配之上。

normal.en: Right plus -eous: the same shape as bounteous and beauteous, meaning full of right.
normal.cn: right 加 -eous，与 bounteous、beauteous 同一构造，意为「充满 right」。

normal.en: Righteous action is the straight path of right carried into moral life.
normal.cn: righteous 的行为就是把「right」这条直线走成道德生活的路径。

normal.en: Righteous anger is anger that believes itself justified.
normal.cn: righteous anger 是自认为有正当理由的愤怒。

normal.en: The righteous, with the article, means upright people as a group.
normal.cn: the righteous 带定冠词，指作为一个群体的正直之人。

normal.en: Compare just and virtuous: just is the legal standard, virtuous the inner character, righteous both with a moral tone.
normal.cn: 对比 just 与 virtuous：just 偏法律标准，virtuous 偏内在品格，righteous 兼有两层且带道德语气。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing perfectly straight while a scale in front of them tilts toward their side.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站得笔直，身前的天平朝他这一侧倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a verdict read aloud in a quiet court, with nobody able to point to an unfair line.
abstract.cn: 想象在安静的法庭上宣判，没有人能指出哪一句不公。

abstract.en: Picture candles and plain clothes, the outward look of a life lived by a strict rule.
abstract.cn: 想象蜡烛与衣着朴素，那是一种循规蹈矩生活的外在模样。

examples.en: They took up arms in a righteous struggle for land rights.
examples.cn: 他们为争取土地权利而投入一场正义的斗争。

examples.en: The old teacher was known for his righteous refusal to accept gifts.
examples.cn: 那位老教师以正直著称，拒绝收受任何礼物。

examples.en: Righteous indignation filled the hall as the report was read.
examples.cn: 报告宣读时，大厅里充满了义愤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖车死」——赖着不肯走、死守规矩的，往往是正直的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 riht（直线、正确的、公正的，一般认为可上溯至原始日耳曼语重构形式 *rekhtaz「笔直」）+ 形容词后缀 -eous（经古法语 -ous 来自拉丁语 -osus「充满……的」）→ 中古英语 righteous，核心义「合乎正道的」。

sensesIntro.en: Righteous applies the straight line of right to a person, to a judgement, to faith, to anger, to a whole group, and finally to the pride that can grow out of virtue.
sensesIntro.cn: righteous 把「right」这条直线分别用到了人、裁决、信仰、愤怒、群体，最后还有可能从德行里长出的傲慢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stands perfectly straight while a scale in front of them tilts toward their side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站得笔直，身前的天平朝他这一侧倾斜。

branches.en: THE PERSON: to be righteous is to walk the straight moral path without turning.
branches.cn: 人线：righteous 就是走一条笔直道德路，不走岔。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: the same line judges a verdict or a creed as fair and approved.
branches.cn: 标准线：同一条直线用来判断裁决或教义是否公正、是否被认可。

branches.en: THE FEELING: anger that believes in its own justice carries the word.
branches.cn: 情绪线：自认为正义的愤怒也带上这个词。

branches.en: THE GROUP: all who keep the line become the righteous as a whole.
branches.cn: 群体线：所有守线的人合起来就是 the righteous。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: the certainty of being right, which passes from virtue into pride, is named self-righteous.
branches.cn: 阴影线：那种「我肯定是对的」的确定感会从德行滑向傲慢，就是 self-righteous。

intro.en: Righteous is a native root wearing a borrowed suffix: right supplies the meaning, and -eous shapes the adjective.
intro.cn: righteous 是「本土词根 + 借来的后缀」：right 提供含义，-eous 把它塑成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Right comes from Old English rather than Latin, so the Latin entries below are words for right and justice that sit in the same meaning field.
latinIntro.cn: right 来自古英语而非拉丁语，所以下面列出的拉丁语词是表示「正当、公正」的同类近邻词，只借意思不借词源。

items.example: The root right carries the meaning of righteous.
items.exampleCN: 词根 right 承载 righteous 的含义。

items.example: The suffix -eous forms righteous, bounteous, and beauteous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eous 构成 righteous、bounteous 与 beauteous。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms righteousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 righteousness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms righteously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 righteously。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unrighteous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unrighteous。

items.example: The prefix self- forms self-righteous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 self- 构成 self-righteous。

items.example: Rightly is the simple adverb beside righteously.
items.exampleCN: rightly 是与 righteously 并列的简单副词。

items.example: Rightful uses -ful where righteous uses -eous.
items.exampleCN: rightful 用 -ful，而 righteous 用 -eous。

items.example: Upright shares the straight image of right.
items.exampleCN: upright 共享 right 的「笔直」意象。

latinEntries.example: Rectus is the Latin cousin of the straight sense of right.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rectus 与 right 的「直」义同属一支古老词源。

latinEntries.example: Justus gave justice and just in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: justus 在英语中产生 justice 与 just。

latinEntries.example: Iustitia gave the English noun justice.
latinEntries.exampleCN: iustitia 产生英语名词 justice。

latinEntries.example: Probus survives in probity, honesty of character.
latinEntries.exampleCN: probus 残留在 probity 一词中，义为「正直」。

definition_zh: （圆形物的）边沿；框；（帽的）帽边；带沿的物件；（眼镜）镜框；（轮胎的）轮辋；形成边沿；以边沿环绕
definition_en: the outer edge of a round or curved object such as a bowl, a wheel, or a pair of glasses; also the hat that carries such an edge, or the act of surrounding something with an edge
core_image: 一只薄薄的白色边沿，沿着碗口绕成完整的一圈
scene: 桌上立着一只白瓷碗，碗口的白釉在光里亮成细细一圈。A thin gold rim ran around the edge of the cup.
sceneCN: 这里 rim 是「圆形器物的边沿」（第 1 个义项：碗口、杯口那样绕成一圈的外缘）；句意为杯口有一圈细细的金边。画面里有白瓷碗、杯口的一圈细沿和照在釉面上的光。

pos.zh: 边沿；框；帽边；轮辋；镜框；带沿的物件
形成边沿；以边沿环绕

collocations.phrase: the wide rim of a hat

derivatives.zh: 由 rim 加 -ed 构成，义为「有边沿的；带框的」，如 gold-rimmed 金边的
由 rim 加 -less 构成，义为「无边沿的；无框的」，常用于眼镜
由动词 rim 加 -ing 构成，义为「装框；镶边；形成边缘的过程」
与 rim 同形不同源的名词，义为「杯沿；帽檐」，由容器边义引申出「满到边沿」

senses.title: The edge around a round opening
senses.definition: the circular edge of a bowl, cup, or other round object that is open at the top
senses.definitionCN: 碗、杯等圆形敞口器物上沿的那一圈边缘
senses.example: The soup was filled right up to the rim of the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 汤一直盛到碗沿。
senses.why: The oldest recorded sense is the outer edge of a curved thing, so a rim is first the thin circle that closes off a round object.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的有记录义项是弯曲之物的外缘，所以 rim 首先指把圆形物体收边的那一圈细线。

senses.title: The band or frame that runs around a wheel
senses.titleCN: 轮辋；箍在车轮上的边圈
senses.definition: the outer band or hoop of a wheel, or a ring holding a tyre in place
senses.definitionCN: 车轮外侧的边圈，或把轮胎固定住的一圈环
senses.example: A deep pothole bent the front rim of the bicycle wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 一个深坑把自行车前轮的轮辋撞弯了。
senses.why: A wheel needs the edge to carry the tyre, so the circular band at its outer limit becomes a rim you can name on its own.
senses.whyCN: 车轮要靠这圈边沿来承托轮胎，于是位于外缘的圆环带本身就被叫作 rim，可以单独指称。

senses.title: The hat that has a projecting edge
senses.definition: a hat, especially one with a firm, projecting edge, as in a hat and rim in old-fashioned speech
senses.definitionCN: 一顶帽子，尤指带硬挺外沿的那种；旧式说法中常把帽子与帽边并提
senses.example: He set his broad rim at an angle and left.
senses.exampleCN: 他把宽帽边一压、歪了歪，就出门了。
senses.why: The projecting edge of a hat was so characteristic that the edge word took over the whole hat in older usage.
senses.whyCN: 帽子上向外伸出的那一圈边太有特征，以致旧用法让「边」这个词代替了整顶帽子。

senses.title: The frame that holds a lens
senses.definition: the frame that holds the lens of a pair of glasses, in phrases such as silver-rimmed or rimless
senses.definitionCN: 眼镜支架镜片的框，见于 silver-rimmed、rimless 等说法
senses.example: She switched to rimless glasses for a lighter look.
senses.exampleCN: 为了显得轻巧些，她换成了无框眼镜。
senses.why: Glasses are shaped like a pair of small circles, so the frame around each lens is called its rim, and rimless tells you there is none.
senses.whyCN: 眼镜就像两只小圆圈，所以每片镜片四周的框被称为 rim；rimless 就是说没有这圈框。

senses.title: A thin line of light or colour
senses.definition: a narrow band of light, colour, or material that runs around an object or a shadow
senses.definitionCN: 绕在物体或阴影周围的一圈光、颜色或物质
senses.example: A pale rim of light showed under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门底下透出一线淡淡的光边。
senses.why: Once an edge is seen as a line you can trace, any thin border of light or colour can be a rim.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把边沿看作可以描摹的一条线，那么任何细窄的光边或色边都可以叫作 rim。

senses.title: To form or surround with an edge
senses.definition: to have something as an edge, or to put an edge around something; usually used in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 以某物作为边沿，或在某物周围加上边沿，常用被动
senses.example: The pond was rimmed with reeds and flat stones.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘四周环绕着芦苇与扁平的石头。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into the act of drawing that circular line around something.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：沿着某物描出那一圈线，就是「环绕、镶边」。

senses.title: A margin between the ordinary and guilt
senses.definition: in the phrase on the rim of, the point or margin just before something dangerous or doubtful happens
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on the rim of 一语，指危险或可疑之事将发未发的那一刻或边界
senses.example: His career was on the rim of scandal for months.
senses.exampleCN: 有好几个月，他的职业都处在丑闻的边缘。
senses.why: An edge separates inside from outside, so to be near the edge is to be near the other side as well.
senses.whyCN: 边沿把里面与外面分开，所以靠近边沿，也就是靠近另一边，这就是临界之意的来处。

intro.en: Rim is a native English noun for an edge, recorded from Old English, and generally taken to be a variant of brim, itself an old word for the edge of water.
intro.cn: rim 是英语本土的边缘名词，古英语中已有记载，一般认为它是 brim 的变体，而 brim 本义是水边。

items.en: Rima means an edge, a border, or a rim, and is recorded in early English texts.
items.cn: rima 意为边、边界、边沿，见于早期英语文献。

items.en: Many sources treat rim as a shortened side form of brim; whether the words split from one root is still uncertain.
items.cn: 许多资料认为 rim 是 brim 的缩略变体；两词是否同出一源尚无定论。

items.en: Rim is used for the edge of a vessel, a shield, or a wheel, and the sense has kept to round things ever since.
items.cn: 中古英语中 rim 用于器皿、盾牌或车轮的边沿，此义此后一直限于圆形物体。

items.en: Specialised uses appear: the rim of a wheel, the rim of a hat, and the frame of spectacles.
items.cn: 专门义项出现：车轮的轮辋、帽子的帽边，以及眼镜框。

items.en: The verb is born from the noun, so a street can be rimmed with trees, and a lens can be rimless.
items.cn: 动词由名词派生，于是街道可以用树环绕，镜片可以是无框的。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short rhyming shape of rim or the same edge family; the near-meaning group ranks words for edges from the tight circle outward.
note.cn: 形近组收与 rim 押韵同形的短词或同属边缘词族的词；近义组把各种「边」由紧贴的圆圈向外排列。

entries.definition: The top edge of a cup or the projecting edge of a hat; generally taken to be the longer form of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杯沿、帽檐」；一般认为它与 rim 同源，是较长的形式。

entries.definition: To cut neatly or decorate the edge of something; only the sound and shape are close, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修剪；镶边装饰」；只是读音与拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Stiffly neat and proper in manner; a rhyming neighbour with no link in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一本正经的、拘谨整洁的」；只是押韵，意义无关。

entries.definition: Unpleasant, serious, and forbidding; another rhyming neighbour, from an older word for fierce.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「严峻的、阴沉的」；同为押韵词，来自另一个古老词根。

entries.definition: Without a rim, especially of glasses whose lenses have no frame.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边框的」，尤指无框眼镜。

entries.definition: The outer limit of any surface; the general word that is not tied to round shapes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「边缘」，是通用词，不限于圆形物体。

entries.definition: The line where one area ends and another begins, often as a strip or design.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「边界、边饰」，指两个区域相接处，常带花边或带状装饰。

entries.definition: The blank edge of a page or the spare amount beyond a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「页边空白；余量」，指页面留白或超出限度的余数。

entries.definition: The edge of a road or the point at which something is about to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「路边；边缘」，指道路边缘或某事将发生的临界点。

entries.definition: The projecting rim of a container such as a jug or a cup.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（容器的）口沿」，指水壶、杯子等器物凸出的边。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the shape of rim, its link with brim, and the round objects the word is found with.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 rim 的拼写形状、它与 brim 的关系，以及这个词常出现的圆形物件。

normal.en: Rim and brim are one old edge word in two sizes; both mean the edge of a round or open thing.
normal.cn: rim 与 brim 是同一个古老「边」词的两种长短形式，都指圆形或敞口之物的边。

normal.en: Rim stays narrow: the rim of a cup, a wheel, a lens, or a hat.
normal.cn: rim 的范围很窄：杯沿、轮辋、镜框或帽边。

normal.en: Rimmed is the past form and rimless the negative: a street rimmed with trees has no bare edges.
normal.cn: rimmed 是过去形式，rimless 是它的否定：被树环绕的街道没有光秃的边。

normal.en: A thin line of light at a door is a rim of light, because a rim is always a line.
normal.cn: 门缝透出的一线光就是 a rim of light，因为 rim 总是一条线。

normal.en: Compare edge: edge fits squares and any surface, while rim prefers circles.
normal.cn: 对比 edge：edge 适用于方块与任何表面，rim 更偏爱圆形。

abstract.en: Picture a thin white line circling a bowl at the very top, closing it like a drawn ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细白线在碗口最高处绕成一圈，像画上的一个环。

abstract.en: Think of a bicycle wheel seen from the side, its thin metal band carrying the rubber tyre.
abstract.cn: 想象从侧面看一只自行车轮，细细的金属圈承着橡胶轮胎。

abstract.en: Picture a rounded pond with reeds standing all around its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆形的池塘，四周立满了芦苇。

examples.en: She wiped the drink that had spilled onto the rim of the glass.
examples.cn: 她擦掉了洒在玻璃杯沿上的饮料。

examples.en: A narrow rim of sand circled the small island.
examples.cn: 一圈窄窄的沙滩环绕着这座小岛。

examples.en: The old map was rimmed with a row of tiny drawings.
examples.cn: 那张旧地图四周镶着一排小小的图案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞姆」——瑞姆把碗口一圈描出来，边沿就显出来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 rima（边缘、边界）；一般认为与表示「水边」的 brim 同源，或为 brim 的变体，确切关系不确定；核心义「绕成一圈的边沿」。

sensesIntro.en: Rim is a line drawn round a round thing: first a bowl edge, then a wheel band, a hat, a lens frame, a line of light, the act of circling, and finally the edge of what is acceptable.
sensesIntro.cn: rim 是沿圆形物描出的一条线：先是碗口，然后是轮圈、帽子、镜框、一圈光，再到环绕的动作，最后落在可接受范围的边界上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white line circles the top of a bowl and closes it into a ring.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细细的白线绕着碗口一圈，把它收成一个环。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: the line round the mouth of a cup or bowl is the starting point.
branches.cn: 容器线：杯口、碗口绕出的一圈是起点。

branches.en: THE HOOP: wheels and lens frames wear the same ring of metal or plastic.
branches.cn: 圆环线：车轮与镜框穿着同一圈金属或塑料。

branches.en: THE BAND: a hat edge or a thin band of light is a rim you can see at a glance.
branches.cn: 带状线：帽边或一圈细光，都是一眼能看到的 rim。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb draws the ring, so a pond is rimmed with reeds.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词把环画出来，所以池塘被芦苇环绕。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: every edge separates inside from outside, and being near it is being nearly over it.
branches.cn: 界线：每条边都分开内与外，临近边沿也就是快要越过去。

intro.en: Rim is a short native noun; English builds rimmed, rimless, and rimming on it with ordinary suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: rim 是短小的本土名词；英语用品后缀与复合方式在它上面构成 rimmed、rimless 与 rimming。

latinIntro.en: Rim has no Latin ancestor, so the Latin entries below are words for borders and rims from the same meaning field, not its origin.
latinIntro.cn: rim 没有拉丁语来源，所以下面列出的拉丁语词是同属「边沿」词场的近邻词，并非它的来源。

items.example: The rim of the saucer was chipped.
items.exampleCN: 碟子的边沿缺了一小块。

items.example: The suffix makes rimmed, as in gold-rimmed.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 rimmed，如 gold-rimmed。

items.example: The suffix makes rimless glasses.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 rimless glasses（无框眼镜）。

items.example: Rimming is the act of fitting an edge.
items.exampleCN: rimming 指装边、加框的动作。

items.meaning: edge of a cup or hat
items.example: Brim is the longer form of the same edge word.
items.exampleCN: brim 是同一个「边」词的较长形式。

items.example: Edge is the general word that rim narrows.
items.exampleCN: edge 是通用词，rim 是它的收窄版。

items.example: A rim of frost had formed on the window.
items.exampleCN: 窗户四周结了一圈霜边。

items.example: The firm stood on the rim of failure.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司濒临倒闭。

items.example: Rim in English compounds almost always means an edge.
items.exampleCN: 英语复合词中的 rim 几乎总表示边缘。
