labrum 在英语中产生 labial。
circulus 产生 circle 与 circular。
orbis 产生 orbit 与 orb。

definition_zh: 手机铃声；来电铃声；自定义铃音
definition_en: the sound a mobile phone makes when someone calls or sends a message
core_image: 口袋里的手机忽然响起，一串熟悉的旋律把周围人的目光都引了过来
scene: 会议进行到一半，他口袋里忽然传出一段响亮的音乐，所有人都转过头来。A loud ringtone suddenly played from his pocket and everyone turned to look.
sceneCN: 这里 ringtone 是「手机铃声」（第 1 个义项：手机响起的提示音）；句意：一个响亮的铃声突然从他口袋里响起，所有人都转头看过去。

pos.zh: 手机铃声；来电铃声；自定义铃音

derivatives.zh: 由 ring 加 back 构成，拨号者听到的回铃音
铃响的动词形式，是构成 ringtone 的基础词
音调，构成 ringtone 的后半部分
由 tone 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，意为音调的
由 ring 加 -ing 构成，指响铃声

senses.title: The sound a phone makes for an incoming call
senses.definition: the sequence of notes a mobile phone plays to announce an incoming call or message
senses.definitionCN: 手机为提示来电或短信而播放的一串音调
senses.example: I set a jazz tune as my ringtone.
senses.exampleCN: 我把一段爵士乐曲设成了铃声。
senses.why: Ringtones were born when mobile phones began ringing, so the word names the sound that announces a ring.
senses.whyCN: 手机开始响起铃声之后才产生了 ringtone 一词，所以它指的就是宣告「响起」的那个声音。

senses.title: A personalized tune chosen by the owner
senses.definition: a song or musical clip that a phone user chooses and downloads to replace the standard alert
senses.definitionCN: 用户选择并下载、用来替换默认提示音的歌曲或音乐片段
senses.example: Young people once paid to download a popular song as a custom ringtone.
senses.exampleCN: 过去年轻人会花钱下载一首流行歌作为个性铃声。
senses.why: Once phones could store music, the ringtone turned from a fixed beep into a personal choice.
senses.whyCN: 当手机能够存储音乐之后，铃声就从固定的哔哔声变成了一种个人选择。

senses.title: The ringtone industry
senses.definition: the commercial market in which music clips are sold for use as phone alerts
senses.definitionCN: 以销售音乐片段供手机提示音使用而形成的商业市场
senses.example: The ringtone market earned huge sums in the early years of this century.
senses.exampleCN: 在本世纪初，铃声市场赚取了巨额收入。
senses.why: A single product word often grows into a market name, as shown by sales figures reported for the ringtone trade.
senses.whyCN: 一个产品词往往会发展成一个市场名，铃声交易的销售额就说明了这一点。

senses.title: A signal rather than music
senses.definition: a short alert sound for an alarm, a timer, or a notification rather than for a voice call
senses.definitionCN: 用于闹钟、计时器或通知提醒的短促提示音，而不是为语音来电而响的音
senses.example: The app let me choose a quieter ringtone for notifications.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用允许我为通知选择一个更安静的提示音。
senses.why: The core meaning is simply a sound that announces something, so it stretches from calls to any alert.
senses.whyCN: 它的核心意思只是「宣告某事的声响」，因此可以从来电延伸到任何提醒。

intro.en: Ringtone is a modern English compound of ring and tone, named when mobile phones spread in the late twentieth century.
intro.cn: ringtone 是现代英语由 ring 与 tone 组成的合成词，在二十世纪后期手机普及之后才出现。

items.en: Hringan means to sound, as a bell does.
items.cn: 古英语 hringan 意为钟铃作响。

items.en: Tonus means a sound or a pitch, from Greek tonos.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonus 意为声音或音高，源自希腊语 tonos。

items.en: Ton arrives in English through French with the sense of musical pitch.
items.cn: ton 经法语进入英语，带着音乐的「音高」之意。

items.en: Linguists describe the patterns of pitch in speech with the term tone.
items.cn: 语言学家用 tone 一词描述说话时的音高模式。

items.en: Ringtones appear as mobile phones bring ringing calls into daily life.
items.cn: 随着手机把「响铃来电」带入日常生活，ringtone 一词出现。

note.en: Ringtone sits beside its two parts ring and tone, and near the words for other sounds a phone makes.
note.cn: ringtone 紧挨着它的两个组成部分 ring 与 tone，也与手机发出的其他声音词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a clear sound like a bell, or a phone making this sound
entries.definitionCN: 像钟一样响；电话响铃；ringtone 的前半部分

entries.definition: the quality or pitch of a sound
entries.definitionCN: 音调；音色；ringtone 的后半部分

entries.definition: the sound a caller hears while waiting for an answer
entries.definitionCN: 回铃音，拨打者等待接听时听到的声音；其实只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an electrical device that makes a buzzing sound as a signal
entries.definitionCN: 蜂鸣器；发出嗡嗡提示音的装置

entries.definition: a shaking alert used instead of a sound on a phone
entries.definitionCN: 手机上的振动提醒，用来代替声音

entries.definition: a light ringing sound made by bells or a doorbell
entries.definitionCN: 钟铃或门铃发出的清脆响声

normalIntro.en: Ringtone is simply ring plus tone: the sound of the phone ringing, shaped into a chosen tune.
normalIntro.cn: ringtone 就是 ring 加 tone：电话响起的声响，被塑造成一段选定的旋律。

normal.en: The first part ring is the phone ringing.
normal.cn: 前半部分 ring 就是电话响起。

normal.en: The second part tone is any note or tune you like.
normal.cn: 后半部分 tone 是任何你喜欢的音符或曲调。

normal.en: People set a ringtone so they know the call is for them.
normal.cn: 人们设置铃声，好分辨这通电话是找自己的。

normal.en: A custom ringtone replaced the old beep once songs could be stored.
normal.cn: 当歌曲能被存储后，个性铃声取代了旧的哔哔声。

normal.en: The word changed ring into the noun ringer and gave us ringtones.
normal.cn: 这个词把 ringing 固化进名词，再变为复数 ringtones。

abstract.en: Picture a jacket pocket moving to its own small rhythm in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里，一件外套的口袋按着自己的小节奏在动。

abstract.en: Imagine writing your own name in musical notes on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象在屏幕上用一个个音符写下自己的名字。

abstract.en: Think of a tiny jukebox in your palm, ringing for coins.
abstract.cn: 想象掌心里一台小小的点唱机，响着等硬币投进来。

examples.en: Please turn your ringtone off before the exam starts.
examples.cn: 考试开始前请把手机铃声关掉。

examples.en: He changes his ringtone almost every week.
examples.cn: 他几乎每周都换一次手机铃声。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to lower the volume of our ringtones.
examples.cn: 老师让我们把手机铃声音量调低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铃通」——铃声一通，就有人找你；这只是一种谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 现代英语合成词：ring（古英语 hringan，钟铃作响）+ tone（拉丁语 tonus，音调）→ ringtone，核心义「让电话响的那段调子」。

sensesIntro.en: Ringtone begins with the basic alert of an incoming call, then grows into a personal tune, a market, and a general alert sound.
sensesIntro.cn: ringtone 先指来电时响起的基本提示音，再发展为个性化的曲调、一个产业，以及更宽泛的提醒音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket that suddenly starts to play music.
core.cn: 核心意象：口袋里忽然开始演奏音乐。

branches.en: The plain alert for an incoming call is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 来电时最普通的提示音是基本义项。

branches.en: Choosing a tune turns the alert into a personal statement.
branches.cn: 挑选曲调把提示音变成个人的表达。

branches.en: Selling tunes turns the word into the name of an industry.
branches.cn: 售卖曲调让这个词变成了产业名称。

branches.en: Calls and notifications are both announced by the same kind of sound.
branches.cn: 来电与通知都由同一类声响来宣告。

branches.en: A custom tune is the product that the ringtone market sells.
branches.cn: 个性曲调正是铃声市场所出售的产品。

intro.en: Ringtone is built from two free English words and a family of related forms: ring, ringing, tone, tonal, and ringback.
intro.cn: ringtone 由两个独立的英语单词构成，并带出 ring、ringing、tone、tonal、ringback 等一组同族形式。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half has a Latin source: tonus means a sound or pitch, borrowed from Greek tonos.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半部分有拉丁来源：拉丁语 tonus 意为声音或音高，借自希腊语 tonos。

items.example: The phone will ring in a moment.
items.exampleCN: 电话马上就会响。

items.meaning: the sound of a bell or phone
items.example: The ringing woke the whole house.
items.exampleCN: 铃声把全家人都吵醒了。

items.meaning: pitch or quality of a sound
items.example: A soft tone suits a quiet office.
items.exampleCN: 安静的办公室适合柔和的音调。

items.example: Tonal variety keeps a speaker interesting.
items.exampleCN: 音调变化让讲话者更有吸引力。

items.meaning: the sound a phone makes for a call
items.example: His ringtone is a famous film theme.
items.exampleCN: 他的铃声是一段著名的电影主题曲。

items.meaning: the sound a caller hears while waiting
items.example: The ringback tells the caller the line is busy.
items.exampleCN: 回铃音告诉拨打者线路正忙。

items.example: The suffix -al turns tone into tonal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 tone 变成 tonal。

items.example: The suffix -ing turns ring into ringing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 把 ring 变成 ringing。

items.example: Silent mode mutes every ringtone.
items.exampleCN: 静音模式会让所有铃声都静下来。

items.example: Many people make phones vibrate instead of using a ringtone.
items.exampleCN: 许多人让手机振动，而不用铃声。

definition_zh: 漫游；漫无目的地游荡；徘徊；巡视
definition_en: to walk or travel around places without a fixed plan or clear goal
core_image: 一个人脚不停步，在街巷与山野间东走西逛，没有目的地也不赶时间
scene: 背包客没有地图，沿着海岸线一路漫走，看到小渔村就停下来住一晚。With no map, the backpackers roamed along the coast and stopped at any small fishing village.
sceneCN: 这里 roam 是「漫游、闲逛」（第 2 个义项：无目的地走动）；句意：背包客没有地图，沿着海岸一路漫游，遇到小渔村就停下来。

pos.zh: 漫游；游荡；徘徊
漫游于某地；在……走来走去

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，指到处漫游的人
由动词加 -ing 构成，指漫游；也是手机出境漫游的说法
由 roam 与 free 组合，指（动物）可以自由走动的

senses.title: To wander on foot without a goal
senses.definition: to walk around a place slowly and aimlessly, often just for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地方慢无目的地走动，常只是为了消遣
senses.example: We roamed through the old town all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在老城里闲逛了一下午。
senses.why: The earliest use of the word is about walking about, so the strongest image is feet moving without a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早就是「四处走动」的意思，所以最鲜明的画面是没有计划的双脚在移动。

senses.title: To travel over a wide area
senses.definition: to travel over a large region freely, staying nowhere for long
senses.definitionCN: 在大片区域内自由地四处行走，不留久居
senses.example: Wild horses roam across the highlands.
senses.exampleCN: 野马在高原上四处漫游。
senses.why: The random walking sense stretches out over distance, so the place becomes a whole region.
senses.whyCN: 随意的走动一旦拉远到更大范围，所说的地方就从一条街道变成了一整片区域。

senses.title: To let the eyes or mind wander
senses.definition: to move freely from place to place, used of eyes, thoughts, or attention
senses.definitionCN: 自由地四处移动，用于说目光、思绪或注意力
senses.example: Her eyes roamed around the crowded hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的目光在拥挤的大厅里四处游移。
senses.why: When people wander, the phrase transfers that free movement to whatever we look at or think about.
senses.whyCN: 当人四处游走时，这种自由的移动也被借到我们看的东西和想的事情上。

senses.title: To move about in a network or signal
senses.definition: to move between mobile networks or computer systems while a service keeps working
senses.definitionCN: 在使用服务不中断的情况下于移动网络或计算机系统之间切换
senses.example: You can make calls while roaming in another country, but it costs more.
senses.exampleCN: 在别的国家漫游时也能打电话，但费用更高。
senses.why: A signal leaves the home network and wanders into another one, so the word spreads by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 信号离开本地网络漫游进另一个网络，这个词就顺着这种类比扩展到了通信领域。

senses.title: To walk about searching for something
senses.definition: to move from place to place with a purpose, such as guards patrolling or a person searching
senses.definitionCN: 有事由地四处移动，比如巡逻的守卫或搜寻的人
senses.example: Dogs roamed the border for stray sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 狗在边界一带四处搜寻走失的羊。
senses.why: Even with a quiet purpose, moving back and forth over an area is still roaming, so the word covers searching and patrolling.
senses.whyCN: 即使带着目的，在一个区域内来回移动仍然属于漫游，所以这个词也能描述搜寻与巡逻。

intro.en: Roam is recorded in Middle English; its exact origin is uncertain, with rival suggestions of an Old French or a direct Romance source.
intro.cn: roam 自中古英语已有记载，确切来源不确定，有学者推测它来自古法语，也有人认为直接来自罗曼语族。

items.en: The origin of roam is uncertain and no root can be firmly established.
items.cn: roam 的来源不确定，无法确认确切的词根。

items.en: One suggestion is Roma, from the image of pilgrims travelling to Rome.
items.cn: 有一种推测认为它来自罗马，取朝圣者长途跋涉前往罗马的意象。

items.en: Another suggestion is romeu, a word for a pilgrim.
items.cn: 另一种推测认为它来自古法语 romeu，指朝圣者。

items.en: Early spelling forms of the verb appear with the sense of going about.
items.cn: 中古英语中这个动词的早期拼写形式已经表示「四处走动」。

items.en: Roam becomes a favourite word for free travel and, later, for mobile phone networks.
items.cn: 现代英语中 roam 广泛用于描述自由旅行，后来又用于手机网络。

note.en: Roam is close to wander and stray, and stands apart from look-alikes that share only its spelling or sound.
note.cn: roam 与 wander、stray 意思相近，而与之形近或音近的 ram、romp 只是巧合，并无同源关系。

entries.definition: a person who wanders about
entries.definitionCN: 漫游者；到处游走的人

entries.definition: to play roughly and noisily
entries.definitionCN: 欢闹地玩耍；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to hit something very hard
entries.definitionCN: 猛撞；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to move about slowly with no clear direction
entries.definitionCN: 漫无目的地慢慢走动；闲逛

entries.definition: to leave the right place or path
entries.definitionCN: 走失；偏离原有的路线

entries.definition: to be carried along by a current or by chance
entries.definitionCN: 漂流；随波逐流

normalIntro.en: Roam has no sure root to follow, so the memory hooks come from its sense of free, unhurried movement.
normalIntro.cn: roam 词根存疑，所以记忆点来自它「自由、不急不忙地移动」的感觉。

normal.en: A roamer is someone who roams, built with the -er suffix.
normal.cn: roamer 是「漫游的人」，由动词加 -er 构成。

normal.en: The roaming setting on a phone comes from the same idea of signals wandering.
normal.cn: 手机的「漫游」设置同样取「信号游走」的意思。

normal.en: Roam is close to wander, but often covers a wider area.
normal.cn: roam 与 wander 接近，但常常指更大的范围。

normal.en: Roam is a regular verb: roams, roamed, roamed, roaming.
normal.cn: roam 是规则动词：变化依次为 roams、roamed、roamed、roaming。

normal.en: Compare with stray: to roam is often chosen, but to stray is to leave the right path.
normal.cn: 对比 stray：roam 往往出于自愿闲走，而 stray 是偏离了该走的路。

abstract.en: Picture footprints that circle back on themselves without any plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一串没有计划、绕回原处的脚印。

abstract.en: Imagine a camera set free over a wide city at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时分，一台摄像机在一座大城上空自由游走。

abstract.en: Think of a radio signal that quietly slips from one tower to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一段无线电信号悄悄从一个信号塔溜进另一个。

examples.en: She likes to roam the hills with her dog on quiet mornings.
examples.cn: 安静的早晨，她喜欢带着狗在山间漫游。

examples.en: Buffalo once roamed the plains in huge numbers.
examples.cn: 野牛曾经成群结队地在大平原上漫游。

examples.en: Turn off roaming before you travel to avoid high bills.
examples.cn: 出国前关掉漫游，以免产生高额费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「罗马」——古时去罗马朝圣，一路走走停停，就是在漫游；这只是谐音联想，词源并无定论。

root: roam 确切的来源不确定；一般认为可能与古法语 romeu（朝圣者）有关，也可能源自拉丁语 Roma（罗马），取朝圣者长途跋涉之意，但此说未能证实。核心义「四处游走」。

sensesIntro.en: Roam starts with aimless walking, widens to travelling over regions, then moves to wandering eyes and minds, to roaming signals, and to moving about with a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: roam 先指漫无目的地走动，再扩展为大范围的游历，然后转到目光与思绪的游移、信号漫游，最后指带有目的的来回走动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet that keep moving and never pick a destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：不停移动却从不选定目的地的双脚。

branches.en: Leisurely walking is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 悠闲的闲逛是日常义项。

branches.en: Wandering over a region is the travelling sense.
branches.cn: 在区域内四处行走是旅行义项。

branches.en: Eyes and thoughts roam as freely as feet.
branches.cn: 目光与思绪像双脚一样自由游走。

branches.en: Physical travel and roaming signals both cross a boundary easily.
branches.cn: 身体旅行与信号漫游都轻松跨越边界。

branches.en: Even a searching guard walks the same unmapped circle.
branches.cn: 即使是搜寻的守卫，走的也是同样没有定数的圈子。

intro.en: Roam is a single free morpheme with no proven affixes; related forms are made with -er, -ing, and the compound roam-free.
intro.cn: roam 是单一的自由语素，没有确证的词缀；相关形式靠 -er、-ing 以及 roam-free 这样的组合构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin origin for roam is proven; the link to Latin Roma is only a suggestion and cannot count as an attested source.
latinIntro.cn: roam 并没有确证的拉丁来源；与拉丁语 Roma 的联系只是一种推测，不能算作已证实的来源。

items.example: They roam the forest every summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天都在森林里漫游。

items.meaningCN: roam 的第三人称单数形式
items.example: A fox roams the garden at night.
items.exampleCN: 夜里有一只狐狸在花园里游荡。

items.example: The tribe roamed these plains for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这个部族曾在这片平原游荡了几个世纪。

items.example: Roaming charges can be high abroad.
items.exampleCN: 在国外的漫游费可能很高。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms roamer from roam.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 roam 变成 roamer。

items.example: The camel is a natural roamer of dry lands.
items.exampleCN: 骆驼是干旱地区天生的漫游者。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms roaming from roam.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 把 roam 变成 roaming。

items.example: Free in a compound lets animals roam without fences.
items.exampleCN: 作为组合成分的 free 表示动物可以无围栏地自由走动。

items.example: The pet chickens live in a roam-free yard.
items.exampleCN: 这些宠物鸡生活在可以自由走动的院子里。

definition_zh: 强壮的；健壮的；坚固耐用的；稳健的；有力的
definition_en: strong and healthy, or able to work well under difficult conditions
core_image: 一棵粗壮的橡树在狂风中只晃动枝叶，树干纹丝不动
scene: 冬日清晨，溪边那棵老橡树依旧枝叶青翠，狂风过后更显坚挺。In the cold morning light, the old oak stayed green and stood as a robust tree after the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 robust 是「强壮的、坚固的」（第 1 个义项：身体强壮、结实）；句意：寒冷的晨光里，那棵老橡树依然青翠，暴风雨过后依旧是一棵强壮挺拔的树。

pos.zh: 强壮的；健壮的
坚固的；结实的；耐用可靠的

collocations.zh: 有力的辩护；牢固的防御

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为强有力地、坚定地
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为强健、稳健、可靠性
由 robust 加 -ious 构成的古雅形容形式，义为喧闹粗壮的

senses.title: Strong and healthy in body
senses.definition: having a strong, healthy body and able to resist illness or hard work
senses.definitionCN: 身体强壮健康，能够抵抗疾病或承受辛苦劳累
senses.example: He is still robust at the age of eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 他八十岁了，身子仍很硬朗。
senses.why: Latin robur means oak, a wood famous for strength, so the first sense carries the hardness of that tree.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 robur 意为橡木，这种木料以坚固著称，因此第一个义项带着那棵树坚硬的特质。

senses.title: Built to withstand hard use
senses.definition: strongly made, so that it is not easily damaged or broken
senses.definitionCN: 制作得很牢固，不容易损坏或折断
senses.example: The phone has a robust metal case.
senses.exampleCN: 这款手机有坚固的金属外壳。
senses.why: The sturdy tree image shifts from a body to a thing, since both must stand up to force without breaking.
senses.whyCN: 挺立的树木形象可以从身体转到器物上，因为二者都要扛住外力而不折断。

senses.title: Strong in a non-physical way
senses.definition: showing strong force or steady condition, used of growth, an economy, or an argument
senses.definitionCN: 表现出强大的力量或稳定的状态，用于说增长、经济或论据
senses.example: The country reported robust growth last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该国去年报告了强劲的增长。
senses.why: Strength of body becomes strength of trend, so an economy or a case can be robust too.
senses.whyCN: 身体的力量变成趋势的力量，于是经济或论据也可以用 robust 来形容。

senses.title: Able to keep working under faults or pressure
senses.definition: designed so that it still works well when data are poor, conditions change, or something goes wrong
senses.definitionCN: 在设计上即使数据不全、条件改变或出现故障也仍能良好运作
senses.example: Engineers test the software to make it robust against power cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试这款软件，让它能在断电时依然稳定运行。
senses.why: A sturdy object resists a blow, and a sturdy system resists errors in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 结实的物件能扛住撞击，稳健的系统同样能扛住错误。

senses.title: Forceful and full-bodied
senses.definition: having a strong, rich flavour or sound rather than a thin delicate one
senses.definitionCN: 味道或声音浓烈饱满，而不是单薄轻柔
senses.example: The restaurant serves a robust country wine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅供应一种口感浓郁的乡土葡萄酒。
senses.why: The force of the tree passes into taste and sound, so a drink or a voice can also be robust.
senses.whyCN: 树木的力量感也进入了味道与声音，所以饮品或嗓音同样可以很 robust。

intro.en: Robust comes from Latin robur, oak wood, by way of robur and robustus, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: robust 源自拉丁语 robur（橡木、力量），经 robur、robustus 与法语进入英语。

items.en: Robur means oak wood, or strength, especially the strength of that hard wood.
items.cn: robur 意为橡木，也可指力量，尤其指这种坚硬木材的强度。

items.en: Robustus means strong and sturdy, made of oak.
items.cn: robustus 意为坚固结实、用橡木制成的。

items.en: Robuste brings the adjective into French with the sense of strong and firm.
items.cn: robuste 把这个形容词带入法语，意为强壮而结实。

items.en: Robust enters English in the sixteenth century as a word for bodily strength.
items.cn: 十六世纪 robust 进入英语，首先指身体的强壮。

items.en: Later the word spreads to arguments, statistics, and computer systems that resist failure.
items.cn: 后来这个词扩展到论据、统计数据和能够抗故障的计算机系统。

note.en: Robust belongs to a Latin family around robur, and stands beside sturdy and vigorous for strength.
note.cn: robust 属于以 robur 为中心的拉丁词族，并与 sturdy、vigorous 等表示强健的词相邻。

entries.definition: strongly and firmly
entries.definitionCN: 强有力地；坚定地

entries.definition: the quality of being strong and reliable
entries.definitionCN: 强健；稳健可靠

entries.definition: to confirm a statement with evidence
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证实；同出拉丁语 robur，原义是「使之强壮」

entries.definition: strong and unlikely to break
entries.definitionCN: 结实的；不易损坏的

entries.definition: full of energy and force
entries.definitionCN: 充满精力与力量的

entries.definition: lasting a long time without getting damaged
entries.definitionCN: 耐用的；经久不坏的

normalIntro.en: Robust grows from Latin robur, the oak: the memory is a hard tree that will not be pushed over.
normalIntro.cn: robust 来自拉丁语 robur，也就是橡木：记忆点就是一棵推不倒的硬木树。

normal.en: The noun robustness is made with the suffix -ness.
normal.cn: 名词 robustness 由后缀 -ness 构成。

normal.en: The adverb robustly is made with the suffix -ly.
normal.cn: 副词 robustly 由后缀 -ly 构成。

normal.en: The root robur also gives corroborate, to make a claim strong with evidence.
normal.cn: 同一个词根 robur 还带来 corroborate，意为用证据让说法变得有力。

normal.en: Robust health and robust growth keep the same image of a tree standing firm.
normal.cn: robust health 与 robust growth 都保留着树木岿然不动的意象。

normal.en: Compare sturdy: sturdy is the everyday word for solid objects, robust is slightly more formal and covers systems.
normal.cn: 对比 sturdy：sturdy 是形容结实物品的日常词，robust 稍正式，还能形容系统。

abstract.en: Picture an oak that bends its branches in a gale but never loses its trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵橡树在狂风里弯动枝条，却始终不折主干。

abstract.en: Imagine a wooden axle that takes every jolt and still turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木轴承受每一次颠簸，却照样转个不停。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy merchant ship that still sails steadily when the wind rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘厚重的商船，风浪再起也依然稳稳前行。

examples.en: The researchers found a robust link between diet and heart health.
examples.cn: 研究者发现饮食与心脏健康之间有很强的关联。

examples.en: This frame is robust enough to carry a heavy load.
examples.cn: 这个框架足够坚固，能承载重物。

examples.en: Farmers need robust crops that survive dry summers.
examples.cn: 农民需要能熬过干旱夏季的强健作物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「罗拔须」——想象一位叫罗拔的壮汉，须发浓密、身板像橡树般结实；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 robur（橡木；力量）→ robustus（坚实的）→ 古法语 robuste → 英语 robust，核心义「像橡木一样结实」。

sensesIntro.en: Robust begins with a strong body like an oak, then moves to sturdy objects, strong trends, reliable systems, and rich flavours.
sensesIntro.cn: robust 先指像橡树一样强壮的身体，再指坚固的器物、强劲的趋势、稳健的系统，以及浓郁的味道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick oak trunk that will not be pushed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：推不倒的粗壮橡树干。

branches.en: A strong body is the oldest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 强壮的身体是这个词最古老的义项。

branches.en: Sturdy goods borrow the strength of the oak.
branches.cn: 坚固的器物借用了橡木的强度。

branches.en: Strong trends are strength without a body.
branches.cn: 强劲的趋势是没有实体的强度。

branches.en: A sturdier system meets errors the way a sturdy object meets a blow.
branches.cn: 更稳健的系统面对错误，就像结实物件面对击打。

branches.en: Health and rich flavour are both described as full and strong.
branches.cn: 健康与浓郁的味道都被描述为饱满而有劲。

intro.en: Robust is a single Latin adjective whose English family is built with -ly, -ness, and a related verb corroborate.
intro.cn: robust 是单一的拉丁语形容词，它在英语中的同族词由 -ly、-ness 构成，并有同根动词 corroborate。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin robur, the oak, and its adjective robustus, strong and sturdy like oak.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 robur（橡木）及其形容词 robustus，意为像橡木般坚固结实。

items.example: Robur stands for the hardest wood of the forest.
items.exampleCN: robur 指林中最硬的木材。

items.example: Robustus describes a body like oak.
items.exampleCN: robustus 形容如橡木般的身体。

items.example: Robust plants survive cold winters.
items.exampleCN: 强健的植物能熬过寒冬。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms robustly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 robustly。

items.example: The idea was robustly defended.
items.exampleCN: 这一观点得到了有力的辩护。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms robustness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 robustness。

items.meaning: the quality of being strong and reliable
items.example: Tests measure the robustness of the design.
items.exampleCN: 测试用来衡量设计的稳健程度。

items.meaning: to strengthen a claim with evidence
items.example: Two witnesses corroborate the report.
items.exampleCN: 两名证人证实了这份陈述。

items.example: The case needs corroboration.
items.exampleCN: 这桩案子需要佐证。

items.meaning: the quality of being solid and strong
items.example: Sturdiness matters for field equipment.
items.exampleCN: 野外设备讲究结实耐用。

definition_zh: 洛可可式（风格）（18 世纪欧洲装饰风格/指一种以贝壳与卷草纹样为特征的装饰风格）；过分精巧而不够大方的；矫饰的
definition_en: a light, highly ornamental style of European art and decoration from the early 18th century, marked by shell work, scrolls and pastel colours; also used of anything too fussy or showily refined
core_image: 贝壳与卷草纹在金色画框里盘绕成形，浅粉墙面配上柔白曲线
scene: 宫廷舞厅的墙面刷成浅粉色，镜框上镀着金，纹样像贝壳一样弯弯绕绕。The salon was decorated in rococo style, with pale walls, gilt mirrors and swirls of shell and leaf.
sceneCN: 这里 rococo 是「洛可可装饰风格」（第 1 个义项：以贝壳与卷草纹样为特征的装饰风格）；句意为厅内以浅色墙、镀金镜与贝壳叶片般的曲线装饰，呈现精致的洛可可风。图中可辨识物件：镀金镜框、浅粉墙面、蜿蜒曲线、烛台、丝绸帷幔。

pos.zh: 形容词：洛可可风格的；过分精巧的；矫饰的
名词：洛可可风格；洛可可艺术

derivatives.zh: 法语借词，指以贝壳、碎石与卷草堆叠成的装饰手法，是洛可可纹样的核心来源
本词加后缀 -esque（具有……风格）构成，义为「仿洛可可的」
由本词加后缀 -osity 构成，指洛可可式的繁复精巧，较少使用
同属装饰史词族的前代风格，意为「巴洛克式的；奇异夸张的」

senses.title: The ornamental style itself
senses.definition: a decorative style of the early and mid eighteenth century, using shell forms, scrolls, pastel colours and asymmetric curves
senses.definitionCN: 十八世纪早中期的装饰风格，使用贝壳纹、卷涡、浅粉色调与不对称曲线
senses.example: The ceiling of the small salon shows the rococo at its lightest.
senses.exampleCN: 小厅的天花板展现了洛可可最轻巧的一面。
senses.why: The French decorative term rocaille named shell and rock work; French designers applied that name to the whole manner of ornament built on such forms.
senses.whyCN: 法语装饰术语 rocaille 本指贝壳与碎石镶嵌，法国设计界把这个名字扩用到整套以这类形态为基础的装饰做法上。

senses.title: Rococo art and architecture
senses.definition: the art, architecture and interiors produced in that style, especially in France and southern Germany in the eighteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 以该风格创作的艺术、建筑与室内，尤见于十八世纪的法国与德国南部
senses.example: Art historians treat the palace as a late example of the rococo.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史家把这座宫殿视为晚期洛可可作品。
senses.why: Once the ornamental manner was named, the works made in it were gathered under the same label, so the style word became the name of a period of art.
senses.whyCN: 装饰手法一旦被命名，用它创作的作品也被归到同一标签之下，于是风格词变成了一个艺术时期的名称。

senses.title: Ornately overdone
senses.definition: too fussy, elaborate or showily refined in style, often said of writing, design or manners
senses.definitionCN: 风格过于繁琐、堆砌或显得刻意精致，常用于写作、设计与举止
senses.example: Critics called the novel rococo, all curls and no backbone.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这部小说矫揉繁复，满篇花饰却没有骨架。
senses.why: Because the style prized ornament over structure, the word drifted from a description of decoration into a criticism of anything that is all ornament.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一风格重装饰而轻结构，这个词便从描写装饰，滑向批评一切只有装饰而没有实质的东西。

senses.title: Pastel colour and gilding
senses.definition: a colour scheme and finish typical of the style, with pale pinks, creams and greens set off by gilding and mirrors
senses.definitionCN: 该风格典型的色彩与表面处理：浅粉、米白、浅绿配以镀金与镜面
senses.example: The dining room was painted in rococo pinks and soft greys.
senses.exampleCN: 餐厅被刷成洛可可式的粉色与柔灰色。
senses.why: Pictures of the style fix on its colours as much as its shapes, so the word came to name a palette that sets pastel walls against bright gold.
senses.whyCN: 人们对这一风格的印象既来自形状，也来自颜色，于是这个词也用来指浅色墙面衬亮金色的一整套配色。

senses.title: Pleasure-seeking taste
senses.titleCN: 追求享乐与轻快的趣味
senses.definition: the playful, courtly taste for charm, pleasure and intimacy that the style expressed, contrasted with solemn grandeur
senses.definitionCN: 该风格所表现的玩弄、宫廷化、亲近私密的趣味，与庄严肃穆的宏伟相对
senses.example: The rococo turned the grand hall into a place for music and conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 洛可可把宏伟的大厅变成聆听音乐与交谈的场所。
senses.why: The style flourished in smaller, private rooms built for amusement, so its name also carries the mood of those rooms: light, intimate and pleasure-seeking.
senses.whyCN: 这一风格盛行于为娱乐而建的小型私密房间，因此其名称也带上那些房间的气氛：轻快、亲密、追求享乐。

senses.title: Chinese and floral motifs
senses.definition: the chinoiserie and naturalistic flower, vine and bird motifs that travelled with the style
senses.definitionCN: 随该风格一同流传的中国风以及写实的花、藤、鸟纹样
senses.example: The porcelain tea service pairs rococo scrolls with Chinese pagodas.
senses.exampleCN: 这套瓷茶具把洛可可卷涡纹与中国宝塔图案配在一起。
senses.why: Traders and decorators added Chinese and botanical ornament to the shell work, and the style name travelled with these motifs too.
senses.whyCN: 商人装饰家把中国纹样与植物纹样加入贝壳纹样之中，风格名称也随之这些母题一起传播。

senses.title: Revival and imitation
senses.definition: work made later that copies or revives the style, as in the nineteenth-century revival
senses.definitionCN: 后来模仿或复兴这一风格的作品，如十九世纪的复古风
senses.example: Nineteenth-century porcelain makers sold rococo revival tea sets.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的瓷器商出售洛可可复兴风格的茶具。
senses.why: Any named style becomes a pattern to copy, so rococo came to describe deliberate imitation as well as original work.
senses.whyCN: 任何被命名的风格都会成为可供模仿的样式，因此 rococo 既指原创作品，也指有意的仿作。

senses.title: Decorative, loose or unrestrained
senses.definition: in music, a free and ornamented style of playing, and generally a loose, fanciful or unrestrained manner
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐中指自由加花、装饰繁多的演奏风格；泛指松散、奇巧、不受约束的方式
senses.example: The players gave the slow movement a rococo freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 演奏者把慢乐章处理得自由而花哨。
senses.why: The style prized small ornament and free embellishment, so performers and writers borrowed the word for any loose, decorated handling.
senses.whyCN: 这一风格推崇细巧的装饰与自由的加花，于是演奏者与写作者借用这个词来形容任何松散而多装饰的处理方式。

intro.en: Rococo comes from French, where it began as a jewellers term for a decorative manner of stone and shell work.
intro.cn: rococo 来自法语，起初是珠宝与石作行业的术语，指一种用碎石与贝壳做装饰的做法。

items.en: Rocaille named ornamental work imitating irregular rocks, pebbles and shells, from roc, a rock; the decorative meaning is well attested.
items.cn: rocaille 指模仿不规则岩石、卵石与贝壳的装饰做法，源于 roc（岩石）；这一装饰义有据可查。

items.en: Rococo is recorded in French around the 1820s as a humorous formation from rocaille, used of the ornament of the previous century.
items.cn: rococo 约在十九世纪二十年代出现于法语，由 rocaille 戏谑地缩合而成，用来指上一世纪的装饰。

items.en: The form is often said to echo barocco, the source of baroque, but the link is a shaping analogy, not a proven borrowing.
items.cn: 这个词形常被认为呼应 barocco（baroque 的来源），但这种联系只是构形上的类比，并非有据可证的借用。

items.en: French critics applied the word to the whole late baroque style of the eighteenth century, first as a label of disparagement.
items.cn: 法国评论家在十九世纪三十年代把这个词用到十八世纪整个晚期巴洛克风格上，最初带有贬义。

items.en: English took the word as a name for the heavily ornamented style of the previous century and its later imitations. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借入，用来称呼上一世纪装饰繁复的风格及其后来的仿作；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The label moved from art history into ordinary description, where rococo can mean ornate, dated or merely over-elaborate.
items.cn: 这个词从艺术史进入日常描写，rococo 可以表示繁复、过时或单纯的过度雕琢。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers its French source and the style words that sit beside it; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of rich and fussy ornament.
note.cn: 形近组收它的法语来源与相邻的风格词；近义组收表示繁复华丽装饰的形容词。

entries.definition: The French term for shell-and-stone ornament, the decorative idea behind the name.
entries.definitionCN: 法语装饰术语，指贝壳与碎石装饰，是本词名称背后的装饰构思。

entries.definition: The French word for a rock, the base of rocaille.
entries.definitionCN: 法语「岩石」一词，是 rocaille 的词基。

entries.definition: The heavier style that preceded and partly overlapped the rococo; its endings sound alike and it shaped the newer name.
entries.definitionCN: 比洛可可更厚重的先行风格，部分时间重叠；两者词尾相近，新词名被认为受其构形影响。

entries.definition: Resembling the style without being an original example of it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指「仿洛可可的」，形似该风格但不是原创作品。

entries.definition: Heavily decorated; describes the amount of ornament, not one named style.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰繁多的，只说明装饰量多，不指某种被命名的风格。

entries.definition: Made of or decorated with flowers and leaves; names the motif, not the period.
entries.definitionCN: 花朵图案的；指名纹样题材，不指具体时期风格。

entries.definition: Too full of small details and hard to please the eye; the most everyday word for over-ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 过分多细节、看着累眼，是形容过度装饰最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the French source rocaille, the shell and rock ornament, and from the style words that appear beside rococo.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子来自法语来源 rocaille（贝壳与岩石装饰），以及常与 rococo 并置的风格词。

normal.en: rocaille named shells and pebbles used as ornament; rococo kept the picture of a coiling shell.
normal.cn: rocaille 指用作装饰的贝壳与卵石，rococo 保留的正是贝壳盘绕的画面。

normal.en: roc is French for a rock, so the whole family began in stone and shell work.
normal.cn: roc 是法语「岩石」，整个词族源自石作与贝壳工艺。

normal.en: rococo grew out of the heavier baroque; picture the same hall made smaller, lighter and paler.
normal.cn: rococo 从厚重的巴洛克演变而来；想象同一座大厅变得更小、更轻、更浅。

normal.en: Rococo rooms are pastel, gilt and intimate, built for music and conversation rather than display.
normal.cn: 洛可可房间浅色、镀金、私密，为音乐与交谈而建，不为炫示。

normal.en: Calling a novel rococo means all curls and no backbone: ornament without structure.
normal.cn: 把小说称作 rococo，意思是满篇花饰却没有骨架：只有装饰，没有结构。

abstract.en: Picture a shell pressed into a gilt frame and slowly growing into a vine.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚贝壳压进镀金画框，再缓缓长成一条藤蔓。

abstract.en: Think of a mirror-lined hall where every surface repeats the same pale curl.
abstract.cn: 想象一间满墙是镜的大厅，每个表面都重复着同一道浅色卷。

abstract.en: Imagine a page covered in flourish that hides a thin, weak line underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象一整页花体装饰下面藏着一条又细又弱的线。

examples.en: The palace chapel is a fine example of German rococo.
examples.cn: 这座宫殿的小教堂是德国洛可可风格的佳作。

examples.en: Rococo interiors replaced heavy damask with pale silk and mirrors.
examples.cn: 洛可可室内用浅色丝绸与镜面取代了厚重的锦缎。

examples.en: The essay is admired for its clear argument rather than its rococo style.
examples.cn: 这篇文章受人称道的是论证清晰，而不是繁复的风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「若可可」——像可可糖纸上卷曲的花纹：洛可可的繁复装饰；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 rocaille（碎石与贝壳装饰，源于 roc「岩石」）缩合为 rococo，一八二零年代见于法语，一八三零年代传入英语；词形可能与意大利语 barocco（巴洛克）形成类比，但并非直接借词。核心义「贝壳般的曲线与繁复装饰」。

sensesIntro.en: Rococo begins as the name of a shell-and-scroll ornamental style, then names a whole period of art, its colours and mood, its later revivals, and finally any style that is ornament without structure.
sensesIntro.cn: rococo 起初指以贝壳与卷涡为特征的装饰风格，进而指整个艺术时期、其色彩与情调、后来的复古仿作，最后指任何只有装饰没有实质的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coiling shell and vine, held inside a pale gilt frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘绕的贝壳与藤蔓，镶在浅色镀金画框里。

branches.en: THE ORNAMENT: shells, scrolls and asymmetric curves are the style at its most concrete.
branches.cn: 装饰线：贝壳、卷涡与不对称曲线是风格最具体的一端。

branches.en: THE PERIOD AND ITS ECHO: the style names a body of art, and later work that copies it.
branches.cn: 时期与回声线：风格词既指一批作品，也指后来模仿它的作品。

branches.en: THE ROOM: pale colours, gilding, intimate amusement and Chinese motifs make up the lived impression.
branches.cn: 房间线：浅色调、镀金、亲密的娱乐与中式母题构成实际感受。

branches.en: THE FREEDOM: ornament and free embellishment extend the name to loose, decorated handling in music and prose.
branches.cn: 自由线：装饰与自由加花把名称扩展到音乐与散文里松散多饰的处理。

branches.en: THE CRITICISM: once ornament outranks structure, the same name turns into a complaint.
branches.cn: 批评线：一旦装饰压过结构，同一个名称就变成抱怨。

intro.en: Rococo is a French coinage whose parts are hard to separate cleanly; the family is held together by the roc and rocaille stone-and-shell vocabulary.
intro.cn: rococo 是法语造词，内部切分并不干净；整族词靠 roc 与 rocaille 这套石作与贝壳词汇联系在一起。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is recorded for this coinage; its documented source is French, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这一造词没有可考的拉丁语形式，有据来源是法语，因此拉丁同源词条目留空。

items.example: roc is the bare base of rocaille.
items.exampleCN: roc 是 rocaille 的词基。

items.example: rocaille is the decorative workshop word.
items.exampleCN: rocaille 是装饰工艺领域的行话。

items.meaning: collective, often a heap of things
items.meaningCN: 集合义，常指一堆东西的词尾
items.example: The suffix gathers small stones into one word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把碎石统合成一个词。

items.meaning: a playful echo of Italian barocco
items.meaningCN: 对意大利语 barocco 的戏谑回响
items.example: The ending gives rococo its mocking first tone.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾让 rococo 一开始就带着调侃语气。

items.example: The suffix builds rococoesque.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 rococoesque。

items.example: It forms the rare word rococosity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成罕见词 rococosity。

items.example: baroque names the style before rococo.
items.exampleCN: baroque 指洛可可之前的风格。

items.example: chinoiserie often travelled with rococo ornament.
items.exampleCN: 中国风常随洛可可纹样一同流行。

items.example: The suffix lets shell work name a craft.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾让 shell work 成为一个工艺名称。

definition_zh: 啮齿动物；啮齿目动物（如鼠、兔、松鼠）；啃咬东西的人或物；啮齿类的
definition_en: a small mammal that has strong front teeth for gnawing wood and food, especially a rat or a mouse; also used as an adjective for such animals
core_image: 一只小动物蹲在木箱边，露在唇外的门牙不停啃咬着板条
scene: 夜里储物间的木箱边传来细细的响动，有人看见一只小家伙抱着干果，露着两颗大门牙在啃。A rodent had worked its way into the storeroom and was gnawing at the grain sacks.
sceneCN: 这里 rodent 是「啮齿动物」（第 1 个义项：用门牙啃咬东西的小型哺乳动物）；句意为一只啮齿动物钻进储物间，啃着粮袋。图中可辨识物件：木箱、干果、露在唇外的门牙、被啃咬的麻袋。

pos.zh: 名词：啮齿动物；啃咬东西的人
形容词：啮齿动物的；啃咬的

collocations.zh: 由啮齿动物传播的疾病

derivatives.zh: 本词加 -cide（杀）构成，义为「灭鼠剂；杀啮齿动物药」
本词加 -ine（属于……的）构成，义为「啮齿类的」，科学文献中使用
本词加 -like（像……的）构成，义为「像啮齿动物的」，多指牙齿与体形
拉丁语原动词，义为「啃咬、啃食」，是 rodent 的直接来源

senses.title: A gnawing mammal
senses.definition: a small mammal with continuously growing front teeth, such as a rat, mouse, squirrel or beaver, which it uses to gnaw
senses.definitionCN: 门牙不断生长、用来啃咬的小型哺乳动物，如鼠、松鼠与河狸
senses.example: Rats, mice and squirrels all belong to the rodents.
senses.exampleCN: 大鼠、小鼠与松鼠都属于啮齿动物。
senses.why: Latin rodere means to gnaw; the animals were grouped by one bodily trait, the front teeth that do the gnawing, and the name is that action itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rodere 意为啃咬；这类动物正是按同一身体特征——用来啃咬的门牙——被归为一类，而名称本身就是这个动作。

senses.title: Rodents as pests or carriers
senses.definition: members of the group treated as pests or carriers of disease in houses, farms and cities
senses.definitionCN: 在住宅、农场与城市中被当作害兽或疾病媒介的此类动物
senses.example: The warehouse closed for a week after a rodent was found near the flour.
senses.exampleCN: 面粉附近发现一只鼠后，仓库停业一周。
senses.why: Because the gnawing animals raid stored food and carry infection, the scientific word took on the practical sense of the unwanted intruder.
senses.whyCN: 由于这些啃咬的动物会抢夺储存的食物并传播感染，这个学术词便带上了「不受欢迎的闯入者」这一实际含义。

senses.title: A person who nibbles at things
senses.definition: a person who gnaws or nibbles food or objects constantly, used as a mildly playful or critical label
senses.definitionCN: 不停啃咬或小口咬食物、咬东西的人，带轻微玩笑或批评的色彩
senses.example: As a child she was a rodent, always chewing the ends of pencils.
senses.exampleCN: 小时候她是个爱啃东西的人，总在咬铅笔头。
senses.why: The action sense is applied to people, so anyone who chews and nibbles like the animals inherits the name.
senses.whyCN: 啃咬这一动作义被用到人身上，于是像那些动物一样不停啃咬的人也被冠上这个称呼。

senses.title: Of or belonging to the group
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean belonging to or characteristic of this group of animals
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示属于或具有该类动物特征的
senses.example: The skull shows clear rodent features at the front of the jaw.
senses.exampleCN: 这副头骨的下颌前部有明显的啮齿类特征。
senses.why: Once the group had a name, the same word could stand in front of a noun to mark membership of that group.
senses.whyCN: 一类动物有了名称之后，同一个词就可以置于名词之前，标出它属于这一类。

senses.title: Scientific grouping
senses.definition: a member of the order Rodentia, traditionally the largest order of mammals, now often joined with rabbits and hares in a larger group
senses.definitionCN: 啮齿目成员，传统上是哺乳动物中最大的一个目，现今常与兔形目合为更大的类群
senses.example: More than four in ten mammal species are classified as rodents.
senses.exampleCN: 四成以上的哺乳动物物种被归为啮齿类。
senses.why: Botanists and zoologists turned the descriptive word into a formal category name, so rodent became a slot in classification.
senses.whyCN: 动物学家与植物学家把这个描述性的词变成正式的分类名，于是 rodent 成了一个分类位置。

senses.title: Model animals in the lab
senses.definition: rats and mice used as standard subjects in medical and behavioural research
senses.definitionCN: 在医学与行为科学研究中用作标准实验对象的鼠与大鼠
senses.example: The team tested the drug on rodents before any human trials.
senses.exampleCN: 研究团队在人体试验之前先在一批鼠类身上测试了这种药物。
senses.why: The same animals, so common and easy to keep, became the laboratory standard, giving the word a research sense.
senses.whyCN: 这些动物数量多、易于饲养，成了实验室的标准对象，这个词因此多出一个科研语境中的含义。

intro.en: Rodent is the present participle of a Latin verb meaning to gnaw, taken into English as the name of the group.
intro.cn: rodent 是拉丁语「啃咬」动词的现在分词形式，被英语借入并用作这一类动物的名称。

items.en: *rehd- is generally reconstructed with the sense to scratch or gnaw; the deeper origin of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *rehd- 表示「抓挠、啃咬」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Rodere meant to gnaw, nibble away, or wear something down by biting, and gave rodens, the gnawing one.
items.cn: rodere 意为啃咬、一点一点啃掉、用牙磨蚀，并派生出 rodens（啃咬的）。

items.en: Modern taxonomic Latin took rodens as the order name and built Rodentia around it.
items.cn: 近代分类学拉丁语以 rodens 为目名，并据此构出 Rodentia。

items.en: English borrowed rodent as a general word for the gnawing mammals; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入 rodent，泛指这类啃咬的哺乳动物；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word spread into pest control, public health and laboratory research, and the everyday image became the rat in the storeroom.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到害虫防治、公共卫生与实验室研究，日常印象则固定在储物间的老鼠身上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin gnawing root and its formed words; the near-meaning group gathers the everyday words for the animals people actually name.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「啃咬」词根及其构成的词；近义组收人们日常真正会用到的那几个动物名称。

entries.definition: The Latin verb to gnaw, from which the group name is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词，义为「啃咬」，这一类动物的名称即由它构成。

entries.definition: A substance used to kill rats and mice; the second part comes from Latin caedere, to kill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灭鼠剂」，后半部分来自拉丁语 caedere（杀）。

entries.definition: An adjective in scientific use meaning of or like the gnawing mammals.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，科学用语，义为「啮齿类的」，指属于或有该类特征的。

entries.definition: A larger long-tailed animal of the group; the everyday name, not the scientific one.
entries.definitionCN: 大鼠，此类动物中体形较大、尾长的一种；是日常名称，不是学术名称。

entries.definition: A small animal of the group with a thin tail and pointed ears.
entries.definitionCN: 小鼠，尾细耳尖的小型同类动物。

entries.definition: Any unwanted insect or animal that damages crops or property; wider than the animal group.
entries.definitionCN: 害兽、害虫，泛指损害作物或财物的昆虫与动物，范围比这一类动物更宽。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on the Latin verb rodere and on the phrases in which the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子建立在拉丁语动词 rodere 与这个词实际出现的搭配之上。

normal.en: rodere is to gnaw, and rodent is the gnawing one: the word is the action, not a body part.
normal.cn: rodere 是啃咬，rodent 就是「啃咬的那一个」：这个词是动作，而不是某个身体部位。

normal.en: -cide means killing, so rodenticide is the chemical that kills them.
normal.cn: -cide 表示「杀」，所以 rodenticide 就是用来杀死它们的药剂。

normal.en: Rodentia is the Latin order name, which tells you rodent is a formal category word.
normal.cn: Rodentia 是拉丁语目名，这说明 rodent 是一个正式的分类用词。

normal.en: rodent control and rodent poison belong to the pest sense, not the biology lesson.
normal.cn: rodent control 与 rodent poison 属于害兽义，而不是生物学课堂里的那一义。

normal.en: Rats, mice, squirrels and beavers are all rodent words, so do not force the word to mean only the rat.
normal.cn: rats、mice、squirrels、beavers 都属啮齿类，不要把这个词只理解成大鼠。

abstract.en: Picture two white front teeth working like a small chisel on a wooden crate.
abstract.cn: 想象两颗白色门牙像小凿子一样凿着木箱。

abstract.en: Think of a cardboard box slowly worn away at one corner, night after night.
abstract.cn: 想象纸箱的一角，被一夜又一夜地慢慢磨掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a pantry where one sack of grain is being quietly emptied from below.
abstract.cn: 想象食品柜里有一袋粮，正从底部被悄悄掏空。

examples.en: Rodents can spread disease through their droppings and bites.
examples.cn: 啮齿动物会通过粪便和叮咬传播疾病。

examples.en: City inspectors found rodent damage in three of the locked shops.
examples.cn: 城市检查员在三家上锁的店铺里发现了鼠类破坏的痕迹。

examples.en: A small rodent had tucked the nuts into the corner of the shed.
examples.cn: 一只小啮齿动物把坚果塞进了棚子角落。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肉的嗑」——一口一口把肉啃着嗑掉，正是啮齿动物那副门牙干的活；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rodere（啃咬、一点点啃掉；更早的印欧词根 *rehd-「抓挠、啃咬」为重构形式）→ rodens（啃咬的）→ 近代分类学拉丁语 Rodentia（啮齿目）→ 英语 rodent，核心义「用门牙不停啃咬的那一类动物」。

sensesIntro.en: Rodent starts as a description of the gnawing action, becomes the name of a group of animals, then of them as pests, lab subjects and scientific categories, and finally of people who nibble.
sensesIntro.cn: rodent 起初是对「啃咬」这个动作的描述，后来成为一类动物的名称，再由这群动物延伸到害兽、实验对象与科学分类，最后指爱啃东西的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small front teeth working steadily on a wooden edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的门牙在木条边缘不停地啃。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the gnawing action itself became the word for the creatures that do it.
branches.cn: 动物线：啃咬这个动作本身成了做出这个动作的动物的名称。

branches.en: THE INTRUDER: the same animal entering a house or store turns the name into a warning.
branches.cn: 闯入者线：同一种动物进入住宅或仓库，这个名称就变成了警告。

branches.en: THE PERSON: anyone who nibbles constantly inherits the action sense.
branches.cn: 人物线：任何不停啃咬的人都继承了那个动作义。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: the word becomes an adjective and a rank inside formal classification.
branches.cn: 体系线：这个词既作形容词，也成为正式分类中的一个层级。

branches.en: THE LAB: cheap, common animals become the standard test subject and give the word a research sense.
branches.cn: 实验室线：便宜常见的动物成了标准受试者，这个词因此有了科研义。

intro.en: Rodent is a Latin verb form build; English adds the usual suffixes for killing, likeness and belonging.
intro.cn: rodent 是拉丁语动词形式的构形；英语再补上表示「杀」「像」「属于」的普通后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rodere, rosus and rodens are all recorded forms, and Rodentia is the Latin order name built on them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rodere、rosus 与 rodens 都是有记录的形式，Rodentia 则是据此构成的拉丁语目名。

items.example: rodere is the source verb of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: rodere 是整个词族的原动词。

items.meaning: present participle, the one doing it
items.meaningCN: 现在分词词尾，表示「正在做的那个」
items.example: The ending makes rodens from rodere.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 rodere 变成 rodens。

items.meaningCN: 啮齿目，即啃咬类哺乳动物
items.example: Rodentia is the formal name of the order.
items.exampleCN: Rodentia 是这一目的正式名称。

items.example: The suffix forms rodenticide.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 rodenticide。

items.example: It forms rodentine.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 rodentine。

items.example: It forms rodentlike.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 rodentlike。

items.example: rodens became the taxonomic base.
items.exampleCN: rodens 成了分类学上的词基。

items.example: It is the past participle of the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是同一个动词的过去分词。

items.meaning: the act of keeping something in check
items.example: The compound names the work of keeping the animals down.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指把这类动物数量压下去的工作。

definition_zh: 爱情；恋情；浪漫事迹；恋爱故事；浪漫传奇（骑士传奇）；罗曼语族语言；追求（某人）；美化叙述
definition_en: a feeling of love between two people, an affair built on that feeling, a story or mood of adventure and wonder, or a tale of love; also, in language history, the Romance languages that grew from Latin
core_image: 烛光下两个人隔着桌角相视，窗外骑士骑着马从故事书里经过
scene: 雨后的小餐馆里，桌角摆着一支蜡烛，两个人隔桌对坐，谁也没说话。What began as a quiet dinner turned into a romance that lasted for years.
sceneCN: 这里 romance 是「爱情、恋情」（第 1 个义项：两人之间的爱情与恋爱关系）；句意为一场起初平静的晚餐变成了一段延续多年的恋情。图中可辨识物件：烛台、餐桌、玻璃窗、窗外骑马的身影。

pos.zh: 名词：爱情；恋情；浪漫事迹；恋爱故事；骑士传奇；罗曼语
动词：追求、向……求爱；美化、虚夸地叙述

derivatives.zh: 本词加 -ic 构成，义为「爱情的；浪漫的；不切实际的」
本词加 -ically 构成，义为「浪漫地；在爱情方面」
本词加 -ism 构成，义为「浪漫主义；浪漫情感」
本词加 -ize 构成，义为「把……理想化、浪漫化」
本词加 -er 构成，义为「写传奇的人；爱编故事、夸大其词的人」

senses.title: A love affair
senses.definition: a romantic relationship between two people, especially one that is loving and exciting
senses.definitionCN: 两个人之间的恋爱关系，尤指充满爱意与激情的
senses.example: Their romance began on a rainy evening in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的恋情始于老城一个雨夜。
senses.why: Medieval romances were tales of love and adventure told in verse; the love story in those tales came to stand for the feeling that made the story possible.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的 romance 是用韵文讲述的爱情与冒险故事；故事里的爱情情节后来就代表促成这个情节的那种感情。

senses.title: The feeling of love
senses.definition: the feeling of love or attraction, or the tender, exciting mood connected with it
senses.definitionCN: 爱慕、恋爱的感觉，以及与之相连的温柔激动的心境
senses.example: There was no romance between them, only a comfortable friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 他们之间没有爱情，只有一段自在的友谊。
senses.why: The story sense separated from the feeling sense: romance can name the emotion on its own, without a relationship or a plot.
senses.whyCN: 故事义与情感义逐渐分开：romance 可以单指这种情感，既不需要一段关系，也不需要情节。

senses.title: A tale of love and adventure
senses.definition: a story, film or book about love, or an old narrative of knights, adventure and wonder
senses.definitionCN: 关于爱情的故事、电影或书；也指讲述骑士、冒险与奇观的古老叙事
senses.example: She reads romances on the train and crime novels at home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在火车上读言情故事，在家读犯罪小说。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense: the French narratives called romanz were tales of love and knights, and they kept the name.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最早的义项：法语称作 romanz 的叙事作品讲的是爱情与骑士，作品连同名称一起保留下来。

senses.title: Worldly feeling and excitement
senses.definition: a sense of wonder, adventure or glamour that fills a place, plan or memory
senses.definitionCN: 让某个地方、计划或记忆充满惊奇、冒险或光鲜感的氛围
senses.example: The station kept the romance of railway journeys long after steam ended.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽时代结束后很久，这座车站仍保留着铁路旅行的浪漫气息。
senses.why: Wonder was the main ingredient of the old tales, so the word kept it even when the knights were gone.
senses.whyCN: 惊奇原本就是古老故事的主要成分，因此即使骑士已经退场，这个词仍然带着这层意味。

senses.title: Romance languages
senses.definition: the languages that descend from Latin, in the phrase the Romance languages
senses.definitionCN: 由拉丁语演变而来的诸语言，见于 the Romance languages 一说
senses.example: French, Spanish and Italian are Romance languages.
senses.exampleCN: 法语、西班牙语与意大利语属于罗曼语族。
senses.why: Romanice meant in the Roman tongue, so speech descended from Latin was first called romanice loqui and eventually Romance, without any idea of love.
senses.whyCN: romanice 意为「用罗马人的方式」，因此由拉丁语演变的语言最早被称作 romanice loqui，后来简化为 Romance，与爱情毫无关系。

senses.title: A deep liking
senses.definition: a deep, sometimes idealized liking for something, as in a romance with a place or a craft
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物深切甚至理想化的喜爱，如对某地或某门技艺的迷恋
senses.example: His romance with the sea began with a toy boat.
senses.exampleCN: 他对大海的迷恋始于一只玩具船。
senses.why: The excitement the word describes was transferred from people to things people fall in love with.
senses.whyCN: 这个词所描述的激动从人转移到了人们会「爱上」的事物上。

senses.title: To woo and court
senses.definition: to court or pursue someone with intentions of love, or to behave in a loving way towards them
senses.definitionCN: 以恋爱为目的追求某人，或用充满爱意的举止对待某人
senses.example: He romanced her for months with picnics and long letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他连着几个月用野餐和长信追求她。
senses.why: The verb turns the poem-and-knight image into action: the courtship performed as a romance.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个充满诗歌与骑士意象的画面变成动作：把求爱过程演成一出浪漫故事。

senses.title: To dress up the truth
senses.definition: to make something, especially news or a plan, sound more exciting or glorious than it really is, often so as to attract someone
senses.definitionCN: 把消息或计划说得比实情更精彩、更辉煌，常为吸引他人
senses.example: Investors were romanced with promises that never came true.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者被一些从未兑现的承诺哄得心动。
senses.why: Old tales added marvels to plain facts, so romancing became a word for adding glory to something in the telling.
senses.whyCN: 古老的故事总在平实的事实上添入奇观，于是 romancing 后来就指叙述时往事物上添光。

intro.en: Romance began as a word for the Roman tongue, then named vernacular French tales, and only later the love in them.
intro.cn: romance 起初指「罗马人的语言」，后来称呼法语白话故事，最后才专指其中的爱情。

items.en: Romanicus meant of Rome or Roman, from Roma and the Roman city of the same name.
items.cn: Romanicus 意为「罗马的」，源自 Roma（罗马）。

items.en: The phrase romanice loqui, to speak in the Roman way, produced the adverb romanz, which also became the name for writing in French rather than Latin.
items.cn: 短语 romanice loqui（以罗马人的方式说话）产生出副词 romanz，它后来也成了「用法语而不用拉丁语写作」的名称。

items.en: A romanz or romance came to mean a verse narrative of chivalry and love, and this is the sense English borrowed.
items.cn: romanz 或 romance 后来指用韵文讲述骑士精神与爱情的故事，英语借入的正是这个义项。

items.en: English romance names tales of knights and later stories of love; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 romance 指骑士故事，后来也指爱情故事；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The feeling of love grew into a sense of its own, and Romance also settled as the group name of the Latin-derived languages.
items.cn: 恋爱之情逐渐独立成义；Romance 也固定为拉丁语系诸语言的族名。

items.en: The verb appeared to cover courting and the dressing up of facts, and the word spread into advertising and diplomacy.
items.cn: 动词义扩展到求爱与美化事实，这个词也进入了广告与外交的话语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Roman and Romance stems; the near-meaning group gathers other words for love and for the tales told about it.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「罗马」与 Romance 词干上的词；近义组收表示爱情以及讲述爱情的其他词。

entries.definition: The adjective for love, for feeling, or for an idealized view of things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与爱情有关的、情感化的，或对事物理想化的。

entries.definition: Of Rome or its people; the spelling has dropped out of the word but the origin remains.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马的、罗马人的；这个词已经失去了这个字形的痕迹，但来源仍是它。

entries.definition: An older adjective for the Latin-derived languages, closer to the original Romanicus.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，指拉丁语系语言的，更接近原形 Romanicus。

entries.definition: A sexual or romantic relationship; plainer than romance and less tied to excitement.
entries.definitionCN: 恋爱关系，语体更平实，不像 romance 那样强调激情。

entries.definition: Intense feeling, often love or desire; much stronger and less serene than romance.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感，常指爱情或欲望；比 romance 更强烈，也更不平静。

entries.definition: A magical story for children, or an unrealistically happy account of events.
entries.definitionCN: 讲给孩子的神奇故事，或对事件不切实际的幸福描述。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real history of the word, from Roman speech to French tales to the love in them.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的真实历史：从罗马人的语言到法语故事，再到故事里的爱情。

normal.en: Roman is hidden inside romance: the story begins with speech called Roman, not with love.
normal.cn: Roman 就藏在 romance 里：这个词的故事从「罗马式的语言」开始，而不是从爱情开始。

normal.en: A medieval romance was a verse tale of knights and love, which is why the word now means a love story.
normal.cn: 中世纪的 romance 是讲述骑士与爱情的韵文故事，这就是它现在表示爱情故事的原因。

normal.en: The Romance languages are the Latin-descended ones, French, Spanish, Italian and their kin.
normal.cn: Romance languages 指由拉丁语演变来的语言，如法语、西班牙语、意大利语等。

normal.en: romance as a verb has two sides: courting someone, and dressing up a plan to sell it.
normal.cn: romance 作动词有两面：追求某人，以及把计划包装得更好听好卖。

normal.en: Romantic and romanticize build on the same stem, so the idealized meaning lives in the whole family.
normal.cn: romantic 与 romanticize 建立在同一词干上，理想化的含义贯穿整个词族。

abstract.en: Picture a candle between two cups of coffee as the room falls quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象两支咖啡杯之间立着一支蜡烛，屋子忽然静下来。

abstract.en: Imagine a knight riding past the window while two people keep looking at each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一名骑士从窗外策马经过，而屋里两个人只顾相望。

abstract.en: Think of an old book where every page turns a plain evening into a legend.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧书，每一页都把平淡的黄昏变成传说。

examples.en: Their romance lasted longer than anyone had predicted.
examples.cn: 这段恋情比任何人预料的都长久。

examples.en: Spanish, French and Portuguese are Romance languages.
examples.cn: 西班牙语、法语与葡萄牙语都属于罗曼语族。

examples.en: The agent romanced new clients with promises of fast returns.
examples.cn: 这名经纪人以高回报的承诺哄得新客户动心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「罗曼史」——早就是汉语里指爱情故事的常用译名，正好对应 romance 的「恋情、恋爱故事」义；这只是谐音与借词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 Romanicus（罗马的）→ 副词 romanice（以罗马人的方式）→ 古法语 romanz（用法语写成的白话作品，后指骑士与爱情故事）→ 英语 romance，核心义「以罗马人的语言讲出来的传奇」。爱情义是在故事义之上后来长出来的。

sensesIntro.en: Romance begins as the name of a vernacular tongue, then of verse tales of chivalry, then of the love inside them, and from there spreads to feelings, mood, deep liking and the actions of courting and embellishing.
sensesIntro.cn: romance 起初是一种白话语言的名称，后来指韵文的骑士故事，再后来指故事里的爱情，由此扩展到情感、氛围、深切喜好，以及追求与美化叙述等动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people by candlelight while a knight rides past the window of their story.
core.cn: 核心意象：烛光下的两个人，而有骑士从他们故事的窗外经过。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the love inside the old tales detached from the tales and became an emotion on its own.
branches.cn: 情感线：古老故事里的爱情脱离了故事，成为独立的感情。

branches.en: THE STORY: the verse narrative itself is the oldest English sense and still names love fiction.
branches.cn: 故事线：韵文叙事是英语最早的义项，至今仍指言情作品。

branches.en: THE WONDER: adventure and glamour spread from tales to places, plans and objects.
branches.cn: 惊奇线：冒险与光鲜从故事扩散到地方、计划与物品。

branches.en: THE TONGUE: the language sense is the oldest stratum and yet the least romantic of all.
branches.cn: 语言线：语言义是最早的层次，却恰恰最不「浪漫」。

branches.en: THE ACTION: courting and embellishing turn the mood into things people do.
branches.cn: 动作线：求爱与美化把氛围变成人可以做出的行动。

intro.en: Romance is a Latin-derived noun; English builds the family with -tic, -ism, -ize and -er.
intro.cn: romance 是源自拉丁语的名词；英语用 -tic、-ism、-ize 与 -er 扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin Romanus and Romanicus are recorded, and the adverb romanice is the direct ancestor of the name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Romanus 与 Romanicus 均有文献记录，副词 romanice 是这一名称的直接源头。

items.exampleCN: 城名处于整个词族的最底层。

items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是罗曼语族名称的基础。

items.meaning: in the Roman way, in Latin-derived speech
items.meaningCN: 以罗马人的方式，用拉丁系的白话
items.example: The adverb became the Old French romanz.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词演变出古法语 romanz。

items.meaning: the noun formed from the Latin adverb
items.meaningCN: 由拉丁语副词形成的法语名词词尾
items.example: The ending turns an adverb into a type of writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把副词变成一种文体的名称。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 romantic。

items.example: It forms romanticism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 romanticism。

items.example: It forms romanticize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 romanticize。

items.example: It forms romancer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 romancer。

items.example: English Roman comes straight from this word.
items.exampleCN: 英语 Roman 直接来自这个词。
